1:/**
2: * Dashboard sidebar sections and the lowest role that can open each. The
3: * admin middleware and the sidebar both read this list, so a section's
4: * access is defined in one place (the database policies enforce the same
5: * rules on the data itself).
6: */
7:export interface AdminSection {
8:  label: string
9:  icon: string
10:  to: string
11:  role: StaffRole
12:  /** Shown at the bottom of the sidebar, under View website. */
13:  bottom?: boolean
14:}
15:
16:export const adminSections: AdminSection[] = [
17:  { label: 'Inventory', icon: 'i-lucide-package', to: '/admin/inventory', role: 'staff' },
18:  { label: 'Calendar', icon: 'i-lucide-calendar-days', to: '/admin/calendar', role: 'staff' },
19:  { label: 'Orders', icon: 'i-lucide-receipt-text', to: '/admin/orders', role: 'staff' },
20:  { label: 'Management', icon: 'i-lucide-users', to: '/admin/management', role: 'manager' },
21:  { label: 'Marketing', icon: 'i-lucide-megaphone', to: '/admin/marketing', role: 'manager' },
22:  { label: 'Site', icon: 'i-lucide-panels-top-left', to: '/admin/site', role: 'manager' },
23:  { label: 'Settings', icon: 'i-lucide-settings', to: '/admin/settings', role: 'manager', bottom: true },
24:]
25:
26:export function adminSectionFor(path: string) {
27:  return adminSections.find(section => path === section.to || path.startsWith(`${section.to}/`))
28:}

[Source raw SHA256:95a26b2c374083c06d2078c92889cda29a2d3b3db163247506ecb915cc466605]
1:-- Admin dashboard: staff roles, inventory, hero photos, calendar, orders,
2:-- settings, marketing, and the media bucket.
3:--
4:-- Access model
5:-- - staff_members gives a user a dashboard role: staff < manager < owner < admin
6:--   (enum order, so `role >= 'manager'` means manager, owner or admin).
7:--   Admin has every permission, including managing owners and other admins.
8:-- - Every table has row-level security. The browser talks to Supabase
9:--   directly; these policies are the real permission boundary, the sidebar
10:--   only hides what a role cannot use.
11:-- - staff_members and app_secrets have no write policies: they change only
12:--   through the Nuxt server routes (service role), which enforce who may
13:--   manage whom and keep API keys out of the browser.
14:
15:/* ---- Roles --------------------------------------------------------------- */
16:create type public.staff_role as enum ('staff', 'manager', 'owner', 'admin');
17:
18:create table public.staff_members (
19:  user_id uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
20:  email text not null,
21:  role public.staff_role not null default 'staff',
22:  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
23:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
24:);
25:
26:-- True when the signed-in user holds `required` or a higher role.
27:-- security definer so policies on staff_members itself can call it.
28:create function public.has_staff_role(required public.staff_role)
29:returns boolean
30:language sql
31:stable
32:security definer
33:set search_path = ''
34:as $$
35:  select coalesce(
36:    (select m.role >= required from public.staff_members m where m.user_id = (select auth.uid())),
37:    false
38:  )
39:$$;
40:
41:-- Looks up an auth user by email (used when inviting someone who already has
42:-- a customer account). Server-only.
43:create function public.find_user_id_by_email(lookup text)
44:returns uuid
45:language sql
46:stable
47:security definer
48:set search_path = ''
49:as $$
50:  select id from auth.users where lower(email) = lower(lookup) limit 1
51:$$;
52:revoke execute on function public.find_user_id_by_email(text) from public, anon, authenticated;
53:grant execute on function public.find_user_id_by_email(text) to service_role;
54:
55:-- There must always be an admin, whatever path the change comes from.
56:create function public.keep_an_admin()
57:returns trigger
58:language plpgsql
59:set search_path = ''
60:as $$
61:begin
62:  if old.role = 'admin' and not exists (select 1 from public.staff_members where role = 'admin') then
63:    raise exception 'At least one admin is required';
64:  end if;
65:  return null;
66:end
67:$$;
68:
69:create constraint trigger staff_members_keep_an_admin
70:  after update or delete on public.staff_members
71:  for each row execute function public.keep_an_admin();
72:
73:/* ---- Shared helpers ------------------------------------------------------ */
74:create function public.touch_updated_at()
75:returns trigger
76:language plpgsql
77:set search_path = ''
78:as $$
79:begin
80:  new.updated_at = now();
81:  return new;
82:end
83:$$;
84:
85:create trigger staff_members_touch before update on public.staff_members
86:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
87:
88:alter table public.staff_members enable row level security;
89:
90:create policy "Members see their own role" on public.staff_members
91:  for select to authenticated
92:  using (user_id = (select auth.uid()) or public.has_staff_role('manager'));
93:
94:/* ---- Inventory ----------------------------------------------------------- */
95:-- One row per item sold. Hand-entered items use source 'manual'; distributor
96:-- syncs (lipseys, sports_south) upsert on (source, external_id).
97:create table public.products (
98:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
99:  slug text not null unique check (slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'),
100:  name text not null check (length(trim(name)) > 0),
101:  category text not null default '',
102:  description text not null default '',
103:  price numeric(10, 2) check (price >= 0), -- null shows "Call for price"
104:  sku text,
105:  upc text,
106:  quantity integer not null default 0 check (quantity >= 0),
107:  status text not null default 'draft' check (status in ('draft', 'active', 'archived')),
108:  featured boolean not null default false, -- shown on the home page rail
109:  sort_order integer not null default 0,
110:  source text not null default 'manual',
111:  external_id text,
112:  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
113:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
114:  unique (source, external_id)
115:);
116:
117:create trigger products_touch before update on public.products
118:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
119:
120:-- Photos in the site-media bucket under products/<product id>/. The lowest
121:-- sort_order is the cover.
122:create table public.product_images (
123:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
124:  product_id uuid not null references public.products (id) on delete cascade,
125:  path text not null,
126:  alt text not null default '',
127:  sort_order integer not null default 0,
128:  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
129:);
130:create index product_images_product_idx on public.product_images (product_id, sort_order);
131:
132:alter table public.products enable row level security;
133:alter table public.product_images enable row level security;
134:
135:create policy "Anyone sees active products" on public.products
136:  for select to anon, authenticated
137:  using (status = 'active' or public.has_staff_role('staff'));
138:create policy "Staff manage products" on public.products
139:  for all to authenticated
140:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'))
141:  with check (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
142:
143:create policy "Anyone sees photos of active products" on public.product_images
144:  for select to anon, authenticated
145:  using (
146:    public.has_staff_role('staff')
147:    or exists (select 1 from public.products p where p.id = product_id and p.status = 'active')
148:  );
149:create policy "Staff manage product photos" on public.product_images
150:  for all to authenticated
151:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'))
152:  with check (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
153:
154:/* ---- Site ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
155:-- Home page hero stack, shown in sort_order. Photos live under hero/.
156:create table public.hero_photos (
157:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
158:  label text not null,
159:  alt text not null default '',
160:  path text,
161:  sort_order integer not null default 0,
162:  active boolean not null default true,
163:  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
164:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
165:);
166:
167:create trigger hero_photos_touch before update on public.hero_photos
168:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
169:
170:-- Public website settings by key (e.g. 'announcement'). Readable by everyone,
171:-- so never store anything private here; private settings go in app_settings.
172:create table public.site_content (
173:  key text primary key,
174:  value jsonb not null default '{}',
175:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
176:  updated_by uuid references auth.users (id) on delete set null
177:);
178:
179:create trigger site_content_touch before update on public.site_content
180:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
181:
182:alter table public.hero_photos enable row level security;
183:alter table public.site_content enable row level security;
184:
185:create policy "Anyone sees active hero photos" on public.hero_photos
186:  for select to anon, authenticated
187:  using (active or public.has_staff_role('manager'));
188:create policy "Managers manage hero photos" on public.hero_photos
189:  for all to authenticated
190:  using (public.has_staff_role('manager'))
191:  with check (public.has_staff_role('manager'));
192:
193:create policy "Anyone reads site content" on public.site_content
194:  for select to anon, authenticated
195:  using (true);
196:create policy "Managers edit site content" on public.site_content
197:  for all to authenticated
198:  using (public.has_staff_role('manager'))
199:  with check (public.has_staff_role('manager'));
200:
201:/* ---- Calendar ------------------------------------------------------------ */
202:-- `source` says where an event came from: 'manual', 'ai', or an importer's
203:-- id. Importers upsert on (source, external_id) and skip rows that already
204:-- exist, so re-running an import never duplicates or overwrites staff edits.
205:-- Automatic sources create 'suggested' events that staff approve.
206:create table public.events (
207:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
208:  title text not null check (length(trim(title)) > 0),
209:  description text not null default '',
210:  location text not null default '',
211:  starts_at timestamptz not null,
212:  ends_at timestamptz,
213:  all_day boolean not null default false,
214:  status text not null default 'scheduled' check (status in ('suggested', 'scheduled', 'cancelled')),
215:  source text not null default 'manual',
216:  external_id text,
217:  source_url text,
218:  created_by uuid references auth.users (id) on delete set null,
219:  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
220:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
221:  unique (source, external_id),
222:  check (ends_at is null or ends_at >= starts_at)
223:);
224:create index events_starts_idx on public.events (starts_at);
225:
226:create trigger events_touch before update on public.events
227:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
228:
229:create table public.event_notes (
230:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
231:  event_id uuid not null references public.events (id) on delete cascade,
232:  body text not null check (length(trim(body)) > 0),
233:  author_id uuid default auth.uid() references auth.users (id) on delete set null,
234:  author_email text,
235:  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
236:);
237:create index event_notes_event_idx on public.event_notes (event_id, created_at);
238:
239:-- Notes keep the author's email so the history reads well even after the
240:-- author leaves (author_id is then cleared).
241:create function public.fill_note_author_email()
242:returns trigger
243:language plpgsql
244:security definer
245:set search_path = ''
246:as $$
247:begin
248:  new.author_email = (select email from public.staff_members where user_id = new.author_id);
249:  return new;
250:end
251:$$;
252:
253:create trigger event_notes_author_email before insert on public.event_notes
254:  for each row execute function public.fill_note_author_email();
255:
256:alter table public.events enable row level security;
257:alter table public.event_notes enable row level security;
258:
259:create policy "Staff manage events" on public.events
260:  for all to authenticated
261:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'))
262:  with check (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
263:
264:create policy "Staff read notes" on public.event_notes
265:  for select to authenticated
266:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
267:create policy "Staff add their own notes" on public.event_notes
268:  for insert to authenticated
269:  with check (public.has_staff_role('staff') and author_id = (select auth.uid()));
270:create policy "Authors and managers delete notes" on public.event_notes
271:  for delete to authenticated
272:  using (author_id = (select auth.uid()) or public.has_staff_role('manager'));
273:
274:/* ---- Orders -------------------------------------------------------------- */
275:-- kind 'customer': placed by a customer (checkout, phone, in store).
276:-- kind 'dealer': placed by the shop with a distributor (Lipsey's, Sports South…).
277:create table public.orders (
278:  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
279:  kind text not null check (kind in ('customer', 'dealer')),
280:  reference text not null default '',
281:  status text not null default 'pending'
282:    check (status in ('pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'ready', 'completed', 'cancelled')),

284:  customer_name text not null default '',

292:  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),

294:);
295:create index orders_kind_placed_idx on public.orders (kind, placed_at desc);
296:
297:create trigger orders_touch before update on public.orders
298:  for each row execute function public.touch_updated_at();
299:

306:  unit_price numeric(10, 2) check (unit_price >= 0)
307:);

309:
310:alter table public.orders enable row level security;

1:/*
2: * Ask the configured AI for local events worth putting on the shop calendar.
3: * Results are saved as 'suggested' events (source 'ai') for staff to check
4: * and approve. A model without web access answers from what it already
5: * knows, so suggestions can be out of date or wrong; the calendar labels them.
6: */
7:import * as z from 'zod'
8:
9:const body = z.object({
10:  from: z.iso.date(),
11:  to: z.iso.date(),
12:  focus: z.string().trim().max(500).default(''),
13:  provider: z.enum(aiProviders).optional(),
14:})
15:
16:const suggestion = z.object({
17:  title: z.string().trim().min(1),
18:  start: z.string().min(10),
19:  end: z.string().nullish(),
20:  all_day: z.boolean().default(false),
21:  location: z.string().default(''),
22:  description: z.string().default(''),
23:  url: z.string().nullish(),
24:})
25:
26:const system = `You help a gunsmithing and firearms shop in Livermore, California (Accurate Arms USA) find events for its calendar: gun shows, shooting competitions and matches, firearms safety and training classes, hunting season dates, and community events in the San Francisco Bay Area and Central Valley.
27:Only list events you have good reason to believe are real. Never invent events. If unsure, leave it out.
28:Reply with JSON only: {"events": [{"title": "", "start": "ISO 8601 date or date-time", "end": "ISO 8601 or null", "all_day": true, "location": "", "description": "", "url": "source page or null"}]}.`
29:
30:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
31:  const { admin } = await requireStaff(event, 'staff')
32:  const { from, to, focus, provider } = await readValidatedBody(event, body.parse)
33:  if (to < from) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'The end date is before the start date' })
34:
35:  const reply = await generateText(event, admin, {
36:    system,
37:    provider,
38:    json: true,
39:    prompt: `Find events between ${from} and ${to}.${focus ? ` Focus on: ${focus}` : ''}`,
40:  })
41:  const raw = (parseJsonReply(reply) as { events?: unknown }).events
42:  const items = (Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : [])
43:    .map(item => suggestion.safeParse(item))
44:    .flatMap(result => result.success ? [result.data] : [])
45:    .filter(item => !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(item.start)))
46:
47:  const { added } = await importEvents(admin, 'ai', await Promise.all(items.map(async item => ({
48:    // Same title on the same day = same event, so asking again doesn't duplicate it.
49:    externalId: await stableId(`${item.title.toLowerCase()}|${item.start.slice(0, 10)}`),
50:    title: item.title,
51:    startsAt: new Date(item.start).toISOString(),
52:    endsAt: item.end && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(item.end)) && Date.parse(item.end) >= Date.parse(item.start)
53:      ? new Date(item.end).toISOString()
54:      : null,
55:    allDay: item.all_day,
56:    location: item.location,
57:    description: item.description,
58:    url: item.url && /^https?:\/\//.test(item.url) ? item.url : null,
59:  }))))
60:
61:  return { found: items.length, added }
62:})
```

## assistant

The dashboard is already set up for this. Inventory, Calendar and Orders all read Supabase tables, and the `products` and `events` tables were built to be filled automatically: each row records where it came from (`source`) and that system's ID for it (`external_id`). So nothing about the dashboard pages has to change. You add a few server jobs that pull from each outside system and write into those tables, and the dashboard fills itself.

## The overall shape

```
Lipsey's / Sports South API ──(scheduled sync)──► products
Bravo (shop PC, store stock + in-store sales) ──(local export/agent)──► products.qty, orders
Website checkout ──► orders (pending) ──Elite payment webhook──► orders (paid)
orders / dealer orders / waiting period ──(derived)──► events (calendar)
```

Supabase is the hub. Each outside system gets one small adapter that only writes into it, and the dashboard and the shop only ever read Supabase.

## 1. Inventory: from the distributor catalog
- A scheduled server job calls the Lipsey's or Sports South catalog API. It saves or updates each item using `source='lipseys'` plus the distributor's item number, so re-running it never creates duplicates. This is the same pattern `importEvents` uses for the calendar.
- **Decide which fields each side owns.** The sync owns cost, distributor stock, UPC, the maker's specs and the stock photo. Staff own the selling price (or a markup rule), status, featured, the description and your own photos. Without this split, every sync would wipe out staff edits.
- New catalog items come in as `draft`, so you choose what shows on the site and don't publish 30,000 SKUs by accident. You could also auto-publish by category.
- **Gap:** `products` has one `quantity` field. You need two: what's on your shelf (from Bravo) and what the distributor has (from their feed). The shop page could then say "In stock" or "Ships to store in 3–5 days".

## 2. Orders: from checkout, Elite and Bravo
- At checkout, create a `pending` customer order with its line items linked to products. Then send the customer to Elite's payment page. Elite calls back (a webhook) when the payment clears, and a server route marks the order paid. Never trust the browser's word that a payment went through.
- Firearms and CA ammo stay pickup-only. Their orders go to `ready`, and the paperwork happens in Bravo, as you planned.
- If a customer buys something that's only in distributor stock, the job automatically creates a matching `dealer` order. Later that could be sent to the distributor automatically, if their API takes orders; I haven't checked whether it does.
- **Bravo:** as far as I know it only runs on shop computers and has no cloud API (not confirmed). The realistic route is a scheduled export on the shop PC, or a small sync program there, that pushes stock levels and in-store sales up to Supabase. Those orders would be marked `source='bravo'`.
- **Gap:** `orders` has no `source`/`external_id`, payment status, Elite transaction ID or `fulfillment` (pickup or ship) fields. These need adding before the webhook and the Bravo import can match records safely.

## 3. Calendar: built from orders
The calendar doesn't need its own data feed. Create events from order changes, linked back to the order (`source='order'`, `external_id=<order id>`):
- An expected-arrival date when a dealer order is placed.
- A pickup window when an order hits `ready`.
- The California 10-day waiting-period release date for a firearm sale, once you enter the start date (or once it comes from Bravo).
- Shop jobs (Cerakote, laser work) with due dates, later on.

The current importer already skips events that exist, so staff edits are never overwritten.

## Where the scheduled jobs run
That depends on where the site is hosted. Nuxt can run scheduled tasks on a normal Node server. On serverless hosting, a Supabase scheduled job (pg_cron) can call a server route. Distributor and Elite keys would go in the existing encrypted `app_secrets` store, alongside the AI keys.

## Suggested order to build it
1. Database changes: split the quantity fields, add the order source/payment/fulfillment fields, and link calendar events to orders.
2. Sync with one distributor, plus a "Sync now" button and a last-sync status on the Inventory page.
3. The public shop page and checkout, with the Elite webhook, which creates the orders.
4. Calendar events created from orders.
5. The Bravo export bridge.

## Questions before building
- **Which distributor first,** Lipsey's or Sports South? And do you have their API login yet? Some distributors give API access only on request.
- **Bravo:** which version, and can it export inventory or sales to CSV on a schedule?
- **Elite:** which gateway sits behind it? That decides how the payment page and webhook work, and I'd confirm it from their documentation.
- **Hosting:** where does the site run?

If you answer those, I can start with step 1: the database changes plus the sync for your first distributor.

    private function login()
    {
        $model = array(
            "Email" => $this->Email,
            "Password" => $this->Password
        );
        $curl = $this->PostRequestBuilder("integration/authentication/login", $model);

                }
                return 1;
            }
        }
        return $response;
    }

## assistant

I looked through the Lipsey's file you downloaded and at how both distributors offer their data. Short version: the site can import this file today, and a hands-off daily sync needs Lipsey's (or Sports South) to switch on data access for your account. No code was changed.

One note: I can't see the tabs open in your browser. I worked from the file in your Downloads folder and from public pages.

## What's in the file
`Lipsey's-Catalog-10-23-2026,_5-04-03_PM.csv` has 9,589 items and 113 columns.

- **Every row is in stock.** Quantities run from 1 to 2,000 with no zeros, so this is only what Lipsey's has on hand, not their full catalog. An item missing from tomorrow's file means it sold out.
- **Item ID:** `ITEMNO` is unique for every row, so it's the key for matching the same item on the next import. `UPC` is also unique and can link items to Bravo later.
- **Prices:** `PRICE` and `CURRENTPRICE` are your cost (they differ on the 1,326 items marked on sale). The file also has `MSRP` and `RETAILMAP`. 4,425 items have a minimum advertised price (MAP), so the site must never show a lower price on those.
- **Item types:** 6,306 firearms, 2,624 accessories, 604 optics and 55 ammo. `FFLREQUIRED`, `CANDROPSHIP` and `AMMOBLOCKSHIP` tell us what can be shipped and what must be pickup-only.
- **Photos:** `IMAGENAME` matches Lipsey's public image server. I checked `https://www.lipseyscloud.com/images/3701113b.jpg` and it loads, so we don't need to copy photos into our own storage.
- **Details:** manufacturer, model, caliber, capacity, barrel length, finish and the other spec columns are enough for shop filters and product pages.

## The California problem
The file has no California handgun roster information. Most of these handguns can't be sold to ordinary CA customers. If we publish the catalog without filtering, the site would list guns you can't legally sell. I'd strongly suggest that imported firearms come in as drafts, and handguns only go live if they're on the CA DOJ roster. We could also start with accessories, optics and parts only. (25 items are marked CA lead-free approved, which matters for hunting ammo.)

## How to make it run on its own
**1. Upload the file in the dashboard (works now, but by hand).** Add an "Import Lipsey's file" button to the Inventory page. Each time, it adds new items, updates price and stock on existing ones, and marks items that dropped off the list as out of stock. Someone would upload a fresh file every day or two.

**2. Lipsey's API (fully hands-off; this is the goal).** I read Lipsey's official example code. It logs in with an email and password, not a separate key, and gets a temporary token. From there it offers:
- the full catalog;
- a separate price-and-stock feed, which is light enough to check every hour;
- placing orders and shipping straight to a customer, for firearms and accessories.

What I don't know is whether your normal dealer login works for this, or whether Lipsey's has to enable it on your account first. I couldn't test it without your login. One call or email to your Lipsey's rep asking to "enable API integration access" probably settles it. Their API page also has a commercial-use restriction notice I couldn't read in full, so ask them about that too.

**3. Sports South web services (same idea).** Their public service page lists the login fields: customer number, username, password and a source name. It can also send only the items that changed since the last check. That makes a daily sync cheap, so Sports South could be the quicker distributor to automate. Their web services support line is (800) 772-4287.

**Not recommended:** having a script log into the dealer website and download the file automatically. It breaks whenever they change the site and may break their terms.

## The plan
Build the importer so the data source can be swapped out underneath it:

```
CSV upload (now) ──┐
Lipsey's API ──────┼─► one import step ─► products table ─► shop + dashboard Inventory
Sports South API ──┘    (match on source + item number)
```

- **What the import updates:** cost, MAP, MSRP, distributor stock, specs, photo link and a "last seen" date.
- **What staff keep control of:** status (draft/active), featured, your selling price or markup, your own photos and description. Re-importing never overwrites these.
- **Selling price:** a markup rule, then raised to MAP if it comes out lower. Staff can override it per item.
- **New items** come in as drafts. You decide which categories go live automatically.
- **Database changes needed:** separate distributor stock from what's in the store, add cost/MAP/MSRP, a specs field and the shipping flags. 9,600 rows is a small, quick import for Supabase.
- **Running on schedule:** once there's API access, the same import step runs automatically (hourly for price and stock, nightly for the full catalog). A "last sync" line on the Inventory page shows whether it worked.

## What I need from you
1. Shall I build the CSV import now (the database changes, the import step and the Inventory upload button)? When API access arrives, it's a small addition on top.
2. Can you ask Lipsey's and Sports South to enable API / web services on your account?
3. For the California roster issue, which do you prefer: firearms always start as drafts for staff to review, or launch with only accessories, optics and parts at first?

1:/**
2: * Small helpers shared by the dashboard pages: toasts for saves and errors,
3: * and the site-media storage bucket (public photo URLs and uploads).
4: */
5:export function useAdmin() {
6:  const toast = useToast()
7:  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
8:  const bucket = () => supabase.storage.from('site-media')
9:
10:  /** Message from a Supabase error, a server route error, or anything thrown. */
11:  function errorMessage(err: unknown): string {
12:    if (typeof err === 'string') return err
13:    const e = err as { data?: { statusMessage?: string, message?: string }, statusMessage?: string, message?: string }
14:    return e?.data?.statusMessage || e?.data?.message || e?.statusMessage || e?.message || 'Something went wrong'
15:  }
16:
17:  function notifyError(err: unknown, title = 'Couldn\'t save') {
18:    toast.add({ title, description: errorMessage(err), color: 'error', icon: 'i-lucide-circle-alert' })
19:  }
20:
21:  function notify(title: string, description?: string) {
22:    toast.add({ title, description, color: 'success', icon: 'i-lucide-check' })
23:  }
24:
25:  /** Throws Supabase's error so callers can use one try/catch; narrows the result to success. */
26:  function check<T extends { error: unknown }>(result: T): Extract<T, { error: null }> {
27:    if (result.error) throw result.error
28:    return result as Extract<T, { error: null }>
29:  }
30:
31:  function mediaUrl(path: string | null | undefined) {
32:    return path ? bucket().getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl : ''
33:  }
34:
35:  /** Uploads a photo under `folder` (products/<id> or hero) and returns its storage path. */
36:  async function uploadPhoto(folder: string, file: File) {
37:    const ext = file.name.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '') || 'jpg'
38:    const path = `${folder}/${crypto.randomUUID()}.${ext}`
39:    check(await bucket().upload(path, file, { contentType: file.type, cacheControl: '31536000' }))
40:    return path
41:  }
42:
43:  async function removePhotos(paths: string[]) {
44:    if (paths.length) check(await bucket().remove(paths))
45:  }
46:
47:  return { supabase, notify, notifyError, errorMessage, check, mediaUrl, uploadPhoto, removePhotos }
48:}
49:
50:/** Formats a price, or "Call for price" when there is none. */
51:export function formatPrice(value: number | null | undefined, digits = 2) {
52:  if (value === null || value === undefined) return 'Call for price'
53:  return new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: digits }).format(value)
54:}
55:
56:/** "Oct 24, 2026, 3:00 PM" in the browser's time zone. */
57:export function formatDateTime(value: string | null | undefined, withTime = true) {
58:  if (!value) return ''
59:  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', withTime
60:    ? { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }
61:    : { dateStyle: 'medium' }).format(new Date(value))
62:}
63:
64:/** ISO timestamp → value for <input type="datetime-local"> (local time). */
65:export function toLocalInput(value: string | null | undefined) {
66:  if (!value) return ''
67:  const d = new Date(value)
68:  const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, '0')
69:  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}T${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}`
70:}
71:
72:/** <input type="datetime-local"> value → ISO timestamp, or null when empty. */
73:export function fromLocalInput(value: string | null | undefined) {
74:  return value ? new Date(value).toISOString() : null
75:}
76:
77:/** "Stippled P365 frame!" → "stippled-p365-frame" */
78:export function slugify(text: string) {
79:  return text.toLowerCase().normalize('NFKD').replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
80:}

[server/utils/events.ts#B67A]
[Source raw SHA256:b67a6f68bab7e4e288373ff320d10c60582e992a6c6b94ffa34d951e4514d2a0]
1:/**
2: * Shared entry point for anything that adds events automatically: AI
3: * discovery today; calendar feeds, distributor or auction-site scrapers, or a
4: * future Python worker later. Each source names itself (`source`) and gives
5: * every event a stable `externalId`; rows that already exist for that pair
6: * are skipped, so re-running an import never duplicates events or overwrites
7: * what staff edited. Imported events arrive as 'suggested' for staff to
8: * approve, unless the source is trusted enough to schedule directly.
9: */
10:
11:/** Stable hex id for text, e.g. to derive an externalId from an event's title and day. */
12:export async function stableId(text: string) {
13:  const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-1', new TextEncoder().encode(text))
14:  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(digest), b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')
15:}
16:
17:export interface ImportedEvent {
18:  externalId: string
19:  title: string
20:  startsAt: string
21:  endsAt?: string | null
22:  allDay?: boolean
23:  location?: string
24:  description?: string
25:  url?: string | null
26:}
27:
28:export async function importEvents(
29:  admin: AdminClient,
30:  source: string,
31:  events: ImportedEvent[],
32:  status: EventStatus = 'suggested',
33:) {
34:  if (!events.length) return { added: 0 }
35:  const rows = events.map(e => ({
36:    source,
37:    external_id: e.externalId,
38:    title: e.title,
39:    starts_at: e.startsAt,
40:    ends_at: e.endsAt ?? null,
41:    all_day: e.allDay ?? false,
42:    location: e.location ?? '',
43:    description: e.description ?? '',
44:    source_url: e.url ?? null,
45:    status,
46:  }))
47:  const { data, error } = await admin
48:    .from('events')
49:    .upsert(rows, { onConflict: 'source,external_id', ignoreDuplicates: true })
50:    .select('id')
51:  failOn(error)
52:  return { added: data?.length ?? 0 }
53:}


[server/utils/staff.ts#7AA7]
[Source raw SHA256:7aa7e0c8275bf1fa3976b09fb93e8ccc9b2c6dcd8ff3da15a29fea55e1d9d493]
1:/**
2: * Server-side role checks for the dashboard API routes. Every route under
3: * server/api/admin starts with `requireStaff`, which also hands back a
4: * service-role client: it bypasses row-level security, so the route itself
5: * is responsible for checking what the caller may do.
6: */
7:import type { H3Event } from 'h3'
8:import { serverSupabaseServiceRole, serverSupabaseUser } from '#supabase/server'
9:import type { Database } from '../../shared/types/database.types'
10:
11:/** Service-role Supabase client, typed from shared/types/database.types.ts. */
12:export type AdminClient = ReturnType<typeof serverSupabaseServiceRole<Database>>
13:
14:export async function requireStaff(event: H3Event, required: StaffRole) {
15:  const claims = await serverSupabaseUser(event).catch(() => null)
16:  const userId = claims?.sub
17:  if (!userId) throw createError({ statusCode: 401, statusMessage: 'Sign in required' })
18:
19:  const admin = serverSupabaseServiceRole(event)
20:  const { data, error } = await admin
21:    .from('staff_members')
22:    .select('email, role')
23:    .eq('user_id', userId)
24:    .maybeSingle()
25:  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: error.message })
26:  if (!data || !hasRole(data.role, required)) {
27:    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Your role does not allow this' })
28:  }
29:  return { userId, email: data.email, role: data.role, admin }
30:}
31:
32:/** Turns a Supabase error into an HTTP error with its message. */
33:export function failOn(error: { message: string } | null, statusCode = 500) {
34:  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode, statusMessage: error.message })
35:}

1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Create or edit one inventory item, including its photos. Photos are
4: * stored under products/<id>/ in the site-media bucket, so they can be added
5: * once the item has been saved. The first photo is the cover shown on the
6: * home page and in the shop.
7: */
8:import * as z from 'zod'
9:
10:const props = defineProps<{ product: ProductRow | null }>()
11:const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
12:const emit = defineEmits<{ saved: [product: ProductRow], deleted: [id: string] }>()
13:
14:const { supabase, check, notify, notifyError, mediaUrl, uploadPhoto, removePhotos } = useAdmin()
15:
16:const statusItems = [
17:  { label: 'Draft (hidden)', value: 'draft' },
18:  { label: 'Active (on the website)', value: 'active' },
19:  { label: 'Archived', value: 'archived' },
20:]
21:
22:const schema = z.object({
23:  name: z.string().trim().min(1, 'Name the item'),
24:  slug: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, 'Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes'),
25:  price: z.string().refine(v => v.trim() === '' || (Number.isFinite(Number(v)) && Number(v) >= 0), 'Enter a price, or leave empty for "Call for price"'),
26:  quantity: z.number().int().min(0),
27:})
28:
29:function blank() {
30:  return {
31:    name: '',
32:    slug: '',
33:    category: '',
34:    description: '',
35:    price: '',
36:    sku: '',
37:    upc: '',
38:    quantity: 0,
39:    status: 'draft' as ProductStatus,
40:    featured: false,
41:    sort_order: 0,
42:  }
43:}
44:const state = reactive(blank())
45:const images = ref<ProductImage[]>([])
46:const slugTouched = ref(false)
47:const saving = ref(false)
48:const uploading = ref(false)
49:const id = ref<string | null>(null)
50:
51:watch(open, (isOpen) => {
52:  if (!isOpen) return
53:  const p = props.product
54:  Object.assign(state, blank(), p
55:    ? { ...p, price: p.price === null ? '' : String(p.price), sku: p.sku ?? '', upc: p.upc ?? '' }
56:    : {})
57:  id.value = p?.id ?? null
58:  images.value = [...(p?.product_images ?? [])].sort((a, b) => a.sort_order - b.sort_order)
59:  slugTouched.value = !!p
60:}, { immediate: true })
61:
62:watch(() => state.name, (name) => {
63:  if (!slugTouched.value) state.slug = slugify(name)
64:})
65:
66:const select = '*, product_images(*)'
67:
68:async function save() {
69:  saving.value = true
70:  try {
71:    const payload = {
72:      name: state.name.trim(),
73:      slug: state.slug,
74:      category: state.category.trim(),
75:      description: state.description,
76:      price: state.price.trim() === '' ? null : Number(state.price),
77:      sku: state.sku.trim() || null,
78:      upc: state.upc.trim() || null,
79:      quantity: state.quantity,
80:      status: state.status,
81:      featured: state.featured,
82:      sort_order: state.sort_order,
83:    }
84:    const query = id.value
85:      ? supabase.from('products').update(payload).eq('id', id.value)
86:      : supabase.from('products').insert(payload)
87:    const { data } = check(await query.select(select).single())
88:    const saved = data as ProductRow
89:    id.value = saved.id
90:    slugTouched.value = true
91:    emit('saved', saved)
92:    notify(props.product ? 'Item saved' : 'Item created', props.product ? undefined : 'You can add photos now.')
93:  }
94:  catch (err) {
95:    const message = (err as { code?: string }).code === '23505' ? 'Another item already uses this URL name (slug).' : err
96:    notifyError(message)
97:  }
98:  finally {
99:    saving.value = false
100:  }
101:}
102:
103:async function refreshImages() {
104:  const { data } = check(await supabase.from('product_images').select('*').eq('product_id', id.value!).order('sort_order'))
105:  images.value = data as ProductImage[]
106:  // Let the list update its cover photo without a full reload.
107:  const { data: product } = check(await supabase.from('products').select(select).eq('id', id.value!).single())
108:  emit('saved', product as ProductRow)
109:}
110:
111:async function addPhotos(files: File[]) {
112:  if (!id.value) return
113:  uploading.value = true
114:  try {
115:    let order = images.value.reduce((max, img) => Math.max(max, img.sort_order + 1), 0)
116:    for (const file of files) {
117:      const path = await uploadPhoto(`products/${id.value}`, file)
118:      check(await supabase.from('product_images').insert({
119:        product_id: id.value,
120:        path,
121:        alt: state.name,
122:        sort_order: order++,
123:      }))
124:    }
125:    await refreshImages()
126:  }
127:  catch (err) {
128:    notifyError(err, 'Upload failed')
129:  }
130:  finally {
131:    uploading.value = false
132:  }
133:}
134:
135:async function movePhoto(index: number, direction: -1 | 1) {
136:  const list = [...images.value]
137:  const target = index + direction
138:  if (target < 0 || target >= list.length) return
139:  ;[list[index], list[target]] = [list[target]!, list[index]!]
140:  try {
141:    await Promise.all(list.map((img, i) =>
142:      supabase.from('product_images').update({ sort_order: i }).eq('id', img.id).then(check)))
143:    await refreshImages()
144:  }
145:  catch (err) {
146:    notifyError(err)
147:  }
148:}
149:
150:async function deletePhoto(image: ProductImage) {
151:  try {
152:    check(await supabase.from('product_images').delete().eq('id', image.id))
153:    await removePhotos([image.path])
154:    await refreshImages()
155:  }
156:  catch (err) {
157:    notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t delete the photo')
158:  }
159:}
160:
161:async function deleteProduct() {
162:  if (!id.value || !window.confirm(`Delete "${state.name}" and its photos? This can't be undone.`)) return
163:  try {
164:    const paths = images.value.map(img => img.path)
165:    check(await supabase.from('products').delete().eq('id', id.value))
166:    await removePhotos(paths)
167:    emit('deleted', id.value)
168:    notify('Item deleted')
169:    open.value = false
170:  }
171:  catch (err) {
172:    notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t delete')
173:  }
174:}

408:            :loading="saving"
409:          />
410:        </div>
411:      </div>
412:    </template>
413:  </USlideover>
414:</template>


[app/components/admin/OrderEditor.vue#DC9D]
[Source raw SHA256:dc9daad7ad96d403ce186b94a69065b09a168b368c567ee2fb15869495f07daf]
1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Create or edit an order. Customer orders record who bought what; dealer
4: * orders record what the shop ordered from a distributor. Line items can
5: * point at an inventory item or just describe what was ordered. Online
6: * checkout will create customer orders here automatically once it exists.
7: */
8:const props = defineProps<{ order: Order | null, kind: OrderKind }>()
9:const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
10:const emit = defineEmits<{ saved: [order: Order], deleted: [id: string] }>()
11:
12:const { supabase, check, notify, notifyError } = useAdmin()
13:
14:const statusItems = orderStatuses.map(value => ({ label: value[0]!.toUpperCase() + value.slice(1), value }))
15:const distributors = ['Lipsey\'s', 'Sports South']
16:
17:interface ItemDraft { product_id: string | null, description: string, quantity: number, unit_price: string }
18:
19:const state = reactive({
20:  reference: '',
21:  status: 'pending' as OrderStatus,
22:  customer_name: '',
23:  customer_email: '',
24:  customer_phone: '',
25:  distributor: '',
26:  total: '',
27:  notes: '',
28:  placed_at: '',
29:})
30:const items = ref<ItemDraft[]>([])
31:const id = ref<string | null>(null)
32:const saving = ref(false)
33:const kind = computed(() => props.order?.kind ?? props.kind)
34:
35:const productOptions = ref<{ label: string, value: string, price: number | null }[]>([])
36:async function loadProducts() {
37:  const { data } = await supabase.from('products').select('id, name, price').neq('status', 'archived').order('name')
38:  productOptions.value = (data ?? []).map(p => ({ label: p.name, value: p.id, price: p.price }))
39:}
40:
41:watch(open, (isOpen) => {
42:  if (!isOpen) return
43:  const o = props.order
44:  id.value = o?.id ?? null
45:  Object.assign(state, {
46:    reference: o?.reference ?? '',
47:    status: o?.status ?? 'pending',
48:    customer_name: o?.customer_name ?? '',
49:    customer_email: o?.customer_email ?? '',
50:    customer_phone: o?.customer_phone ?? '',
51:    distributor: o?.distributor ?? '',
52:    total: o?.total === null || o?.total === undefined ? '' : String(o.total),
53:    notes: o?.notes ?? '',
54:    placed_at: toLocalInput(o?.placed_at ?? new Date().toISOString()),
55:  })
56:  items.value = (o?.order_items ?? []).map(i => ({
57:    product_id: i.product_id,
58:    description: i.description,
59:    quantity: i.quantity,
60:    unit_price: i.unit_price === null ? '' : String(i.unit_price),
61:  }))
62:  if (!productOptions.value.length) loadProducts()
63:}, { immediate: true })
64:
65:function addItem() {
66:  items.value.push({ product_id: null, description: '', quantity: 1, unit_price: '' })
67:}
68:
69:function pickProduct(item: ItemDraft, productId: string | null) {
70:  item.product_id = productId
71:  const product = productOptions.value.find(p => p.value === productId)
72:  if (!product) return
73:  if (!item.description) item.description = product.label
74:  if (!item.unit_price && product.price !== null) item.unit_price = String(product.price)
75:}
76:
77:const itemsTotal = computed(() => {
78:  const priced = items.value.filter(i => i.unit_price.trim() !== '' && Number.isFinite(Number(i.unit_price)))
79:  return priced.length ? priced.reduce((sum, i) => sum + Number(i.unit_price) * i.quantity, 0) : null
80:})
81:
82:const money = (v: string) => (v.trim() === '' ? null : Number(v))
83:
84:async function save() {
85:  if (items.value.some(i => !i.description.trim())) return notifyError('Every line needs a description')
86:  if ([state.total, ...items.value.map(i => i.unit_price)].some(v => v.trim() !== '' && !(Number(v) >= 0))) {
87:    return notifyError('Prices must be numbers of 0 or more')
88:  }
89:  saving.value = true
90:  try {
91:    const payload = {
92:      kind: kind.value,
93:      reference: state.reference.trim(),
94:      status: state.status,
95:      customer_name: state.customer_name.trim(),
96:      customer_email: state.customer_email.trim(),
97:      customer_phone: state.customer_phone.trim(),
98:      distributor: state.distributor.trim(),
99:      total: money(state.total),
100:      notes: state.notes,
101:      placed_at: fromLocalInput(state.placed_at) ?? new Date().toISOString(),
102:    }
103:    const query = id.value
104:      ? supabase.from('orders').update(payload).eq('id', id.value)
105:      : supabase.from('orders').insert(payload)
106:    const { data } = check(await query.select('id').single())
107:    const orderId = data.id
108:    id.value = orderId
109:
110:    // Replace the line items with the edited list.
111:    check(await supabase.from('order_items').delete().eq('order_id', orderId))
112:    if (items.value.length) {
113:      check(await supabase.from('order_items').insert(items.value.map(i => ({
114:        order_id: orderId,
115:        product_id: i.product_id,
116:        description: i.description.trim(),
117:        quantity: i.quantity,
118:        unit_price: money(i.unit_price),
119:      }))))
120:    }
121:    const { data: saved } = check(await supabase.from('orders').select('*, order_items(*)').eq('id', id.value!).single())
122:    emit('saved', saved as Order)
123:    notify('Order saved')
124:    open.value = false
125:  }
126:  catch (err) {
127:    notifyError(err)
128:  }
129:  finally {
130:    saving.value = false
131:  }
132:}
133:
134:async function remove() {
135:  if (!id.value || !window.confirm('Delete this order? This can\'t be undone.')) return
136:  try {
137:    check(await supabase.from('orders').delete().eq('id', id.value))
138:    emit('deleted', id.value)
139:    open.value = false
140:  }
141:  catch (err) {
142:    notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t delete')
143:  }
144:}
145:</script>
146:
147:<template>
148:  <USlideover
149:    v-model:open="open"
150:    :title="`${order ? 'Edit' : 'New'} ${kind === 'dealer' ? 'dealer' : 'customer'} order`"
151:    :description="kind === 'dealer' ? 'Something the shop ordered from a distributor.' : 'Something a customer ordered.'"
152:    :ui="{ content: 'sm:max-w-2xl' }"
153:  >
154:    <template #body>
155:      <form
156:        id="order-form"
157:        class="grid gap-5"
158:        @submit.prevent="save"
159:      >
160:        <div class="grid gap-5 sm:grid-cols-3">
161:          <UFormField :label="kind === 'dealer' ? 'Distributor PO / order #' : 'Order #'">
162:            <UInput

180:          </UFormField>
181:        </div>
182:
183:        <UFormField

185:          label="Distributor"
186:        >
187:          <UInput
188:            v-model="state.distributor"
189:            placeholder="Lipsey's, Sports South…"
190:            class="w-full"
191:          />
192:          <div class="mt-2 flex gap-2">
193:            <UButton
194:              v-for="name in distributors"
195:              :key="name"
196:              size="xs"
197:              variant="soft"
198:              :label="name"
199:              @click="state.distributor = name"
200:            />
201:          </div>
202:        </UFormField>
203:
204:        <div class="grid gap-5 sm:grid-cols-3">

206:            <UInput
207:              v-model="state.customer_name"
208:              class="w-full"
209:            />
210:          </UFormField>
211:          <UFormField label="Email">
212:            <UInput
213:              v-model="state.customer_email"
214:              type="email"
215:              class="w-full"
216:            />
217:          </UFormField>
218:          <UFormField label="Phone">
219:            <UInput
220:              v-model="state.customer_phone"
221:              type="tel"
222:              class="w-full"
223:            />
224:          </UFormField>
225:        </div>
226:
227:        <section class="grid gap-3">
228:          <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
229:            <h3 class="font-sans text-base font-medium text-highlighted">
230:              Items
231:            </h3>
232:            <UButton
233:              icon="i-lucide-plus"
234:              size="sm"
235:              variant="outline"
236:              label="Add line"
237:              @click="addItem"
238:            />
239:          </div>
240:          <p
241:            v-if="!items.length"
242:            class="text-sm text-muted"
243:          >
244:            No lines yet.
245:          </p>
246:          <div
247:            v-for="(item, i) in items"
248:            :key="i"
249:            class="grid items-end gap-2 rounded-lg border border-default p-3 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_1fr_5rem_7rem_auto]"
250:          >
251:            <UFormField label="Inventory item">
252:              <USelectMenu
253:                :model-value="item.product_id ?? undefined"
254:                :items="productOptions"
255:                value-key="value"
256:                placeholder="Optional"
257:                class="w-full"
258:                @update:model-value="pickProduct(item, ($event as string | undefined) ?? null)"
259:              />
260:            </UFormField>
261:            <UFormField label="Description">

264:                class="w-full"

266:            </UFormField>

273:            </UFormField>

287:            />

290:

297:          <template

322:

[app/pages/shop/[slug].vue#D646]
[Source raw SHA256:d646f16fa5c93ad1dfa3abb25838bf944f283237634a6662a656a9f9fbcb8d6e]
1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * One shop item: photos, price, availability and description, from the
4: * products the dashboard's Inventory marks active. The home page shop rail
5: * links here. There is no online checkout yet, so buying means contacting
6: * the shop; the email is prefilled with the item and a link back to it.
7: * The built-in sample items (app/data/products) resolve too, but only while
8: * the home page rail is showing them (no featured items in the database), so
9: * the placeholders don't lead to a 404 and real drafts never fall through.
10: */
11:import { products as placeholderProducts } from '~/data/products'
12:
13:interface ProductRow {
14:  slug: string
15:  name: string
16:  category: string
17:  description: string
18:  price: number | null
19:  sku: string | null
20:  quantity: number
21:  product_images: { path: string, alt: string }[]
22:}
23:
24:interface ShopItem {
25:  slug: string
26:  name: string
27:  category: string
28:  description: string
29:  price: number | null
30:  sku: string | null
31:  /** null when unknown (sample items). */
32:  quantity: number | null
33:  images: { src: string, alt: string }[]
34:}
35:
36:const route = useRoute()
37:const { site } = useAppConfig()
38:const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
39:const slug = computed(() => String(route.params.slug))
40:const publicUrl = (path: string) => supabase.storage.from('site-media').getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl
41:
42:const { data: item } = await useAsyncData(`shop-item-${slug.value}`, async (): Promise<ShopItem | null> => {
43:  const { data, error } = await supabase
44:    .from('products')
45:    .select('slug, name, category, description, price, sku, quantity, product_images(path, alt)')
46:    .eq('slug', slug.value)
47:    .eq('status', 'active') // staff can read drafts; the public page must not show them
48:    .order('sort_order', { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
49:    .maybeSingle()
50:  if (error) console.error('[shop] product:', error.message)
51:  if (data) {
52:    const row = data as ProductRow
53:    return {
54:      ...row,
55:      images: row.product_images.map(image => ({ src: publicUrl(image.path), alt: image.alt || row.name })),
56:    }
57:  }
58:  // Same rule as useHomeContent: samples only stand in when nothing is featured.
59:  const { count } = await supabase.from('products').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
60:    .eq('status', 'active').eq('featured', true)
61:  if (count) return null
62:  const sample = placeholderProducts.find(product => product.slug === slug.value)
63:  if (!sample) return null
64:  return {
65:    ...sample,
66:    description: '',
67:    sku: null,
68:    quantity: null,
69:    images: sample.image ? [{ src: sample.image, alt: sample.name }] : [],
70:  }
71:})
72:
73:if (!item.value) {
74:  throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Item not found', fatal: true })
75:}
76:
77:const product = computed(() => item.value!)
78:const selected = ref(0)
79:const current = computed(() => product.value.images[selected.value])
80:
81:const price = computed(() => product.value.price === null
82:  ? 'Call for price'
83:  : new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }).format(product.value.price))
84:
85:const availability = computed(() => {
86:  const quantity = product.value.quantity
87:  if (quantity === null) return 'Ask about availability'
88:  if (quantity === 0) return 'Out of stock, ask about ordering'
89:  if (quantity <= 3) return `Only ${quantity} left`
90:  return 'In stock'
91:})
92:
93:const pageUrl = computed(() => `${useRequestURL().origin}/shop/${product.value.slug}`)
94:const emailLink = computed(() => {
95:  const query = new URLSearchParams({
96:    subject: `Shop inquiry: ${product.value.name}`,
97:    body: `Hello ${site.name},\n\nI'm interested in the ${product.value.name}${product.value.sku ? ` (SKU ${product.value.sku})` : ''}.\n${pageUrl.value}\n\n`,
98:  })
99:  return `mailto:${site.email}?${query.toString().replace(/\+/g, '%20')}`
100:})
101:const phoneLink = `tel:+1${site.phone.replace(/\D/g, '')}`
102:
103:useSeoMeta({
104:  title: () => product.value.name,
105:  description: () => product.value.description.slice(0, 160)
106:    || `${product.value.name} from ${site.name} in ${site.address.city}, California.`,
107:  ogImage: () => product.value.images[0]?.src,
108:})
109:</script>
110:
111:<template>
112:  <article class="item-page">
113:    <NuxtLink
114:      to="/#shop"
115:      class="back"
116:    >
117:      <UIcon name="i-lucide-arrow-left" />
118:      Back to the shop
119:    </NuxtLink>
120:
121:    <div class="item">
122:      <div class="gallery">
123:        <div class="main-photo">
124:          <NuxtImg
125:            v-if="current"
126:            :src="current.src"
127:            :alt="current.alt"
128:            sizes="sm:100vw lg:55vw"
129:            class="photo"
130:          />
131:          <div
132:            v-else
133:            class="photo empty"
134:          >
135:            <span>{{ product.category }}</span>
136:          </div>
137:        </div>
138:        <ul
139:          v-if="product.images.length > 1"
140:          class="thumbs"
141:        >
142:          <li
143:            v-for="(image, i) in product.images"
144:            :key="image.src"
145:          >
146:            <button
147:              type="button"
148:              class="thumb"
149:              :aria-label="`Photo ${i + 1} of ${product.images.length}`"
150:              :aria-current="i === selected"
151:              @click="selected = i"
152:            >
153:              <NuxtImg
154:                :src="image.src"
155:                alt=""
156:                sizes="6rem"
157:                loading="lazy"
158:              />
159:            </button>
160:          </li>
161:        </ul>
162:      </div>
163:
164:      <div class="details">
165:        <p
166:          v-if="product.category"
167:          class="category"
168:        >
169:          {{ product.category }}
170:        </p>
171:        <h1>{{ product.name }}</h1>
172:        <p class="price">
173:          {{ price }}
174:        </p>
175:        <p class="availability">
176:          {{ availability }}
177:        </p>
178:
179:        <div class="actions">
180:          <UButton
181:            :to="emailLink"
182:            size="xl"
183:            icon="i-lucide-mail"
184:            label="Ask about this item"
185:          />
186:          <UButton
187:            :to="phoneLink"
188:            size="xl"
189:            variant="ghost"
190:            icon="i-lucide-phone"
191:            :label="site.phone"
192:          />
193:        </div>
194:        <p class="note">
195:          Online checkout is coming soon. Contact the shop to buy or reserve this item;
196:          pickup is in {{ site.address.city }}, by appointment.
197:        </p>
198:
199:        <div
200:          v-if="product.description"
201:          class="description"
202:        >
203:          {{ product.description }}
204:        </div>
205:
206:        <dl
207:          v-if="product.sku"
208:          class="facts"
209:        >
210:          <div><dt>SKU</dt><dd>{{ product.sku }}</dd></div>
211:        </dl>
212:      </div>
213:    </div>
214:  </article>
215:</template>
216:
217:<style scoped>
218:.item-page {
219:  max-width: var(--ui-container);
220:  margin-inline: auto;
221:  padding: calc(var(--header-offset) + 2rem) 1.5rem 5rem;
222:}
223:
224:.back {
225:  display: inline-flex;
226:  align-items: center;
227:  gap: 0.5rem;
228:  font-size: 0.875rem;
229:  color: var(--ui-text-muted);
230:  transition: color 0.3s var(--ease-fluid);
231:}
232:.back:hover {
233:  color: var(--ui-text-highlighted);
234:}
235:
236:.item {
237:  display: grid;
238:  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.2fr) minmax(0, 1fr);
239:  gap: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem);
240:  margin-top: 2rem;
241:}
242:
243:/* ---- Photos -------------------------------------------------------------- */
244:.main-photo {
245:  aspect-ratio: 4 / 5;
246:  overflow: hidden;
247:  border-radius: 1rem;
248:  background: var(--ui-bg-muted);
249:}
250:.photo {
251:  width: 100%;
252:  height: 100%;
253:  object-fit: cover;
254:}
255:.empty {
256:  display: flex;
257:  align-items: flex-end;
258:  padding: 1.5rem;
259:  color: var(--ui-text-muted);
260:  background:
261:    repeating-linear-gradient(
262:      -45deg,
263:      transparent 0 11px,
264:      color-mix(in oklab, var(--ui-text-highlighted) 5%, transparent) 11px 12px
265:    ),
266:    var(--ui-bg-muted);
267:}
268:.thumbs {
269:  display: flex;
270:  flex-wrap: wrap;
271:  gap: 0.75rem;
272:  margin-top: 0.75rem;
273:}
274:.thumb {
275:  display: block;
276:  width: 5rem;
277:  aspect-ratio: 4 / 5;
278:  overflow: hidden;
279:  border: 1px solid var(--ui-border);
280:  border-radius: 0.5rem;
281:  opacity: 0.6;
282:  cursor: pointer;
283:  transition: opacity 0.3s var(--ease-fluid), border-color 0.3s var(--ease-fluid);
284:}
285:.thumb img {
286:  width: 100%;
287:  height: 100%;
288:  object-fit: cover;
289:}
290:.thumb:hover,
291:.thumb[aria-current="true"] {
292:  opacity: 1;
293:  border-color: var(--ui-text-highlighted);
294:}
295:
296:/* ---- Details ------------------------------------------------------------- */
297:.details {
298:  align-self: start;
299:  position: sticky;
300:  top: calc(var(--header-offset) + 1.5rem);
301:}
302:.category {
303:  font-size: 0.875rem;
304:  color: var(--ui-text-muted);
305:}
306:h1 {
307:  margin-top: 0.5rem;

[app/composables/useHomeContent.ts#F478]
[Source raw SHA256:f4789dfc0528a8e675f0f1de1340a7146660ac8ebd189808eda8785d95f9b803]
1:/**
2: * Home page content managed from the dashboard: the hero stack (Site) and
3: * featured shop items (Inventory). Fetched during SSR, so the page is
4: * complete for visitors and search engines.
5: *
6: * Until the dashboard has entries, or if the database can't be reached, the
7: * built-in placeholders in app/data are shown instead, so the page never
8: * renders empty.
9: */
10:import { showcase as placeholderPhotos } from '~/data/showcase'
11:import type { ShowcasePhoto } from '~/data/showcase'
12:import { products as placeholderProducts } from '~/data/products'
13:import type { Product } from '~/data/products'
14:
15:interface HeroRow { label: string, alt: string, path: string | null }
16:interface FeaturedRow {
17:  slug: string
18:  name: string
19:  category: string
20:  price: number | null
21:  product_images: { path: string }[]
22:}
23:
24:export async function useHomeContent() {
25:  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
26:  const publicUrl = (path: string) => supabase.storage.from('site-media').getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl
27:
28:  const { data } = await useAsyncData('home-content', async () => {
29:    const [hero, featured] = await Promise.all([
30:      supabase.from('hero_photos').select('label, alt, path').eq('active', true).order('sort_order'),
31:      supabase
32:        .from('products')
33:        .select('slug, name, category, price, product_images(path)')
34:        .eq('status', 'active')
35:        .eq('featured', true)
36:        .order('sort_order')
37:        .order('sort_order', { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
38:        .limit(1, { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
39:        .limit(24),
40:    ])
41:    if (hero.error) console.error('[home] hero photos:', hero.error.message)
42:    if (featured.error) console.error('[home] featured products:', featured.error.message)
43:
44:    const photos: ShowcasePhoto[] = ((hero.data ?? []) as HeroRow[]).map(row => ({
45:      label: row.label,
46:      alt: row.alt || row.label,
47:      src: row.path ? publicUrl(row.path) : undefined,
48:    }))
49:    const products: Product[] = ((featured.data ?? []) as FeaturedRow[]).map(row => ({
50:      slug: row.slug,
51:      name: row.name,
52:      category: row.category,
53:      price: row.price,
54:      image: row.product_images[0] ? publicUrl(row.product_images[0].path) : undefined,
55:    }))
56:    return { photos, products }
57:  })
58:
59:  return {
60:    photos: computed(() => data.value?.photos.length ? data.value.photos : placeholderPhotos),
61:    products: computed(() => data.value?.products.length ? data.value.products : placeholderProducts),
62:  }
63:}

California AB 1263 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB1263), signed into law on October 11, 2025, significantly broadens the definition of unlawful firearm manufacturing; imposes new rules for barrels, accessories, and manufacturing machines; increases liability for digital firearm manufacturing code; and creates new 10-year prohibitions for certain misdemeanors. The law affects not only California FFLs, but also out-of-state businesses selling into California or interacting with California residents.

#### SB-704 imposes additional requirements pertaining firearm barrels, effective 1.1.26 and additional requirements on 7.1.27.

````
# CA Handgun Roster UPC Agent

An automated pipeline designed to synchronize the California Department of Justice (DOJ) Handgun Roster and use an AI agent to intelligently identify the CA-compliant UPC/SKU codes for every certified firearm.

Because the CA DOJ does not officially provide UPCs alongside their roster models, this system bridges the gap by leveraging a LangGraph ReAct agent that autonomously navigates manufacturer websites and search engines to extract compliant identifiers.

## Features

- **Automated DOJ Scraping:** Directly parses the CA DOJ official search tool to extract all currently certified handguns, including Make, Model, Caliber, Barrel Length, and Expiration Date.
- **Intelligent Upsert:** Database synchronization ensures existing records are only updated (e.g., if expiration dates change) and new records are safely inserted without wiping existing UPC data.
- **Agentic Web Browsing:** Powered by `LangGraph`, the AI agent can autonomously fetch URLs, parse HTML into readable Markdown, and click links to locate specific product specifications.
- **Universal Strategy System:** Instead of hard-coding logic per manufacturer, the agent reads a universal markdown strategy that dictates step-by-step reasoning for validating CA Compliance (e.g., searching for "10-round" or "CA COMPLIANT" keywords).
- **Flexible AI Integration:** Securely configure powerful remote APIs (like OpenAI's GPT-4o) via `.env`, with a seamless fallback to a local Ollama model (e.g., `gemma4`) for offline execution.
- **Structured Output:** Enforces strict JSON arrays for UPC storage directly into the SQLite database.

## Architecture

The project is split into two completely independent tasks:

### 1. `task_scraper.py`
A lightweight, fast script that fetches the DOJ HTML table, extracts the active roster, and updates the local `database/roster.db` SQLite database. It runs completely independently of the AI agent.

### 2. `task_agent.py`
The AI heavy-lifter. When executed, it:
1. Queries the database for up to 10 handguns that are missing UPCs (or haven't been checked in over 10 days).
2. Loads the strategy from `manuals/universal_strategy.md`.
3. Triggers the ReAct Agent (`agents/researcher.py`) which uses `WebBrowserTool` and `DuckDuckGoSearchTool` to locate the UPCs.
4. Validates the resulting JSON array and updates the SQLite record.

## Installation

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- (Optional but Recommended) [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) running locally.
- (Optional but Recommended) An OpenAI API Key.

### Setup
1. Clone the repository.
2. Create and activate a virtual environment:
   ```bash
   python3 -m venv venv
   source venv/bin/activate
   ```
3. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```
4. Set up your environment variables:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```
   Open `.env` and insert your `OPENAI_API_KEY` (if using GPT-4o).

## Usage

**To sync the database with the current CA DOJ Roster:**
```bash
python task_scraper.py
```

**To process a batch of 10 handguns and find their UPCs:**
```bash
python task_agent.py
```
*(Run this command periodically or on a cron job to slowly enrich the database without hitting rate limits.)*

## Database Schema
The SQLite database stores data under `database/roster.db` with the following key fields:
- `make`
- `model`
- `caliber`
- `barrel_length`
- `expire_date`
- `upc` (Native JSON array, e.g., `[{"tag": "CA Model 10-round", "UPC": "123456789012"}]`)

1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Role checks for the dashboard API routes (server/api/admin), using the
3:# seeded local accounts from supabase/seed.sql. Needs `supabase start` and
4:# `pnpm dev` running. Usage: bash scripts/check-admin-api.sh [base-url]
5:# Exits non-zero if any check fails. Restores the seeded roles it changes.
6:set -u
7:BASE=${1:-http://localhost:3000}
8:set -a; . ./.env; set +a
9:API=$NUXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
10:KEY=$NUXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_KEY
11:STAFF_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad03
12:ADMIN_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad01
13:OWNER_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad04
14:failures=0
15:
16:# Session cookie the way @supabase/ssr stores it: base64url JSON, prefixed.
17:session_cookie() {
18:  local session
19:  session=$(curl -s "$API/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password" -H "apikey: $KEY" \
20:    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"email\":\"$1@admin.test\",\"password\":\"admin\"}")
21:  printf 'sb-127-auth-token=base64-%s' "$(printf '%s' "$session" | base64 | tr -d '\n=' | tr '+/' '-_')"
22:}
23:
24:# expect <status> <label> <cookie> <method> <path> [json body]
25:expect() {
26:  local want=$1 label=$2 cookie=$3 method=$4 path=$5 body=${6:-}
27:  local got
28:  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
29:    got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -b "$cookie" -X "$method" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$body" "$BASE$path")
30:  else
31:    got=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -b "$cookie" -X "$method" "$BASE$path")
32:  fi
33:  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "ok   $label ($got)"; else echo "FAIL $label: expected $want, got $got"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
34:}
35:
36:AI='{"ai":{"defaultProvider":"local","localUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","models":{"local":"llama3.1","openai":"gpt-4.1-mini","anthropic":"claude-sonnet-4-5","gemini":"gemini-2.5-flash"}}}'
37:KEYBODY='{"secrets":{"openai_api_key":"sk-test-abcd1234"}}'

45:expect 403 'staff: team list' "$STAFF" GET /api/admin/staff
46:expect 403 'staff: settings' "$STAFF" GET /api/admin/settings
47:expect 403 'staff: save settings' "$STAFF" PUT /api/admin/settings "$AI"
48:expect 200 'manager: team list' "$MANAGER" GET /api/admin/staff

[Source raw SHA256:1d9346853e9a17ed8a51b30356a335f5841d8d9e8c627700480acb6314cf6122]
1:-- Role checks for the admin dashboard's row-level security, run against the
2:-- local database with the seeded admin/owner/manager/staff accounts (seed.sql):
3:--   docker exec -i supabase_db_accurate-arms-web psql -U postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < supabase/tests/admin_roles.sql
4:-- Everything runs in one transaction that is rolled back, so it leaves no data.
5:-- Each check raises an exception (and stops the script) when it fails.
6:begin;
7:
8:create function pg_temp.act_as(uid uuid) returns void language sql as $$
9:  select set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated')::text, true);
10:  select set_config('role', 'authenticated', true);
11:$$;
12:
13:create function pg_temp.expect(ok boolean, what text) returns void language plpgsql as $$
14:begin
15:  if not ok then raise exception 'FAILED: %', what; end if;
16:  raise notice 'ok: %', what;
17:end $$;
18:
19:-- Admin ad01, manager ad02, staff ad03, owner ad04.
20:
21:-- Staff: inventory, calendar, orders yes; site, settings, marketing, team no.
22:select pg_temp.act_as('00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad03');
23:insert into products (slug, name) values ('rls-test', 'RLS test');
24:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from products where slug = 'rls-test') = 1, 'staff can add inventory');
25:insert into events (title, starts_at) values ('RLS event', now());
26:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from events where title = 'RLS event') = 1, 'staff can add events');
27:insert into orders (kind, reference) values ('dealer', 'RLS-1');
28:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from orders where reference = 'RLS-1') = 1, 'staff can add orders');
29:update hero_photos set label = 'hacked';
30:select pg_temp.expect(not exists (select 1 from hero_photos where label = 'hacked'), 'staff cannot edit the hero stack');
31:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from app_settings) = 0, 'staff cannot read settings');
32:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from marketing_posts) = 0, 'staff cannot read marketing');
33:do $$ begin
34:  insert into staff_members (user_id, email, role) values ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad03', 'x', 'owner');
35:  raise exception 'FAILED: staff promoted themselves';
36:exception when insufficient_privilege then raise notice 'ok: staff cannot write team membership';
37:end $$;
38:do $$ begin
39:  insert into site_content (key, value) values ('announcement', '{}');
40:  raise exception 'FAILED: staff wrote site content';
41:exception when insufficient_privilege then raise notice 'ok: staff cannot change the announcement';
42:end $$;
43:
44:-- Manager: site, settings and marketing too; still no secrets or team writes.
45:select pg_temp.act_as('00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad02');
46:update hero_photos set label = label;
47:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from hero_photos) > 0, 'manager sees the hero stack');
48:insert into marketing_posts (title) values ('RLS post');
49:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from marketing_posts where title = 'RLS post') = 1, 'manager can write marketing');
50:insert into site_content (key, value) values ('announcement', '{"enabled": false}')
51:  on conflict (key) do update set value = excluded.value;
52:select pg_temp.expect(true, 'manager can change the announcement');
53:do $$ begin
54:  perform * from app_secrets;
55:  raise exception 'FAILED: manager read encrypted secrets';
56:exception when insufficient_privilege then raise notice 'ok: secrets are server-only';
57:end $$;
58:do $$ begin
59:  update staff_members set role = 'owner' where user_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad02';
60:  if exists (select 1 from staff_members where user_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000ad02' and role = 'owner') then
61:    raise exception 'FAILED: manager promoted themselves';
62:  end if;
63:  raise notice 'ok: manager cannot change roles directly';
64:exception when insufficient_privilege then raise notice 'ok: manager cannot change roles directly';
65:end $$;
66:
67:-- A signed-in customer (no staff row) sees nothing private.
68:reset role;
69:insert into auth.users (id, instance_id, aud, role, email) values
70:  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000c0001', '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'authenticated', 'authenticated', 'customer@rls.test');
71:select pg_temp.act_as('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000c0001');
72:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from products) = (select count(*) from products where status = 'active'), 'customers see only active products');
73:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from orders) = 0, 'customers see no other orders');
74:select pg_temp.expect((select count(*) from events) = 0, 'customers see no calendar');
75:
76:-- The last admin can't be removed or demoted, even with full privileges.
77:reset role;
78:do $$ begin
