131:/* ---- Settings ------------------------------------------------------------ */
132:export const defaultCatalogSettings: CatalogSettings = { markupPercent: 20, lastImport: null }
133:
134:export async function getCatalogSettings(admin: AdminClient): Promise<CatalogSettings> {
135:  const { data, error } = await admin.from('app_settings').select('value').eq('key', 'catalog').maybeSingle()
136:  failOn(error)
137:  return { ...defaultCatalogSettings, ...(data?.value as Partial<CatalogSettings> | undefined) }
138:}
139:
140:async function saveCatalogSettings(admin: AdminClient, settings: CatalogSettings, userId: string) {
141:  failOn((await admin.from('app_settings').upsert({
142:    key: 'catalog',
143:    value: settings as unknown as NonNullable<Json>,
144:    updated_by: userId,
145:  })).error)
146:}
147:
148:/* ---- Import -------------------------------------------------------------- */
149:const batchSize = 500
150:
151:export interface ImportOptions {
152:  source: CatalogSource
153:  markupPercent: number
154:  /** The export lists everything the distributor has: zero out what it doesn't. */
155:  complete: boolean
156:  /** Status for items the shop hasn't carried before: review them first, or list them right away. */
157:  newStatus: 'draft' | 'active'
158:  userId: string
159:}
160:
161:export async function importCatalog(admin: AdminClient, parsed: { items: CatalogItem[], skipped: number }, options: ImportOptions) {
162:  const { items, skipped } = parsed
163:  const { source, markupPercent, complete, newStatus, userId } = options
164:  // Distributors occasionally list an item twice; the last row wins.
165:  const unique = [...new Map(items.map(i => [i.externalId, i])).values()]
166:  // An empty "complete" file would otherwise mark the whole catalog sold out.
167:  if (complete && !unique.length) {
168:    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'The file has no items, so nothing was changed.' })
169:  }
170:
171:  const roster = await loadRoster(admin)
172:  // Handguns drop off the roster; a copy over a month old can't clear anything.
173:  const rosterFresh = !!roster.fetchedAt && Date.now() - Date.parse(roster.fetchedAt) < 30 * 24 * 3600 * 1000
174:  const rosterIndex = rosterFresh ? buildRoster(roster.entries) : null
175:
176:  const syncedAt = new Date().toISOString()
177:  const ca: Record<CaStatus, number> = { compliant: 0, restricted: 0, review: 0 }
178:  let added = 0
179:  let updated = 0
180:  // Slugs only matter for new items (existing ones keep theirs), but must not repeat.
181:  const slugs = new Set<string>()
182:  const uniqueSlug = (base: string) => {
183:    let slug = base
184:    for (let n = 2; slugs.has(slug); n++) slug = `${base}-${n}`
185:    slugs.add(slug)
186:    return slug
187:  }
188:  for (let start = 0; start < unique.length; start += batchSize) {
189:    const batch = unique.slice(start, start + batchSize).map((item) => {
190:      const result = classifyCa(item.ca, rosterIndex)
191:      ca[result.status]++
192:      return {
193:        external_id: item.externalId,
194:        slug: uniqueSlug(slugify(`${item.name} ${item.externalId}`)),
195:        name: item.name,
196:        category: item.category,
197:        description: item.description,
198:        price: catalogPrice(item.cost, item.mapPrice, markupPercent),
199:        sku: item.sku,
200:        upc: item.upc,
201:        manufacturer: item.manufacturer,
202:        distributor_quantity: item.quantity,
203:        image_url: item.imageUrl,
204:        specs: item.specs,
205:        ffl_required: item.fflRequired,
206:        ca_status: result.status,
207:        ca_reason: result.reason,
208:        cost: item.cost,
209:        map_price: item.mapPrice,
210:        msrp: item.msrp,
211:      }
212:    })
213:    const { data, error } = await admin.rpc('import_catalog_items', {
214:      p_source: source,
215:      p_items: batch,
216:      p_synced_at: syncedAt,
217:      p_new_status: newStatus,
218:    })
219:    failOn(error)
220:    const counts = data as { added: number, updated: number }
221:    added += counts.added
222:    updated += counts.updated
223:  }
224:
225:  // Only after every batch succeeded: a failed import never empties stock.
226:  let soldOut = 0
227:  if (complete) {
228:    const { count, error } = await admin
229:      .from('products')
230:      .update({ distributor_quantity: 0 }, { count: 'exact' })
231:      .eq('source', source)
232:      .gt('distributor_quantity', 0)
233:      .or(`synced_at.is.null,synced_at.lt.${syncedAt}`)
234:    failOn(error)
235:    soldOut = count ?? 0
236:  }
237:
238:  const summary: ImportSummary = {
239:    source,
240:    at: syncedAt,
241:    rows: items.length + skipped,
242:    added,
243:    updated,
244:    soldOut,
245:    skipped,
246:    ca,
247:    rosterFetchedAt: roster.fetchedAt,
248:  }
249:  await saveCatalogSettings(admin, { markupPercent, lastImport: summary }, userId)
250:  return { summary, warning: roster.warning }
251:}

1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Import a distributor catalog export into Inventory (managers and up).
4: * The server prices each item (cost + markup, never below MAP), sets its
5: * California status and updates the distributor's stock; the shop's own
6: * stock counts are never changed. See server/utils/catalogImport.ts.
7: */
8:const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
9:const emit = defineEmits<{ imported: [] }>()
10:
11:const { notify, notifyError } = useAdmin()
12:
13:const file = ref<File | null>(null)
14:const markupPercent = ref(20)
15:const complete = ref(true)
16:const listNew = ref(false)
17:const importing = ref(false)
18:const result = ref<{ summary: ImportSummary, warning: string | null } | null>(null)
19:const lastImport = ref<ImportSummary | null>(null)
20:
21:const resultText = computed(() => {
22:  const s = result.value?.summary
23:  if (!s) return ''
24:  const parts = [`${s.added.toLocaleString()} new items`, `${s.updated.toLocaleString()} updated`]
25:  if (s.soldOut) parts.push(`${s.soldOut.toLocaleString()} no longer in stock at ${sourceLabel(s.source)}`)
26:  return `${s.rows.toLocaleString()} rows read: ${parts.join(', ')}.`
27:})
28:
29:watch(open, async (isOpen) => {
30:  if (!isOpen) return
31:  file.value = null
32:  result.value = null
33:  try {
34:    const settings = await $fetch<CatalogSettings>('/api/admin/catalog')
35:    markupPercent.value = settings.markupPercent
36:    lastImport.value = settings.lastImport
37:  }
38:  catch (err) {
39:    notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t load import settings')
40:  }
41:})
42:
43:async function run() {
44:  if (!file.value) return
45:  importing.value = true
46:  try {
47:    const form = new FormData()
48:    form.append('file', file.value)
49:    form.append('source', 'lipseys')
50:    form.append('markupPercent', String(markupPercent.value))
51:    form.append('complete', String(complete.value))
52:    form.append('newStatus', listNew.value ? 'active' : 'draft')
53:    const response = await $fetch('/api/admin/catalog/import', { method: 'POST', body: form })
54:    result.value = response
55:    lastImport.value = response.summary
56:    notify('Catalog imported')
57:    emit('imported')
58:  }
59:  catch (err) {
60:    notifyError(err, 'Import failed')
61:  }
62:  finally {
63:    importing.value = false
64:  }
65:}
66:</script>
67:

69:  <UModal

133:

137:        >

146:

163:        </p>

[Source raw SHA256:5ccf3f6158f2e0582d2185c4610967e1342b09a4ddf812d8567fdff06b187d03]
1:/*
2: * Save AI configuration (managers and owners) and API keys (owners only).
3: * In `secrets`, a string replaces the stored value and null deletes it;
4: * omitted keys are left alone, so the form never has to send (or know) a key
5: * it isn't changing.
6: */
7:import * as z from 'zod'
8:
9:const body = z.object({
10:  ai: z.object({
11:    defaultProvider: z.enum(aiProviders),
12:    localUrl: z.union([z.literal(''), z.url({ protocol: /^https?$/ })]),
13:    models: z.object(Object.fromEntries(aiProviders.map(p => [p, z.string().trim().max(200)])) as Record<AiProvider, z.ZodString>),
14:  }).optional(),
15:  secrets: z.partialRecord(z.enum(secretNames), z.string().max(4000).nullable()).optional(),
16:})
17:
18:export default defineEventHandler(async (event): Promise<SettingsResponse> => {
19:  const { admin, userId, role } = await requireStaff(event, 'manager')
20:  const { ai, secrets } = await readValidatedBody(event, body.parse)
21:  if (Object.keys(secrets ?? {}).length && !hasRole(role, 'owner')) {
22:    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Only an owner can change API keys and the webhook URL.' })
23:  }
24:
25:  if (ai) {
26:    const { error } = await admin.from('app_settings').upsert({
27:      key: 'ai',
28:      value: ai,
29:      updated_by: userId,
30:    })
31:    failOn(error)
32:  }
33:  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(secrets ?? {})) {
34:    await writeSecret(event, admin, name as SecretName, value ?? null, userId)
35:  }
36:
37:  return {
38:    ai: await getAiSettings(admin),
39:    secrets: await getSecretStatuses(admin),
40:    canStoreSecrets: canStoreSecrets(event),
41:  }
42:})


[server/utils/staff.ts#7AA7]
[Source raw SHA256:7aa7e0c8275bf1fa3976b09fb93e8ccc9b2c6dcd8ff3da15a29fea55e1d9d493]
1:/**
2: * Server-side role checks for the dashboard API routes. Every route under
3: * server/api/admin starts with `requireStaff`, which also hands back a
4: * service-role client: it bypasses row-level security, so the route itself
5: * is responsible for checking what the caller may do.
6: */
7:import type { H3Event } from 'h3'
8:import { serverSupabaseServiceRole, serverSupabaseUser } from '#supabase/server'
9:import type { Database } from '../../shared/types/database.types'
10:
11:/** Service-role Supabase client, typed from shared/types/database.types.ts. */
12:export type AdminClient = ReturnType<typeof serverSupabaseServiceRole<Database>>
13:
14:export async function requireStaff(event: H3Event, required: StaffRole) {
15:  const claims = await serverSupabaseUser(event).catch(() => null)
16:  const userId = claims?.sub
17:  if (!userId) throw createError({ statusCode: 401, statusMessage: 'Sign in required' })
18:
19:  const admin = serverSupabaseServiceRole(event)
20:  const { data, error } = await admin
21:    .from('staff_members')
22:    .select('email, role')
23:    .eq('user_id', userId)
24:    .maybeSingle()
25:  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: error.message })
26:  if (!data || !hasRole(data.role, required)) {
27:    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Your role does not allow this' })
28:  }
29:  return { userId, email: data.email, role: data.role, admin }
30:}
31:
32:/** Turns a Supabase error into an HTTP error with its message. */
33:export function failOn(error: { message: string } | null, statusCode = 500) {
34:  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode, statusMessage: error.message })
35:}

[Source raw SHA256:430fce2afec4ac31c7dcbe474eb7ec9bdcb947b6670eaee5aefcffab9bda558a]
1:-- Distributor catalog import and California compliance.
2:--
3:-- Stock
4:-- - products.quantity is what is physically in the shop. Imports never
5:--   change it; staff do (or Bravo, later).
6:-- - products.distributor_quantity is what the distributor has. Those items
7:--   are ordered in for the customer, so the website shows them as
8:--   "available to order", never as in stock.
9:--
10:-- Imports (server/utils/catalogImport.ts) upsert on (source, external_id)
11:-- through import_catalog_items(). They own the distributor fields below and
12:-- refresh them every run; staff own the rest (name, description, status,
13:-- featured, photos, in-store quantity). An imported price is recalculated
14:-- from cost + markup on every run until staff type their own price
15:-- (price_manual), and the automatic CA status likewise until staff set it
16:-- (ca_manual).
17:
18:/* ---- Products ------------------------------------------------------------ */
19:alter table public.products
20:  add column manufacturer text not null default '',
21:  add column distributor_quantity integer not null default 0 check (distributor_quantity >= 0),
22:  -- Distributor's photo, used when the item has no uploaded photos.
23:  add column image_url text,
24:  -- Distributor specs for the item page and filters (caliber, capacity, …).
25:  add column specs jsonb not null default '{}',
26:  add column ffl_required boolean not null default false,
27:  add column price_manual boolean not null default false,
28:  -- compliant: may be sold to California residents; restricted: may not;
29:  -- review: unknown until staff check it. The shop's CA filter shows only
30:  -- 'compliant'.
31:  add column ca_status text not null default 'review'
32:    check (ca_status in ('compliant', 'restricted', 'review')),
33:  add column ca_reason text not null default '',
34:  add column ca_manual boolean not null default false,
35:  -- Last import that listed this item.
36:  add column synced_at timestamptz;
37:
38:create index products_listing_idx on public.products (featured desc, sort_order, name);
39:create index products_ca_idx on public.products (ca_status);
40:
41:-- Dealer cost and pricing rules, one row per imported product. Kept out of
42:-- products because the website reads that table: visitors must never see
43:-- what the shop pays.
44:create table public.distributor_items (
45:  product_id uuid primary key references public.products (id) on delete cascade,
46:  cost numeric(10, 2) check (cost >= 0),
47:  map_price numeric(10, 2) check (map_price >= 0), -- minimum advertised price
48:  msrp numeric(10, 2) check (msrp >= 0),
49:  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
50:);
51:
52:alter table public.distributor_items enable row level security;
53:create policy "Staff see dealer costs" on public.distributor_items
54:  for select to authenticated
55:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
56:
57:/* ---- California handgun roster ------------------------------------------ */
58:-- Copy of the CA DOJ Roster of Certified Handguns
59:-- (oag.ca.gov/firearms/certified-handguns/search), refreshed by imports when
60:-- it is a week old. Written only by the server.
61:create table public.ca_handgun_roster (
62:  id text primary key, -- DOJ page slug, e.g. 'grp-recon'
63:  make text not null,
64:  model text not null,
65:  gun_type text not null default '',
66:  caliber text not null default '',
67:  barrel_length text not null default '',
68:  expires_on date,
69:  fetched_at timestamptz not null default now()
70:);
71:
72:alter table public.ca_handgun_roster enable row level security;
73:create policy "Staff read the CA roster" on public.ca_handgun_roster
74:  for select to authenticated
75:  using (public.has_staff_role('staff'));
76:
77:/* ---- Shop ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
78:-- Categories that have something on the website, for the shop's filter.
79:-- Runs with the caller's rights, so visitors only count active items.
80:create function public.shop_categories()
81:returns table (category text, items bigint)
82:language sql
83:stable
84:set search_path = ''
85:as $$
86:  select category, count(*)
87:  from public.products
88:  where status = 'active' and category <> ''
89:  group by category
90:  order by category
91:$$;
92:
93:grant execute on function public.shop_categories() to anon, authenticated;
94:
95:/* ---- Import -------------------------------------------------------------- */
96:-- Merges one batch of distributor items (a JSON array, see
97:-- server/utils/catalogImport.ts) into products and distributor_items. New
98:-- items get p_new_status ('draft' to review first, or 'active'); existing
99:-- items keep theirs. Returns {"added": n, "updated": n}. Server only.
100:create function public.import_catalog_items(p_source text, p_items jsonb, p_synced_at timestamptz, p_new_status text default 'draft')
101:returns jsonb
102:language plpgsql
103:set search_path = ''
104:as $$
105:declare
106:  result jsonb;
107:begin
108:  with input as (
109:    select *
110:    from jsonb_to_recordset(p_items) as x (
111:      external_id text, slug text, name text, category text, description text,
112:      price numeric, sku text, upc text, manufacturer text, distributor_quantity integer,
113:      image_url text, specs jsonb, ffl_required boolean, ca_status text, ca_reason text,
114:      cost numeric, map_price numeric, msrp numeric
115:    )
116:  ),
117:  upserted as (
118:    insert into public.products as p (
119:      source, external_id, slug, name, category, description, price, sku, upc,
120:      manufacturer, distributor_quantity, image_url, specs, ffl_required,
121:      ca_status, ca_reason, synced_at, status
122:    )
123:    select
124:      p_source, i.external_id, i.slug, i.name, coalesce(i.category, ''), coalesce(i.description, ''),
125:      i.price, i.sku, i.upc, coalesce(i.manufacturer, ''), coalesce(i.distributor_quantity, 0),
126:      i.image_url, coalesce(i.specs, '{}'), coalesce(i.ffl_required, false),
127:      coalesce(i.ca_status, 'review'), coalesce(i.ca_reason, ''), p_synced_at, p_new_status
128:    from input i
129:    on conflict (source, external_id) do update set
130:      sku = excluded.sku,
131:      upc = excluded.upc,
132:      manufacturer = excluded.manufacturer,
133:      distributor_quantity = excluded.distributor_quantity,
134:      image_url = excluded.image_url,
135:      specs = excluded.specs,
136:      ffl_required = excluded.ffl_required,
137:      synced_at = excluded.synced_at,
138:      price = case when p.price_manual then p.price else excluded.price end,
139:      ca_status = case when p.ca_manual then p.ca_status else excluded.ca_status end,
140:      ca_reason = case when p.ca_manual then p.ca_reason else excluded.ca_reason end
141:    returning p.id, p.external_id, (xmax = 0) as inserted
142:  ),
143:  costs as (
144:    insert into public.distributor_items as d (product_id, cost, map_price, msrp, updated_at)
145:    select u.id, i.cost, i.map_price, i.msrp, now()
146:    from upserted u
147:    join input i on i.external_id = u.external_id
148:    on conflict (product_id) do update set
149:      cost = excluded.cost,
150:      map_price = excluded.map_price,
151:      msrp = excluded.msrp,
152:      updated_at = excluded.updated_at
153:    returning 1
154:  )
155:  select jsonb_build_object(
156:    'added', count(*) filter (where inserted),
157:    'updated', count(*) filter (where not inserted)
158:  )
159:  into result
160:  from upserted;
161:  return result;
162:end
163:$$;
164:
165:revoke execute on function public.import_catalog_items(text, jsonb, timestamptz, text) from public, anon, authenticated;
166:grant execute on function public.import_catalog_items(text, jsonb, timestamptz, text) to service_role;

1:/**
2: * Public shop helpers shared by the home page rail, the /shop listing and
3: * item pages.
4: */
5:
6:/**
7: * What a shopper sees about stock. The shop's own stock is "in store";
8: * distributor stock is ordered in for the customer, so it is never shown as
9: * in stock. `quantity` is null when unknown (sample items).
10: */
11:export function availabilityLabel(quantity: number | null, distributorQuantity = 0) {
12:  if (quantity === null) return 'Ask about availability'
13:  if (quantity > 0) return quantity <= 3 ? `In store: only ${quantity} left` : 'In store'
14:  if (distributorQuantity > 0) return 'Available to order'
15:  return 'Out of stock, ask about ordering'
16:}
17:
18:/** Cover photo: the first uploaded photo, else the distributor's. */
19:export function coverImage(images: { path: string }[] | undefined, imageUrl: string | null, publicUrl: (path: string) => string) {
20:  const first = images?.[0]
21:  return first ? publicUrl(first.path) : imageUrl ?? undefined
22:}

**Shop page (`/shop`)**

- **Category buttons:** a row of buttons (Everything, Handguns, Rifles, Shotguns, Optics, …) with item counts. Clicking the active one clears it.
- **Brand filter:** a searchable dropdown that only lists brands with items in the chosen category.
- **Price filter:** min/max boxes plus quick buttons (Under $250, $250–$500, $500–$1,000, $1,000+).

- Every filter is kept in the URL, so filtered views can be shared, and there's a "Clear filters" link.

**Inventory**
- In-shop items are listed first. A heavier line and a small "In the shop" / "Order from distributor" label mark where the second group starts.
- Each row shows "category · SKU". Clicking the category filters the list without opening the editor, and a bar with "Show all categories" clears it.

332:<style scoped>
333:/* ---- Surface tokens --------------------------------------------------------
334: * At rest the header is transparent and uses the page's own text colors.
335: * Compact/open it becomes a frosted panel in the *same* theme as the page
336: * (a slightly raised tone of the background, blurred), never the inverse, so
337: * dark mode stays dark. Built only from the semantic --ui-* tokens.

339:.site-header {

[app/pages/shop/[slug].vue#22AF]
[Source raw SHA256:22af3af5c06dcd9bd4924cf850bed4fd592e6e84cbd3fa229ff565eb0c801c10]
1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * One shop item: photos, price, availability, California status,
4: * description and specs, from the products the dashboard's Inventory marks
5: * active. The /shop listing and the home page rail link here. There is no
6: * online checkout yet, so buying means contacting the shop; the email is
7: * prefilled with the item and a link back to it.
8: * The built-in sample items (app/data/products) resolve too, but only while
9: * the home page rail is showing them (no featured items in the database), so
10: * the placeholders don't lead to a 404 and real drafts never fall through.
11: */
12:import { products as placeholderProducts } from '~/data/products'
13:
14:interface ProductRow {
15:  slug: string
16:  name: string
17:  category: string
18:  description: string
19:  price: number | null
20:  sku: string | null
21:  upc: string | null
22:  quantity: number
23:  distributor_quantity: number
24:  image_url: string | null
25:  specs: Record<string, string>
26:  ffl_required: boolean
27:  ca_status: CaStatus
28:  product_images: { path: string, alt: string }[]
29:}
30:
31:interface ShopItem {
32:  slug: string
33:  name: string
34:  category: string
35:  description: string
36:  price: number | null
37:  sku: string | null
38:  upc: string | null
39:  /** null when unknown (sample items). */
40:  quantity: number | null
41:  distributorQuantity: number
42:  specs: Record<string, string>
43:  fflRequired: boolean
44:  caStatus: CaStatus | null
45:  images: { src: string, alt: string }[]
46:}
47:
48:const route = useRoute()
49:const { site } = useAppConfig()
50:const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
51:const slug = computed(() => String(route.params.slug))
52:const publicUrl = (path: string) => supabase.storage.from('site-media').getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl
53:
54:const { data: item } = await useAsyncData(`shop-item-${slug.value}`, async (): Promise<ShopItem | null> => {
55:  const { data, error } = await supabase
56:    .from('products')
57:    .select('slug, name, category, description, price, sku, upc, quantity, distributor_quantity, image_url, specs, ffl_required, ca_status, product_images(path, alt)')
58:    .eq('slug', slug.value)
59:    .eq('status', 'active') // staff can read drafts; the public page must not show them
60:    .order('sort_order', { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
61:    .maybeSingle()
62:  if (error) console.error('[shop] product:', error.message)
63:  if (data) {
64:    const row = data as ProductRow
65:    const images = row.product_images.map(image => ({ src: publicUrl(image.path), alt: image.alt || row.name }))
66:    if (!images.length && row.image_url) images.push({ src: row.image_url, alt: row.name })
67:    return {
68:      slug: row.slug,
69:      name: row.name,
70:      category: row.category,
71:      description: row.description,
72:      price: row.price,
73:      sku: row.sku,
74:      upc: row.upc,
75:      quantity: row.quantity,
76:      distributorQuantity: row.distributor_quantity,
77:      specs: row.specs ?? {},
78:      fflRequired: row.ffl_required,
79:      caStatus: row.ca_status,
80:      images,
81:    }
82:  }
83:  // Same rule as useHomeContent: samples only stand in when nothing is featured.
84:  const { count } = await supabase.from('products').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
85:    .eq('status', 'active').eq('featured', true)
86:  if (count) return null
87:  const sample = placeholderProducts.find(product => product.slug === slug.value)
88:  if (!sample) return null
89:  return {
90:    ...sample,
91:    description: '',
92:    sku: null,
93:    upc: null,
94:    quantity: null,
95:    distributorQuantity: 0,
96:    specs: {},
97:    fflRequired: false,
98:    caStatus: null,
99:    images: sample.image ? [{ src: sample.image, alt: sample.name }] : [],
100:  }
101:})
102:
103:if (!item.value) {
104:  throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Item not found', fatal: true })
105:}
106:
107:const product = computed(() => item.value!)
108:const selected = ref(0)
109:const current = computed(() => product.value.images[selected.value])
110:
111:const price = computed(() => product.value.price === null
112:  ? 'Call for price'
113:  : new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }).format(product.value.price))
114:
115:const availability = computed(() => availabilityLabel(product.value.quantity, product.value.distributorQuantity))
116:const ordersIn = computed(() => product.value.quantity === 0 && product.value.distributorQuantity > 0)
117:const facts = computed(() => [
118:  ...Object.entries(product.value.specs),
119:  ...(product.value.sku ? [['Model / SKU', product.value.sku]] : []),
120:  ...(product.value.upc ? [['UPC', product.value.upc]] : []),
121:])
122:
123:const pageUrl = computed(() => `${useRequestURL().origin}/shop/${product.value.slug}`)
124:const emailLink = computed(() => {
125:  const query = new URLSearchParams({
126:    subject: `Shop inquiry: ${product.value.name}`,
127:    body: `Hello ${site.name},\n\nI'm interested in the ${product.value.name}${product.value.sku ? ` (SKU ${product.value.sku})` : ''}.\n${pageUrl.value}\n\n`,
128:  })
129:  return `mailto:${site.email}?${query.toString().replace(/\+/g, '%20')}`
130:})
131:const phoneLink = `tel:+1${site.phone.replace(/\D/g, '')}`
132:
133:useSeoMeta({
134:  title: () => product.value.name,
135:  description: () => product.value.description.slice(0, 160)
136:    || `${product.value.name} from ${site.name} in ${site.address.city}, California.`,
137:  ogImage: () => product.value.images[0]?.src,
138:})
139:</script>
140:

184:                :src="image.src"

186:                sizes="6rem"
187:                loading="lazy"
188:              />

193:

200:        </p>

[app/components/home/ProductRail.vue#F1B6]
[Source raw SHA256:f1b66c522ebd129e36d928a43956cf27810cd2ad798ba3eb6ac5efd55dffb16c]
1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Horizontally scrolling row of shop items.
4: * Scrolls natively (trackpad, touch, shift+wheel) with snap points; mouse users
5: * can also drag it or use the arrow buttons. A progress line tracks position.
6: * `active` stages the cards in when the containing deck section arrives.
7: */
8:import type { Product } from '~/data/products'
9:
10:defineProps<{ products: Product[], active?: boolean }>()
11:/** Scroll position 0..1, for backgrounds that move with the row. */
12:const emit = defineEmits<{ progress: [value: number] }>()
13:
14:const rail = ref<HTMLElement>()
15:const progress = ref(0) // 0..1 scroll position
16:const atStart = ref(true)
17:const atEnd = ref(false)
18:
19:function update() {
20:  const el = rail.value
21:  if (!el) return
22:  const max = el.scrollWidth - el.clientWidth
23:  progress.value = max > 0 ? el.scrollLeft / max : 0
24:  emit('progress', progress.value)
25:  atStart.value = el.scrollLeft <= 2
26:  atEnd.value = el.scrollLeft >= max - 2
27:}
28:
29:function step(direction: 1 | -1) {
30:  const el = rail.value
31:  const card = el?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.card')
32:  if (!el || !card) return
33:  const gap = Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el.firstElementChild!).columnGap) || 0
34:  el.scrollBy({ left: direction * (card.offsetWidth + gap), behavior: 'smooth' })
35:}
36:
37:/* ---- Mouse drag ------------------------------------------------------------ */
38:const dragging = ref(false)
39:let dragStartX = 0
40:let dragStartScroll = 0
41:let dragMoved = false
42:
43:function onPointerDown(event: PointerEvent) {
44:  if (event.pointerType !== 'mouse' || event.button !== 0 || !rail.value) return
45:  dragStartX = event.clientX
46:  dragStartScroll = rail.value.scrollLeft
47:  dragMoved = false
48:  dragging.value = true
49:}
50:function onPointerMove(event: PointerEvent) {
51:  if (!dragging.value || !rail.value) return
52:  const dx = event.clientX - dragStartX
53:  if (Math.abs(dx) > 5) dragMoved = true
54:  rail.value.scrollLeft = dragStartScroll - dx
55:}
56:function onPointerUp() {
57:  dragging.value = false
58:}
59:// A drag must not count as a click on the card it ended on.
60:function onClickCapture(event: MouseEvent) {
61:  if (dragMoved) {
62:    event.preventDefault()
63:    event.stopPropagation()
64:    dragMoved = false
65:  }
66:}
67:
68:const formatPrice = (price: number | null) =>
69:  price === null
70:    ? 'Call for price'
71:    : new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(price)
72:
73:onMounted(() => {
74:  update()
75:  window.addEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove)
76:  window.addEventListener('pointerup', onPointerUp)
77:  window.addEventListener('resize', update)
78:})
79:onBeforeUnmount(() => {
80:  window.removeEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove)
81:  window.removeEventListener('pointerup', onPointerUp)
82:  window.removeEventListener('resize', update)
83:})
84:</script>
85:
86:<template>
87:  <div
88:    class="product-rail"
89:    :class="{ 'is-active': active }"
90:  >
91:    <div
92:      ref="rail"
93:      class="rail"
94:      :class="{ 'is-dragging': dragging }"
95:      tabindex="0"
96:      aria-label="Shop items, scroll sideways"
97:      @scroll.passive="update"
98:      @pointerdown="onPointerDown"
99:      @click.capture="onClickCapture"
100:      @dragstart.prevent
101:    >
102:      <ul class="track">
103:        <li
104:          v-for="(product, i) in products"
105:          :key="product.slug"
106:          class="card"
107:          :style="{ '--i': i }"
108:        >
109:          <NuxtLink
110:            :to="`/shop/${product.slug}`"
111:            class="card-link"
112:          >
113:            <div class="card-media">
114:              <NuxtImg
115:                v-if="product.image"
116:                :src="product.image"
117:                :alt="product.name"
118:                sizes="sm:70vw lg:22vw"
119:                class="card-image"
120:                loading="lazy"
121:              />
122:              <div
123:                v-else
124:                class="card-image empty"
125:              >
126:                <span>{{ product.category }}</span>
127:              </div>
128:            </div>
129:            <div class="card-meta">
130:              <span class="card-name">{{ product.name }}</span>
131:              <span class="card-row">
132:                <span>{{ product.category }}</span>
133:                <span class="card-price">{{ formatPrice(product.price) }}</span>
134:              </span>
135:            </div>
136:          </NuxtLink>
137:        </li>
138:      </ul>
139:    </div>
140:
141:    <div class="rail-foot">
142:      <span
143:        class="rail-progress"
144:        aria-hidden="true"
145:      >
146:        <span :style="{ transform: `scaleX(${0.12 + progress * 0.88})` }" />
147:      </span>
148:      <span class="rail-buttons">
149:        <button
150:          type="button"
151:          class="rail-button"
152:          aria-label="Scroll left"
153:          :disabled="atStart"
154:          @click="step(-1)"
155:        >
156:          <UIcon name="i-lucide-arrow-left" />
157:        </button>
158:        <button
159:          type="button"
160:          class="rail-button"
161:          aria-label="Scroll right"
162:          :disabled="atEnd"
163:          @click="step(1)"
164:        >
165:          <UIcon name="i-lucide-arrow-right" />
166:        </button>
167:      </span>
168:    </div>
169:  </div>
170:</template>
171:
172:<style scoped>
173:.product-rail {
174:  /* Left edge lines up with the page container; the right edge bleeds off-screen. */
175:  --edge: max(1.5rem, calc((100vw - var(--ui-container)) / 2 + 1.5rem));
176:}
177:
178:.rail {
179:  overflow-x: auto;
180:  overscroll-behavior-x: contain;
181:  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
182:  scroll-padding-inline: var(--edge);
183:  scrollbar-width: none;
184:  cursor: grab;
185:}
186:
187:.rail::-webkit-scrollbar {
188:  display: none;
189:}
190:
191:.rail.is-dragging {
192:  cursor: grabbing;
193:  scroll-snap-type: none; /* snapping fights the drag; it resumes on release */
194:  user-select: none;
195:}
196:
197:.rail:focus-visible {
198:  outline: 2px solid var(--ui-primary);
199:  outline-offset: -2px;
200:}
201:
202:.track {
203:  display: flex;
204:  gap: 1.25rem;
205:  width: max-content;
206:  padding-inline: var(--edge);
207:}
208:
209:/* ---- Cards ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
210:.card {
211:  /* Sized by width and height, so the whole section fits short screens. */
212:  width: clamp(12rem, min(21vw, 30svh), 19rem);
213:  scroll-snap-align: start;
214:  opacity: 0;
215:  transform: translateX(3rem);
216:  transition:
217:    opacity 0.9s var(--ease-fluid),
218:    transform 1.1s var(--ease-fluid);
219:}
220:
221:/* Cards slide in from the right, one after another, when the section arrives. */
222:.is-active .card {
223:  opacity: 1;
224:  transform: none;
225:  transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * 70ms + 350ms);
226:}
227:
228:.card-link {
229:  display: block;
230:  border-radius: 0.75rem;
231:}
232:
233:.card-link:focus-visible {
234:  outline: 2px solid var(--ui-primary);
235:  outline-offset: 4px;
236:}
237:
238:.card-media {
239:  aspect-ratio: 4 / 5;
240:  overflow: hidden;
241:  border-radius: 0.75rem;
242:  background: var(--ui-bg-muted);
243:}
244:
245:.card-image {
246:  width: 100%;
247:  height: 100%;
248:  object-fit: cover;
249:  transition: transform 1.2s var(--ease-fluid);
250:}
251:
252:.card-link:hover .card-image {
253:  transform: scale(1.04);
254:}
255:
256:.empty {
257:  display: flex;
258:  align-items: flex-end;
259:  padding: 1rem;
260:  font-size: 0.8125rem;
261:  color: var(--ui-text-muted);
262:  background:
263:    repeating-linear-gradient(
264:      -45deg,
265:      transparent 0 11px,
266:      color-mix(in oklab, var(--ui-text-highlighted) 5%, transparent) 11px 12px
267:    ),
268:    var(--ui-bg-muted);
269:}
270:
271:.card-meta {
272:  display: grid;
273:  gap: 0.25rem;
274:  padding-top: 1rem;
275:}
276:
277:.card-name {
278:  font-family: var(--font-display);
279:  font-size: 1.5rem;
280:  line-height: 1.15;
281:  color: var(--ui-text-highlighted);
282:}
283:
284:.card-row {
285:  display: flex;
286:  justify-content: space-between;
287:  gap: 1rem;
288:  font-size: 0.875rem;
289:  color: var(--ui-text-muted);
290:}
291:
292:.card-price {
293:  color: var(--ui-text-highlighted);
294:  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
295:}
296:
297:/* ---- Footer: progress + arrows ------------------------------------------- */
298:.rail-foot {
299:  display: flex;
300:  align-items: center;
301:  gap: 1.5rem;
302:  max-width: var(--ui-container);
303:  margin: 2rem auto 0;
304:  padding-inline: 1.5rem;
305:}
306:
307:.rail-progress {
308:  position: relative;
309:  flex: 1;
310:  height: 1px;

312:}

320:}
321:

325:}
326:
327:.rail-button {

336:  transition:
337:    background-color 0.3s var(--ease-fluid),
338:    color 0.3s var(--ease-fluid),
339:    opacity 0.3s;
340:}

 * complete for visitors and search engines.

 * Until the dashboard has entries, or if the database can't be reached, the

import { showcase as placeholderPhotos } from '~/data/showcase'
import type { ShowcasePhoto } from '~/data/showcase'
import { products as placeholderProducts } from '~/data/products'
import type { Product } from '~/data/products'

interface HeroRow { label: string, alt: string, path: string | null }
interface FeaturedRow {
  slug: string
  name: string
  category: string
  price: number | null
  image_url: string | null
  product_images: { path: string }[]
}

export async function useHomeContent() {
  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
  const publicUrl = (path: string) => supabase.storage.from('site-media').getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl

  const { data } = await useAsyncData('home-content', async () => {
    const [hero, featured] = await Promise.all([
      supabase.from('hero_photos').select('label, alt, path').eq('active', true).order('sort_order'),
      supabase
        .from('products')
        .select('slug, name, category, price, image_url, product_images(path)')
        .eq('status', 'active')
        .eq('featured', true)
        .order('sort_order')
        .order('sort_order', { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
        .limit(1, { referencedTable: 'product_images' })
        .limit(24),
    ])
    if (hero.error) console.error('[home] hero photos:', hero.error.message)
    if (featured.error) console.error('[home] featured products:', featured.error.message)

    const photos: ShowcasePhoto[] = ((hero.data ?? []) as HeroRow[]).map(row => ({
      label: row.label,
      alt: row.alt || row.label,
      src: row.path ? publicUrl(row.path) : undefined,
    }))
    const products: Product[] = ((featured.data ?? []) as FeaturedRow[]).map(row => ({
      slug: row.slug,
      name: row.name,
      category: row.category,
      price: row.price,
      image: coverImage(row.product_images, row.image_url, publicUrl),
    }))
    return { photos, products }
  })

  return {
    photos: computed(() => data.value?.photos.length ? data.value.photos : placeholderPhotos),
    products: computed(() => data.value?.products.length ? data.value.products : placeholderProducts),
  }
}

+/** The discount fields every product row carries (see the discounts migration). */
+export interface DiscountFields {
+  price: number | null
+  discount_enabled: boolean
+  discount_percent: number | null
+  discount_ends_at: string | null
+}
+
+const dayMs = 24 * 3600 * 1000
+
+/**
+ * The item's current sale, or null when it isn't on sale (switched off, no
+ * percentage, or past its end date). `daysLeft` is null for sales without an
+ * end date, which run until staff switch them off.
+ */
+export function saleInfo(row: DiscountFields, now = Date.now()) {
+  const percent = Number(row.discount_percent)
+  if (!row.discount_enabled || !(percent > 0 && percent < 100)) return null
+  const endsAt = row.discount_ends_at ? Date.parse(row.discount_ends_at) : null
+  if (endsAt !== null && endsAt <= now) return null
+  const daysLeft = endsAt === null ? null : Math.ceil((endsAt - now) / dayMs)
+  return {
+    percent,
+    original: row.price,
+    price: row.price === null ? null : Math.round(row.price * (100 - percent)) / 100,
+    endsAt: row.discount_ends_at,
+    daysLeft,
+    /** "3 days left", "Last day", or null without an end date. */
+    countdown: daysLeft === null ? null : daysLeft <= 1 ? 'Last day' : `${daysLeft} days left`,
+  }
+}
+export type Sale = NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof saleInfo>>
+
+/** PostgREST filter for "on sale right now": pass to .or() together with .eq('discount_enabled', true). */
+export const saleEndsFilter = (now = new Date()) => `discount_ends_at.is.null,discount_ends_at.gt.${now.toISOString()}`

1:/**
2: * The signed-in staff member's event bookmarks (ids of bookmarked events),
3: * shared across the calendar, the event editor and the Find events dialog.
4: * Bookmarks are personal; row-level security limits reads and writes to the
5: * user's own rows.
6: */
7:export function useEventBookmarks() {
8:  const { supabase, check, notify, notifyError } = useAdmin()
9:  const { userId } = useStaff()
10:  const state = useState<{ userId: string | null, ids: string[] }>('event-bookmarks', () => ({ userId: null, ids: [] }))
11:  const ids = computed(() => new Set(state.value.userId === userId.value ? state.value.ids : []))
12:
13:  async function load() {
14:    try {
15:      const { data } = check(await supabase.from('event_bookmarks').select('event_id'))
16:      state.value = { userId: userId.value, ids: (data ?? []).map(row => row.event_id) }
17:    }
18:    catch (err) {
19:      notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t load bookmarks')
20:    }
21:  }
22:
23:  /** Records a bookmark made elsewhere (the Find events dialog saves through the API). */
24:  function remember(id: string) {
25:    if (!ids.value.has(id)) state.value = { userId: userId.value, ids: [...ids.value, id] }
26:  }
27:
28:  /** Bookmarks or un-bookmarks a saved event; returns whether it is now bookmarked. */
29:  async function toggle(eventId: string) {
30:    const on = !ids.value.has(eventId)
31:    try {
32:      if (on) check(await supabase.from('event_bookmarks').insert({ event_id: eventId }))
33:      else check(await supabase.from('event_bookmarks').delete().eq('event_id', eventId))
34:      state.value = { userId: userId.value, ids: on ? [...ids.value, eventId] : [...ids.value].filter(id => id !== eventId) }
35:      notify(on ? 'Bookmarked' : 'Bookmark removed')
36:      return on
37:    }
38:    catch (err) {
39:      notifyError(err, 'Couldn\'t update the bookmark')
40:      return !on
41:    }
42:  }
43:
44:  return { ids, load, remember, toggle, isBookmarked: (id: string) => ids.value.has(id) }
45:}

## assistant

Discounts, the cart and the wider inventory gap are all in and working against your local database. Lint and type check pass; the earlier `EventFinder.vue` errors are gone too. I tested in a headless browser by checking what each page contains. I saved screenshots in `.tmp/` but haven't looked at them myself, so please look over the sale styling yourself.

**Discounts**
- **Editor:** each item now has an "On sale" switch, a discount percentage, and an optional "Runs for (days)" box. It previews what the shop will show, e.g. "$245.65 ~~$289.00~~ · 15% off · 5 days left".
  - Leave the days empty and the item stays discounted with no countdown, until you switch it off.
  - With days set, the sale switches itself off on the site when they run out. Reopening the item doesn't restart the clock.
  - It warns you if the sale price goes under the distributor's minimum advertised price (MAP), since that can break your dealer agreement.
- **Shop cards:** sale items get a red outline, a "−15%" badge, a red sale price next to the crossed-out old price, and a "5 days left" strip on timed sales. The product page and the home page row show the sale the same way.
- **Filter:** there's a new "On sale" switch on `/shop` that only shows items currently on sale.
- Discounts are kept apart from imports, so a re-import never clears them. The price filter and price sorting still use the regular price.

**Cart**
- A cart icon with an item count sits in the header and opens a side panel. In it you can change quantities (up to 10), remove items, see the subtotal and press Checkout.
- Every shop card has an Add / Remove button, and product pages have "Add to cart" and "Remove from cart".
- Items marked "Call for price" can't be added.
- The cart is saved in the shopper's browser, so it survives page reloads and needs no account. Prices and discounts are rechecked whenever the cart opens, and items no longer for sale are taken out with a notice.
- **Checkout (`/checkout`):** shows the items and subtotal and asks for name, phone and optional notes. Since there's no online payment yet, "Send order request" opens an email to the shop with the order filled in. When the Elite payment setup is ready, that button is the one thing to swap for the payment step.

**Inventory:** there's now a real 40px gap between the in-shop items and the distributor items, and sale items show their discounted price in the Price column.

**Browser checks**
- With three test sales (15% for 5 days, 10% with no end date, and one already expired), the On sale filter showed 2 items. Only the dated one had a countdown, and the expired one showed no discount.
- Adding to the cart, the header count, removing, the item carrying over to checkout, and the email link all worked.
- Pages with a saved cart first loaded with an error in the browser console; I fixed that and the console is now clean.
- I turned the test sales off again afterwards.

**Not done or not tested**
- No real payment, nothing is saved as an order in the dashboard, and no tax is worked out; the checkout page says tax and fees are confirmed with the order.
- Opening the email from "Send order request" depends on the shopper having an email app set up.
- I didn't click through saving a discount in the editor; the switch and fields are there and the preview works.
- The new migration, `supabase/migrations/20261027000000_discounts.sql`, is applied to your local database only, and a fresh database reset hasn't been tested.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.reprice_catalog(p_markup numeric)
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE sql
 SET search_path TO ''
AS $function$
  with priced as (
    select d.product_id,
      case
        when d.cost is null or d.cost <= 0 then nullif(d.map_price, 0)
        else greatest(round(d.cost * (100 + p_markup) / 100, 2), coalesce(nullif(d.map_price, 0), 0))
      end as price
    from public.distributor_items d
  ),
  changed as (
    update public.products p
    set price = priced.price
    from priced
    where p.id = priced.product_id
      and not p.price_manual
      and p.price is distinct from priced.price
    returning 1
  )
  select count(*)::integer from changed

export async function saveCatalogSettings(admin: AdminClient, settings: CatalogSettings, userId: string) {
  failOn((await admin.from('app_settings').upsert({
    key: 'catalog',
    value: settings as unknown as NonNullable<Json>,
    updated_by: userId,
  })).error)
}

/** Saves a new markup (owners only, checked by the route) and re-prices the catalog. */
export async function setCatalogMarkup(admin: AdminClient, markupPercent: number, userId: string) {
  const settings = await getCatalogSettings(admin)
  await saveCatalogSettings(admin, { ...settings, markupPercent }, userId)
  const { data, error } = await admin.rpc('reprice_catalog', { p_markup: markupPercent })
  failOn(error)
  return { markupPercent, repriced: data ?? 0 }
}

-- Shop filters, in-store grouping and owner-only pricing.

/* ---- Grouping ------------------------------------------------------------ */
-- Lists show what is physically in the shop first, then what is ordered in
-- from a distributor, with a divider between the two. PostgREST can only
-- order by columns, so the group is a stored column.
alter table public.products
  add column in_store boolean generated always as (quantity > 0) stored;

drop index public.products_listing_idx;
create index products_listing_idx on public.products (in_store desc, featured desc, sort_order, name);
create index products_shop_idx on public.products (status, category, manufacturer);

/* ---- Shop filters -------------------------------------------------------- */
-- Brands with something on the website (optionally within one category),
-- for the shop's brand filter. Caller's rights, like shop_categories().
create function public.shop_brands(p_category text default null)
returns table (manufacturer text, items bigint)
language sql
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select manufacturer, count(*)
  from public.products
  where status = 'active' and manufacturer <> ''
    and (p_category is null or category = p_category)
  group by manufacturer
  order by manufacturer
$$;

grant execute on function public.shop_brands(text) to anon, authenticated;

/* ---- Pricing ------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- The catalog markup (app_settings 'catalog') is owner-only: managers can
-- otherwise read and write app_settings, so this restrictive policy hides
-- that one row from them. The dashboard reaches it through the server.
create policy "Only owners see catalog pricing" on public.app_settings
  as restrictive
  for all to authenticated
  using (key <> 'catalog' or public.has_staff_role('owner'))

## assistant

The 1911 is fixed, markup pricing now always works from dealer cost, and the shop filters have a new layout. One urgent thing first: **your saved markup is 0%.** At 0%, about 5,170 imported items sell at exactly dealer cost, which is no margin. I put it back to 0% after testing because that's what you had saved, so change it in Settings if you didn't mean that.

**Why the Custom 1911 build was under "from distributors"**
The page split items only by whether the shop had stock (quantity above 0). The 1911 is your own made-to-order item with a quantity of 0, so it fell into the distributor group. Now anything your staff added by hand always counts as "In the shop," whatever its quantity, along with imported items you physically have. The "In store now" filter still only shows items actually on hand. Your local database doesn't have the 1911 right now, so I tested with a temporary copy: it showed under "In the shop" in both Inventory and the shop. I deleted the copy afterwards.

**Markup and pricing**
Saving a markup does change prices; I tested the Save button in the browser and checked the database afterwards. Here's why it can look like nothing happened:
- **Many prices are held at MAP** (the distributor's minimum advertised price). Every price is cost + markup, but never below MAP. At 0%, 4,423 items sit at MAP, and at 20% it's still 2,512. Those prices only move once cost + markup goes above MAP.
- **The Settings card now shows this as you type**, e.g. "At 22%: 7,430 items sell at cost + 22%, 2,159 stay at MAP." The message after saving gives the same counts.
- **Prices are always worked out from the original dealer cost**, never from the current price, so changes don't stack. Going 20% → 35% → 20% landed on exactly the same prices for all 9,589 items.
- **The import and the markup button now use the same rule.** I compared every item at 20% and 12.5% and they matched. I also fixed a rare rounding difference in the import's version.
- **"Let imports set the price again"** in the item editor now restores the automatic price as soon as you save. Before, the hand-typed price stayed until the next import.

**Shop filters**
- **Desktop:** a sidebar on the left with four labelled sections:
  - Show only (In store now, On sale, California compliant)
  - Category, as a list with item counts (8 shown, then "All categories")
  - Brand, a searchable dropdown with counts
  - Price, with min/max boxes and quick ranges
- **Above the results:** search and sort on one row. Below that, the item count and each active filter as a chip you can remove, plus "Clear all".
- **Tablets and phones:** the sidebar becomes a "Filters" button that shows how many filters are on. It opens a panel with the same sections and a "Show N items" button.

In the browser, picking a category, a price range and a switch updated the address and chips correctly. Removing a chip and typing a minimum price both worked. Nothing spills sideways at 1440, 1100, 768 or 390px wide. I took screenshots but couldn't view the images myself, so please look the new layout over.

**Not done or not tested**
- The new database change, `supabase/migrations/20261028000000_shop_group_pricing_summary.sql`, is only applied to your local database, and a fresh database reset hasn't been tested.
- I didn't click through the item editor's "Let imports set the price again" button. I tested the database side directly, and the editor shows the old price until you reopen the item.

Lint and type check pass.

## assistant

The shop now has a page-size dropdown with 24, 48 or 96 items per page. It sits at the right end of the row above the results that shows the item count and active filters.

- **Default:** 24, as before.
- **In the address:** your choice is saved as `?per=48` or `?per=96`, so shared links keep it. Other values in the address fall back to 24.
- **Page reset:** changing the size takes you back to page 1, so you don't land past the last page.
- **Clear all:** now clears only the filters and keeps your sort order and page size. Before, it reset those too.

I tested it in a headless browser at desktop (1440px) and phone (390px) widths. Choosing 96 showed 96 items and went from page 3 back to page 1. "Clear all" kept `?per=96`, and `?per=500` fell back to 24. There were no console errors, and lint and type check pass. I took screenshots of both sizes but couldn't view them, so please check how the dropdown looks next to the item count, especially on a phone.

The largest option is 96 because the database won't return more than 1,000 items at once, and image-heavy pages get slow well before that. Adding a bigger option like 192 is just one more number in the list in `app/pages/shop/index.vue`.

<script setup lang="ts">
/*
 * Account modal, opened from the header's account button.
 * Email/password auth through Supabase (@nuxtjs/supabase):
 * - signin / signup / forgot: the three forms, sharing one email field.
 * - Signed in: shows the account email and a sign-out button.
 * Password reset emails link to /account/reset-password, which sets the new one.
 */
import * as z from 'zod'
import type { FormSubmitEvent } from '@nuxt/ui'

type Mode = 'signin' | 'signup' | 'forgot'

const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
const { site } = useAppConfig()
const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
const user = useSupabaseUser()
const staff = useStaff()
watch(user, () => staff.load(), { immediate: true })

const mode = ref<Mode>('signin')
const loading = ref(false)
const error = ref('')
const message = ref('')
const showPassword = ref(false)

const email = z.email('Enter a valid email address')
// Length rules apply when choosing a password, not when entering an existing one.
const password = z.string('Enter your password').min(1, 'Enter your password')
const newPassword = z.string('Choose a password').min(8, 'At least 8 characters')
const schemas = {
  signin: z.object({ email, password }),
  signup: z.object({ email, password: newPassword }),
  forgot: z.object({ email }),
}
type Schema = { email: string, password?: string }

const state = reactive<Partial<Schema>>({ email: undefined, password: undefined })

const copy = computed(() => ({
  signin: { title: 'Sign in', description: `Your ${site.name} account.`, submit: 'Sign in' },
  signup: { title: 'Create account', description: `Join ${site.name} online.`, submit: 'Create account' },
  forgot: { title: 'Reset password', description: 'We\'ll email you a link to set a new one.', submit: 'Send reset link' },
})[mode.value])

const title = computed(() => user.value ? 'Your account' : copy.value.title)
const description = computed(() => user.value ? `Signed in to ${site.name}.` : copy.value.description)

function switchMode(next: Mode) {
  mode.value = next
  error.value = ''
  message.value = ''
}

async function onSubmit(event: FormSubmitEvent<Schema>) {
  loading.value = true
  error.value = ''
  message.value = ''
  const { email, password = '' } = event.data
  try {
    if (mode.value === 'signin') {
      const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })
      if (err) throw err
      open.value = false
    }
    else if (mode.value === 'signup') {
      const { data, error: err } = await supabase.auth.signUp({
        email,
        password,
        options: { emailRedirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/` },
      })
      if (err) throw err
      // With email confirmation on, there is no session until the link is clicked.
      if (data.session) open.value = false
      else message.value = 'Check your email to confirm your account, then sign in.'
    }
    else {
      const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email, {
        redirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/account/reset-password`,
      })
      if (err) throw err
      message.value = 'If that email has an account, a reset link is on its way.'
    }
  }
  catch (err) {
    error.value = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
  }
  finally {
    loading.value = false
  }
}

async function signOut() {
  loading.value = true
  error.value = ''
  const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.signOut()
  loading.value = false
  if (err) error.value = err.message
  else open.value = false
}

// Start fresh each time the modal opens.
watch(open, (isOpen) => {
  if (!isOpen) return
  switchMode('signin')
  state.password = undefined
  showPassword.value = false
})
</script>

/**
 * The signed-in user's dashboard role (null for customers and signed-out
 * visitors). Loaded once per user and shared app-wide; row-level security
 * enforces the same role in the database, so this only decides what to show.
 */
export function useStaff() {
  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
  const user = useSupabaseUser()
  const state = useState<{ userId: string | null, role: StaffRole | null }>('staff-role', () => ({ userId: null, role: null }))

  const userId = computed(() => (user.value?.sub as string | undefined) ?? null)
  const role = computed(() => (state.value.userId && state.value.userId === userId.value ? state.value.role : null))

  async function load() {
    if (!userId.value) return null
    if (state.value.userId === userId.value) return state.value.role
    const { data } = await supabase.from('staff_members').select('role').eq('user_id', userId.value).maybeSingle()
    state.value = { userId: userId.value, role: isStaffRole(data?.role) ? data.role : null }
    return state.value.role
  }

  return {
    userId,
    email: computed(() => (user.value?.email as string | undefined) ?? ''),
    role,
    load,
    can: (required: StaffRole) => hasRole(role.value, required),
  }
}

<script setup lang="ts">
/*
 * Set a new password. Reached from the reset email sent by AppSignIn: the
 * link's ?code is exchanged for a recovery session by the Supabase client on
 * load, then updateUser() sets the password. Without a valid link there is no
 * session, and the page says so.
 */
import * as z from 'zod'
import type { FormSubmitEvent } from '@nuxt/ui'

useSeoMeta({ title: 'Reset password', robots: 'noindex' })

const supabase = useSupabaseClient()

const status = ref<'checking' | 'ready' | 'invalid' | 'done'>('checking')
const loading = ref(false)
const error = ref('')

const schema = z.object({
  password: z.string('Enter a new password').min(8, 'At least 8 characters'),
  confirm: z.string('Repeat the new password'),
}).refine(data => data.password === data.confirm, { message: 'Passwords don\'t match', path: ['confirm'] })
type Schema = z.output<typeof schema>

const state = reactive<Partial<Schema>>({ password: undefined, confirm: undefined })

onMounted(async () => {
  // getSession() waits for the client to finish exchanging the link's code.
  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
  status.value = data.session ? 'ready' : 'invalid'
})

async function onSubmit(event: FormSubmitEvent<Schema>) {
  loading.value = true
  error.value = ''
  const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: event.data.password })
  loading.value = false
  if (err) error.value = err.message
  else status.value = 'done'
}

/*
 * Site header.
 * - At the top of the page it sits open and transparent on the paper.
 * - Once the page scrolls (or a <SectionDeck> leaves its first section) it
 *   morphs into a narrower floating bar.
 * - Items with `children` expand the same surface downward (one shape, no popover).
 * - A highlight glides between nav links and rests on the current page.
 * All content comes from app.config.ts (nav.main, nav.cta, site).
 */
const { site, nav } = useAppConfig()
const route = useRoute()

type NavItem = (typeof nav.main)[number]

/* ---- Scroll state --------------------------------------------------------- */
const scrolled = ref(false)
const activeSection = useActiveSection()
const compact = computed(() => scrolled.value || activeSection.value > 0)
const signInOpen = ref(false)
const user = useSupabaseUser()
const accountLabel = computed(() => user.value ? 'Account' : 'Sign in')
const cart = useCart()
const cartCount = computed(() => cart.loaded.value ? cart.count.value : 0)
function onScroll() {
  scrolled.value = window.scrollY > 24
}

/* ---- Panel state ---------------------------------------------------------- */
const openLabel = ref<string | null>(null) // desktop submenu
const mobileOpen = ref(false)
const isOpen = computed(() => openLabel.value !== null || mobileOpen.value)

// Keep rendering the last panel while it collapses, so content doesn't vanish mid-animation.
const panelMode = ref<'submenu' | 'mobile'>('submenu')
const panelItem = shallowRef<NavItem>()

function openSubmenu(item: NavItem) {
  panelItem.value = item
  panelMode.value = 'submenu'
  mobileOpen.value = false
  openLabel.value = item.label
}
function closeAll() {
  openLabel.value = null
  mobileOpen.value = false
}
// Set when hover opens a panel, so the click that usually follows doesn't immediately close it.
let hoverOpenedAt = 0
function toggleSubmenu(item: NavItem) {
  const justHovered = performance.now() - hoverOpenedAt < 500
  if (openLabel.value === item.label && !justHovered) closeAll()
  else openSubmenu(item)
}
function toggleMobile() {
  if (mobileOpen.value) return closeAll()
  panelMode.value = 'mobile'
  openLabel.value = null
  mobileOpen.value = true
}
}
</script>

}

export interface MarketingPost {

## assistant

Clicking the profile icon now opens a dropdown menu instead of a panel. The right-hand sidebar you saw that said "Browse the shop" was the cart drawer, which is what an empty cart shows. On phones the icons were crowded together, so you most likely clicked the cart, which sits right next to the profile icon.

**Restart your dev server before you try it.** The one on port 3000 isn't picking up new files, so it still returns 404 for the two new pages. I didn't stop it because it's your process. All my testing ran on a separate temporary server, which I've since shut down.

**The menu, when signed in:**
- Your email at the top
- **Account information**, a new page at `/account` with your email, the date you joined, your dashboard role if you're staff, and a change-password form
- **Orders**, a new page at `/account/orders` that lists your orders with status, line items and total, or "You don't have any orders yet"
- **Dashboard**, only for people with a staff role (owner, manager or staff)
- **Log out** in red; if you're on an account or dashboard page, it takes you back to the home page

When you're signed out, the icon still opens the sign-in window. The phone menu (the hamburger) has the same four links.

**Header spacing fix:** adding the profile menu exposed that the header was too crowded. The hamburger got squeezed to nothing on phones, and the profile icon stuck out past the edge on wide screens. The cart, profile and menu icons now sit close together as one group, and the logo shrinks a little on very small phones. Nothing overflows from 320px to 1920px wide, including when the header shrinks on scroll.

**Tested in a real browser:**
- **New customer** (signed up during the test): the menu had no Dashboard, the Orders page showed the empty state, Log out was red and signed them out.
- **Owner** (desktop) and **manager** (phone): both saw Dashboard, and the Account information page showed the correct details.
- **Checks:** lint and type check pass.
- **Cleanup:** I deleted the three test customer accounts afterwards.

I took screenshots but couldn't look at them, so please check the dropdown's look yourself.

**Still to know:**
- The Orders page will be empty for now. Checkout still only sends an email and doesn't save orders. Orders staff enter in the dashboard show up there only if they're linked to the customer's account, and the order editor doesn't do that yet.
- I didn't test actually changing a password through the new form.
- Separately, I noticed someone editing `StippleField.vue` during this session. It briefly threw a `repaintAll is not defined` error while I was testing. I didn't touch that file.

function lipseysCategory(itemType: string, type: string) {
  if (itemType === 'Firearm') {
    if (['Semi-Auto Pistol', 'Revolver', 'Specialty Handgun'].includes(type)) return 'Handguns'
    if (type === 'Rifle') return 'Rifles'
    if (type === 'Shotgun') return 'Shotguns'
    return 'Firearm parts'
  }
  if (itemType === 'Ammo' || type === 'Accessory-Ammunition') return 'Ammunition'
  if (itemType === 'Optic') return 'Optics'
  if (type === 'Accessory-Magazines') return 'Magazines'
  return 'Accessories'
}

## assistant

All three changes are in. They're applied to your local database only; nothing has been deployed.

**Shop filter list:** Handguns, Rifles and Shotguns are now at the top of the category list, right under "Everything." The other categories follow alphabetically. Before, the whole list was alphabetical.

**Shop listing:** in the default "Featured" sort, the 6,244 guns now come before any parts, accessories, optics, magazines or ammo. Within the guns, handguns, rifles and shotguns are mixed together by name, with featured guns first.
- Your own shop items still get their own "In the shop" section at the very top. None of those six are guns.
- The guns go first in the "Available to order" section below it.
- Sorting by price still sorts purely by price.

**Inventory SKU:** the SKU was already there, but only as small grey text under the category, which is easy to miss. It now has its own **SKU** column next to the item name. The SKU is in larger type, with the Lipsey's item number in smaller grey text under it (e.g. `SR-105452` / `Lipsey's ADSR-105452`). Items with no SKU show "—". That includes all six of your own items, so add their SKUs in the item editor if you want them to show.

**Tested:**
- **Shop:** in the browser, the filter list showed Handguns, Rifles, Shotguns first.
- **Database:** the order matches what the page uses. Every gun comes before the first non-gun item, and the default sort is still served by an index, so it stays fast.
- **Inventory:** the new column shows on a 1440px-wide screen with no sideways scrolling.
- **Checks:** lint and type check pass.

I took screenshots but couldn't view them, so please check the new column's look yourself.

"Gun categories" means the three categories the Lipsey's import assigns: Handguns, Rifles and Shotguns. Firearm parts, Barrels and Slides are not counted as guns. If you add a new gun category later, its name needs adding to the database function `is_firearm_category` in the new migration file, `20261029000000_firearms_first.sql`.

## assistant

I've stopped the scan transition on every page except the home page. Your document question is answered below, plus how I'd build it, but I haven't built that part yet.

## The scan transition

Inner pages (about, contact, shop and so on) replayed the laser sweep every time you navigated. Now the dots just fade in over under a second, and the home page keeps its scan. People who've turned on "reduce motion" get no fade at all. In the browser, the about and contact pages had their dots up within 0.35 seconds with no sweep. The shop page took a bit longer to load, then showed them all at once. The change is in `app/components/app/PageBackdrop.vue`, and lint passes.

## Can customers store ID, residency proof, CCW and FSC in their account?

Yes, it's generally legal. No California or federal law stops a dealer from letting customers store these with their consent. Storing them does bring obligations and limits, though. This is general information, not legal advice, so have your attorney or insurer review it before launch.

**What it obligates you to do:**
- **Reasonable security (Civil Code 1798.81.5):** driver's license, state ID, passport and military ID numbers count as protected personal information. You're required to protect them.
- **Breach notice (Civil Code 1798.82):** if the data leaks, you must notify affected customers, and customers can sue. ID scans make you a bigger target, so this is the real risk.
- **CCPA/CPRA:** this probably only applies if you make over about $25M a year, or handle data for 100,000+ people. If it does apply, government ID numbers are "sensitive personal information," with extra disclosure rules and limits on use.
- **Privacy policy:** it needs to say what you collect, why, how long you keep it, and how customers can delete it.

**What it can't replace:**
- **At the counter:** the 4473 and DROS still need the original ID, residency documents and FSC presented in person. An upload is not verification.
- **Records:** the website copy isn't your required record. Bravo stays your system of record.
- **What it's good for:** filling in forms ahead of time, checking a customer is ready before they come in (e.g. "your FSC expires before pickup"), and expiration reminders.

## How I'd build it

1. **Profile details only:** document type, number, issuing state and expiration date for each item (ID/passport/license, residency proof, CCW, FSC). Numbers would be visible only to the customer and to staff. This gets most of the benefit with much less risk.
2. **Optional uploads:** a private file store per customer, links that expire, file size and type limits, a customer delete button, and a log of which staff viewed what. Ideally files get deleted automatically after a set time.
3. **Avoid** storing full ID scans by default, emailing them, or letting anyone besides the customer and authorized staff see them.

Should I build option 1 alone, or option 1 plus uploads? And which staff roles should be able to see these documents: everyone, or just managers and the owner?

## assistant

Yes, partly, but not for the steps the law covers. An uploaded copy is fine for preparing a sale. It can't take the place of examining the customer's originals in person when you complete the transfer.

This is general information, not legal advice. Confirm the details with ATF (your Industry Operations Investigator) and the CA DOJ Bureau of Firearms before you rely on it.

## What an upload can't do

- **4473 identity check (federal):** under 27 CFR 478.124, the buyer presents their government photo ID to you and you examine it, in person, at the time of transfer. ATF doesn't accept photocopies or images for this, and an uploaded scan is an image. Any supplemental government documents, like a current-address document or proof of lawful presence, also have to be presented as originals.
- **DROS (California):** the dealer gets the buyer's information by electronically reading the physical ID card at the counter. You can't swipe an upload.
- **FSC:** the original certificate must be presented at the sale.
- **Proof of residency (handguns):** a utility bill, lease and similar documents must be presented for the transaction. You can photocopy the originals you're shown at the counter for your records. A copy the customer uploaded weeks earlier isn't the same thing.
- **"Federal limits apply" REAL ID licenses:** these need extra lawful-presence documents, also presented at the counter.
- **CCW:** in California a CCW doesn't let a buyer skip the federal background check, DROS or the 10-day wait. An uploaded copy doesn't change any of that.
- **Your official records:** the 4473s and DROS records stay in Bravo and your paper files. The website copy isn't part of your required records.

## What uploads are good for

- **Pre-checking before pickup:** you can look over a customer's documents before they come in and catch problems early, like an expired FSC, an out-of-date residency document, a name that doesn't match their ID, or a REAL ID license that needs extra paperwork. Those issues cause most failed or delayed pickups.
- **Pre-filling:** name, address, date of birth and ID number can be filled in ahead of time. The customer still checks and signs the actual form.
- **Expiration reminders:** for example, "your FSC expires before your 10-day wait ends."
- **Holding orders:** on the order page, staff can see "documents look complete" before ordering a gun from Lipsey's for that customer.
- **Gunsmithing and Cerakote:** checking customer details for intake and pickup. Returning a gun you repaired to the same person generally doesn't need a 4473, but checking ID is still good practice.

At the counter, the original ID, FSC and residency documents still get presented, scanned and examined every time.

## Effect on the account-documents feature

The documents feature from my last message fits this: it's built for preparation, not verification. I'd add three things:
- A note shown to customers: "Bring originals to pickup; uploads are for pre-check only."
- A staff checkbox on the order: "pre-check reviewed," with the staff member's name and the date.
- No setting anywhere that marks a document as "verified for transfer." Only the in-person check can do that.

/**
 * Dashboard settings on the server: non-secret values in app_settings, and
 * API keys in app_secrets encrypted with AES-256-GCM (Web Crypto, so it runs
 * on any server runtime). The encryption key comes from
 * NUXT_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and never reaches the database, so a database
 * leak alone does not expose the keys. Decrypted values stay on the server;
 * the browser only ever sees whether a key is set and its last 4.
 */
import type { H3Event } from 'h3'

export const defaultAiSettings: AiSettings = {
  defaultProvider: 'local',
  localUrl: 'http://localhost:11434/v1',
  models: {
    local: 'llama3.1',
    openai: 'gpt-4.1-mini',
    anthropic: 'claude-sonnet-4-5',
    gemini: 'gemini-2.5-flash',
  },
}

export async function getAiSettings(admin: AdminClient): Promise<AiSettings> {
  const { data, error } = await admin.from('app_settings').select('value').eq('key', 'ai').maybeSingle()
  failOn(error)
  const saved = (data?.value ?? {}) as Partial<AiSettings>
  return {
    ...defaultAiSettings,
    ...saved,
    models: { ...defaultAiSettings.models, ...saved.models },
  }
}

/* ---- Encryption ---------------------------------------------------------- */
function passphrase(event: H3Event) {
  return useRuntimeConfig(event).settingsEncryptionKey || ''
}

export function canStoreSecrets(event: H3Event) {
  return passphrase(event) !== ''
}

async function requireKey(event: H3Event) {
  const raw = passphrase(event)
  if (!raw) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: 'NUXT_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on the server' })
  }
  // Any string works as a passphrase; hashing gives the 32 bytes AES-256 needs.
  const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(raw))
  return crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', digest, 'AES-GCM', false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt'])
}

const toBase64 = (bytes: Uint8Array) => btoa(Array.from(bytes, b => String.fromCharCode(b)).join(''))
const fromBase64 = (text: string) => Uint8Array.from(atob(text), c => c.charCodeAt(0))

/** "v1:<iv>:<ciphertext with auth tag>", both base64. */
async function encrypt(key: CryptoKey, plain: string) {
  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12))
  const data = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv }, key, new TextEncoder().encode(plain))
  return `v1:${toBase64(iv)}:${toBase64(new Uint8Array(data))}`
}

async function decrypt(key: CryptoKey, stored: string) {
  const [version, iv, data] = stored.split(':')
  if (version !== 'v1' || !iv || !data) throw new Error('Unrecognized secret format')
  const plain = await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: fromBase64(iv) }, key, fromBase64(data))
  return new TextDecoder().decode(plain)
}

/* ---- Secret storage ------------------------------------------------------ */
export async function getSecretStatuses(admin: AdminClient) {
  const { data, error } = await admin.from('app_secrets').select('name, last4, updated_at')
  failOn(error)
  return Object.fromEntries(secretNames.map((name) => {
    const row = data?.find(r => r.name === name)
    return [name, { set: !!row, last4: row?.last4 ?? '', updated_at: row?.updated_at ?? null }]
  })) as Record<SecretName, SecretStatus>
}

/** Saves a secret, or deletes it when `value` is null or empty. */
export async function writeSecret(event: H3Event, admin: AdminClient, name: SecretName, value: string | null, userId: string) {
  const trimmed = value?.trim()
  if (!trimmed) {
    failOn((await admin.from('app_secrets').delete().eq('name', name)).error)
    return
  }
  const { error } = await admin.from('app_secrets').upsert({
    name,
    ciphertext: await encrypt(await requireKey(event), trimmed),
    last4: trimmed.slice(-4),
    updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
    updated_by: userId,
  })
  failOn(error)
}

/** The decrypted secret, or '' when it isn't set. */
export async function readSecret(event: H3Event, admin: AdminClient, name: SecretName) {
  const { data, error } = await admin.from('app_secrets').select('ciphertext').eq('name', name).maybeSingle()
  failOn(error)
  if (!data) return ''
  const key = await requireKey(event)
  try {
    return await decrypt(key, data.ciphertext)
  }
  catch {
    throw createError({
      statusCode: 500,
      statusMessage: `Could not decrypt ${name}. The encryption key changed; save the key again in Settings.`,
    })
  }
}

/**
 * Server-side role checks for the dashboard API routes. Every route under
 * server/api/admin starts with `requireStaff`, which also hands back a
 * service-role client: it bypasses row-level security, so the route itself
 * is responsible for checking what the caller may do.
 */
import type { H3Event } from 'h3'
import { serverSupabaseServiceRole, serverSupabaseUser } from '#supabase/server'
import type { Database } from '../../shared/types/database.types'

/** Service-role Supabase client, typed from shared/types/database.types.ts. */
export type AdminClient = ReturnType<typeof serverSupabaseServiceRole<Database>>

export async function requireStaff(event: H3Event, required: StaffRole) {
  const claims = await serverSupabaseUser(event).catch(() => null)
  const userId = claims?.sub
  if (!userId) throw createError({ statusCode: 401, statusMessage: 'Sign in required' })

  const admin = serverSupabaseServiceRole(event)
  const { data, error } = await admin
    .from('staff_members')
    .select('email, role')
    .eq('user_id', userId)
    .maybeSingle()
  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: error.message })
  if (!data || !hasRole(data.role, required)) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Your role does not allow this' })
  }
  return { userId, email: data.email, role: data.role, admin }
}

/** Turns a Supabase error into an HTTP error with its message. */
export function failOn(error: { message: string } | null, statusCode = 500) {
  if (error) throw createError({ statusCode, statusMessage: error.message })
}
