/*
 * Import a distributor catalog export (multipart form: `file` plus the
 * options below). Managers and up, since it sets prices for the whole
 * catalog. See server/utils/catalogImport.ts for what an import changes.
 */
import * as z from 'zod'

const options = z.object({
  source: z.enum(Object.keys(catalogSources) as [CatalogSource]),
  complete: z.enum(['true', 'false']).transform(v => v === 'true'),
})

const maxBytes = 50 * 1024 * 1024

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { admin, userId } = await requireStaff(event, 'manager')
  const parts = await readMultipartFormData(event)
  const file = parts?.find(p => p.name === 'file' && p.filename)
  if (!file) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Choose a CSV file to import.' })
  if (file.data.length > maxBytes) throw createError({ statusCode: 413, statusMessage: 'The file is over 50 MB.' })

  const fields = Object.fromEntries((parts ?? []).filter(p => !p.filename && p.name).map(p => [p.name!, p.data.toString('utf8')]))
  const parsedOptions = options.safeParse(fields)
  if (!parsedOptions.success) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: z.prettifyError(parsedOptions.error) })

  let rows: Record<string, string>[]
  try {
    rows = parseCsv(file.data.toString('utf8'))
  }
  catch (err) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: `Couldn't read the CSV: ${(err as Error).message}` })
  }
  return importCatalog(admin, lipseysItems(rows), { ...parsedOptions.data, userId })
})

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)

/**
 * Dashboard roles, lowest to highest. Each role can do everything the roles
 * below it can. Mirrors the `staff_role` enum in the database, where the same
 * order is enforced by row-level security.
 */
export const staffRoles = ['staff', 'manager', 'owner', 'admin'] as const
export type StaffRole = (typeof staffRoles)[number]

export const staffRoleLabels: Record<StaffRole, string> = {
  staff: 'Staff',
  manager: 'Manager',
  owner: 'Owner',
  admin: 'Admin',
}

export function isStaffRole(value: unknown): value is StaffRole {
  return staffRoles.includes(value as StaffRole)
}

## assistant

Customers can now add these on their account page: optional name, phone and contact email, the notification choices you described, and the ID, proof of residency, CCW and FSC uploads. All of it is encrypted before it's stored. It's only on your local database for now, nothing is deployed, and **restart your dev server to see it**. The restart picks up the new pages and the new encryption key I added to your `.env` file.

**What customers get**
- **Contact details:** full name, phone and contact email, all optional.
- **Order and pickup updates:** email and text both start off; customers turn them on.
- **Marketing email:** starts on and can be turned off.
- **Marketing texts:** these start off. Federal law (the TCPA) requires a customer's written consent before you send marketing texts, so this one can't be on by default. The consent wording is shown next to the switch, and the time a customer turns texts on is recorded as proof.
- **Phone needed for texts:** the text switches stay greyed out until a phone number is entered. Phone numbers are checked and saved in one standard format.
- **Documents:** four sections (ID, proof of residency, CCW, FSC). Each document can have its type, who issued it, expiry date, number, and a photo or PDF up to 10 MB. Customers can keep up to 20.
- **Viewing:** the list shows only the last 4 digits of a number. "Show number" reveals the full number for 30 seconds. A customer can open the file or permanently delete a document.
- **Expiry warnings:** a document within 30 days of expiring is flagged, and an expired one is flagged red.
- **Notice:** the page tells customers to bring the originals to pickup.

**How the data is protected**
- **Encryption:** each document gets its own key, and the number and file are encrypted with it on the server before being saved. Those keys are themselves encrypted with a master key that lives only in the server's settings, never in the database. A leaked database or file store alone reveals nothing.
- **No swapping:** each encrypted item is tied to its owner and document, so moving one onto another account makes it fail to open.
- **No direct access:** the browser can't read the document table or the file storage at all. Only the server can, after checking who is signed in.
- **Upload checks:** the server checks a file's actual contents, not its name. An HTML page renamed to `.png` was rejected.
- **When a file is opened:** it isn't cached, and it's shown in a locked-down mode so a malicious PDF can't run code on your site.
- **Access log:** every upload, number reveal, file view and delete is recorded, and the record stays even after the document is deleted.

**Tested on a separate local test server, with two throwaway accounts (both deleted afterwards)**
- **Defaults:** a new account started with marketing email on and everything else off.
- **Phone and texts:** "555 123 4567" saved as `+15551234567`, and turning on texts recorded the consent time. An invalid number showed an error.
- **Upload:** I saved a license number plus a photo. The database copy doesn't contain the number, and the stored file doesn't contain the image.
- **Reading back:** "Show number" returned the right number, and the opened file was byte-for-byte identical to the upload.
- **Another customer:** they got "not found" for the first customer's number, file and delete, and saw an empty list. A signed-out visitor was refused.
- **Moved row:** moving a document onto the other account made it fail to open.
- **Delete:** deleting removed both the database row and the stored file.
- **Display:** no sideways scrolling on a phone-sized screen, and no page errors. I also fixed a page-load warning the documents list was causing.
- **Checks:** lint and type check pass.
- **Not checked:** I took screenshots but couldn't view them, so I haven't judged how the page looks.

**Before going live**
1. **Production key:** set `NUXT_DOCUMENTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` on the production server to its own new value. Back it up in a password manager: if it's lost or changed, every saved document becomes unreadable.
2. **Staff can't view documents yet.** I didn't build a staff view because you haven't said which roles should see them. Separately, any staff member can currently read customers' contact details (name, phone, email), which is meant for order follow-ups.
3. **Nothing is sent yet.** The notification and marketing choices are saved, but no emails or texts go out. When sending is hooked up, it has to follow these settings and include unsubscribe and STOP instructions.
4. **Deleting a customer account leaves their encrypted files behind.** Their database rows are removed, but the files stay in storage. One test file was orphaned this way, and I deleted it by hand.
5. **Not built yet:** limits on how often someone can upload or reveal, automatic deletion of old documents, and a way to change the master key later.

Which staff roles should be able to view customers' documents: everyone, or only managers and the owner?

## user

what are the benifits to allowing customers to upload their docs

## assistant

Most of the benefit comes from catching paperwork problems before the customer drives in, not from speeding up the transfer itself. The originals still have to be examined in person every time.

## Benefits

**1. Fewer failed or delayed pickups**
Most problems at the counter are paperwork, not background checks. With documents on file, staff can spot these days ahead:
- An FSC that's expired, or will expire during the 10-day wait
- A residency document older than allowed, or a name or address that doesn't match the ID
- A REAL ID marked "Federal limits apply," which needs extra lawful-presence documents
- A missing proof of residency for a handgun purchase

Without that, the customer finds out at the counter, leaves angry, and the sale stalls.

**2. Less risk on special orders**
Before ordering a gun from Lipsey's for someone, you can check that their basic paperwork is in order. That means fewer guns sitting unclaimed and fewer awkward refunds. It can't predict a background check result, though.

**3. Shorter counter time**
Staff can have the customer's details ready before they arrive. That matters most on busy days and at events. There's no Bravo integration yet, so for now staff would read the details off the site rather than have them filled in automatically.

**4. Expiration reminders**
FSCs last 5 years and CCWs usually 2. The site can remind customers before theirs expire. That's useful to them and brings them back to the shop. The dates are saved now, but no reminder emails or texts go out yet.

**5. Convenience for repeat customers**
They enter their details once instead of every visit. It also comes across as professional, and most shops don't offer it.

**6. Transfers, gunsmithing and out-of-area buyers**
You can confirm someone's paperwork before they make a long trip in for a transfer or pickup.

## Costs

- **Liability:** a database of ID scans is a target. Even encrypted, a breach brings notification duties and possible lawsuits.
- **Staff view not built yet:** right now only the customer can see their documents. Benefits 1–3 depend on staff seeing them, which waits on your answer about which roles get access.
- **Ongoing work:** someone has to actually review documents before pickups, or the feature does nothing.

## A lighter option

Most of the value comes from the **type, expiry date and last 4 digits**, not the image. Photos mainly help with residency documents and name/address checks. If you want less risk, I can turn off file uploads and keep only those details. You'd still get the pre-check and expiry reminders, with far less sensitive data stored.

Do you want to keep uploads, or switch to details-only? And for the staff view: everyone, or just managers and the owner?

/*
 * Hand a post to the social automation webhook set in Settings (Zapier, Make,
 * n8n, Buffer, or a custom service), which publishes it to the connected
 * accounts. The webhook receives:
 *   { id, title, body, platforms, scheduled_for, source: 'accurate-arms-web' }
 * A future scheduled_for means "publish then"; null means "publish now".
 *
 * Only posts with a platform-safety check (review.post.ts) of their exact
 * current text and platforms are sent: never if it found something that would
 * break a platform's rules, and with warnings only when the sender confirms
 * them ({ acknowledged: true }).
 */
import * as z from 'zod'

const body = z.object({ acknowledged: z.boolean().default(false) }).default({ acknowledged: false })

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { admin } = await requireStaff(event, 'manager')
  const id = getRouterParam(event, 'id')
  if (!id) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Missing post id' })
  const { acknowledged } = body.parse((await readBody(event).catch(() => undefined)) ?? undefined)

  const { data: post, error } = await admin.from('marketing_posts').select('*').eq('id', id).maybeSingle()
  failOn(error)
  if (!post) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Post not found' })
  if (!post.body.trim()) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'The post is empty' })

  const review = post.review as unknown as PostReview | null
  if (!reviewIsCurrent(review, post.body, post.platforms)) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 409, statusMessage: 'Check this post for platform rules before sending it.' })
  }
  // The rules run again in case they've been tightened since the check.
  const verdict = worstLevel(review.verdict, issuesVerdict(checkPost(post.body, post.platforms)))
  if (verdict === 'block') {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'This post would break platform rules. Fix the problems the check found, then check it again.' })
  }
  if (verdict === 'caution' && !acknowledged) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 409, statusMessage: 'Confirm the check\'s warnings before sending.' })
  }

  const webhook = await readSecret(event, admin, 'social_webhook_url')
  if (!webhook) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Add the social automation webhook in Settings first' })

  const future = post.scheduled_for && Date.parse(post.scheduled_for) > Date.now()
  let update: Partial<Pick<MarketingPost, 'status' | 'sent_at' | 'last_error'>>
  try {
    await $fetch(webhook, {
      method: 'POST',
      timeout: 30_000,
      body: {
        id: post.id,
        title: post.title,
        body: post.body,
        platforms: post.platforms,
        scheduled_for: post.scheduled_for,
        source: 'accurate-arms-web',
      },
    })
    update = { status: future ? 'scheduled' : 'sent', sent_at: new Date().toISOString(), last_error: null }
  }
  catch (err) {
    update = { status: 'failed', last_error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Webhook request failed' }
  }

  const { data: saved, error: saveError } = await admin
    .from('marketing_posts')
    .update(update)
    .eq('id', post.id)
    .select('*')
    .single()
  failOn(saveError)
  return saved as MarketingPost
})

1:/**
2: * The signed-in account menu, shared by the header's account dropdown and
3: * the mobile menu: account information, orders, the dashboard for staff
4: * (any dashboard role; row-level security still decides what they can do),
5: * then sign out.
6: */
7:import type { DropdownMenuItem } from '@nuxt/ui'
8:
9:export function useAccountMenu() {
10:  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
11:  const user = useSupabaseUser()
12:  const staff = useStaff()
13:  const toast = useToast()
14:  const route = useRoute()
15:
16:  watch(() => user.value?.sub, () => staff.load(), { immediate: true })
17:
18:  async function signOut() {
19:    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut()
20:    if (error) {
21:      toast.add({ title: 'Couldn\'t sign out', description: error.message, color: 'error' })
22:      return
23:    }
24:    // Account and dashboard pages need a session: leave them.
25:    if (route.path.startsWith('/account') || route.path.startsWith('/admin')) await navigateTo('/')
26:  }
27:
28:  const items = computed<DropdownMenuItem[][]>(() => [
29:    [{ label: (user.value?.email as string | undefined) ?? 'Account', type: 'label' }],
30:    [
31:      { label: 'Account information', icon: 'i-lucide-user-round', to: '/account' },
32:      { label: 'Orders', icon: 'i-lucide-package', to: '/account/orders' },
33:      ...(staff.role.value ? [{ label: 'Dashboard', icon: 'i-lucide-layout-dashboard', to: '/admin' }] : []),
34:    ],
35:    [{ label: 'Log out', icon: 'i-lucide-log-out', color: 'error', onSelect: signOut }],
36:  ])
37:
38:  return { items, signOut, isStaff: computed(() => !!staff.role.value) }
39:}

import { createError } from "h3";
import { serverSupabaseClient } from "../services/serverSupabaseClient.js";
export const serverSupabaseUser = async (event) => {
  const client = await serverSupabaseClient(event);
  const { data, error } = await client.auth.getClaims();
  if (error) {
    throw createError({ statusMessage: error?.message });
  }
  return data?.claims ?? null;
};
import { createServerClient, parseCookieHeader } from "@supabase/ssr";
import { getHeader } from "h3";
import { fetchWithRetry } from "../../utils/fetch-retry.js";
import { withTimezoneHeader } from "../../utils/timezone.js";
import { setCookies } from "../../utils/cookies.js";
import { useRuntimeConfig } from "#imports";
export const serverSupabaseClient = async (event) => {
  if (!event.context._supabaseClient) {
    const {
      url,
      key,
      cookiePrefix,
      cookieOptions,
      clientOptions: { auth = {}, global = {} },
      timezone
    } = useRuntimeConfig(event).public.supabase;
    event.context._supabaseClient = createServerClient(url, key, {
      auth,
      cookies: {
        getAll: () => parseCookieHeader(getHeader(event, "Cookie") ?? ""),
        setAll: (cookies, headers) => setCookies(event, cookies, headers)
      },
      cookieOptions: {
        ...cookieOptions,
        name: cookiePrefix
      },
      global: {
        fetch: fetchWithRetry,
        ...global,
        headers: withTimezoneHeader(global.headers, timezone)
      }
    });
  }
  return event.context._supabaseClient;
};

1:/**
2: * Envelope encryption for customer documents (see the customer_documents
3: * migration). Each document gets its own random AES-256-GCM data key, which
4: * encrypts the document number and the uploaded file. The data key is stored
5: * only wrapped (encrypted) by a master key derived with HKDF-SHA-256 from
6: * NUXT_DOCUMENTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which lives in the server environment and
7: * never in the database or storage.
8: *
9: * Every ciphertext carries associated data naming what it is, its owner and
10: * its document id, so a value copied onto another row or account fails to
11: * decrypt instead of revealing someone else's document. GCM also detects any
12: * tampering. Plaintext exists only in server memory while handling a request.
13: */
14:import type { H3Event } from 'h3'
15:

17:const encoder = new TextEncoder()
18:
19:/** Bytes backed by a plain ArrayBuffer, which is what Web Crypto accepts. */
20:type Bytes = Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>
21:
22:const toBase64 = (bytes: Bytes) => btoa(Array.from(bytes, b => String.fromCharCode(b)).join(''))
23:const fromBase64 = (text: string): Bytes => Uint8Array.from(atob(text), c => c.charCodeAt(0))
24:
25:export function documentVaultReady(event: H3Event) {
26:  return (useRuntimeConfig(event).documentsEncryptionKey || '').length >= 32

30:  const secret = useRuntimeConfig(event).documentsEncryptionKey || ''
31:  if (secret.length < 32) {

/* The full document number, decrypted for its owner. Each reveal is logged. */
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { userId, admin } = await requireCustomer(event)
  privateResponse(event)
  const doc = await ownDocument(admin, userId, getRouterParam(event, 'id') ?? '')
  if (!doc.number_ciphertext) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'No number saved for this document' })
  const key = await unwrapDocumentKey(event, userId, doc.id, doc.wrapped_key)
  const number = await decryptNumber(key, userId, doc.id, doc.number_ciphertext)
  await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: doc.id, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'view_number' })
  return { number }
})
/*
 * The uploaded file, decrypted for its owner. Served with a locked-down
 * content security policy so even a crafted PDF can't run script on our
 * origin. Each view is logged.
 */
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { userId, admin } = await requireCustomer(event)
  const doc = await ownDocument(admin, userId, getRouterParam(event, 'id') ?? '')
  if (!doc.file_path || !doc.file_type) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'No file saved for this document' })

  const { data, error } = await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).download(doc.file_path)
  failOn(error)
  const key = await unwrapDocumentKey(event, userId, doc.id, doc.wrapped_key)
  let bytes: Uint8Array
  try {
    bytes = await decryptFile(key, userId, doc.id, doc.file_type, new Uint8Array(await data!.arrayBuffer()))
  }
  catch {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: 'This file could not be decrypted.' })
  }
  await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: doc.id, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'view_file' })

  privateResponse(event)
  const extension = { 'image/jpeg': 'jpg', 'image/png': 'png', 'image/webp': 'webp', 'image/heic': 'heic', 'application/pdf': 'pdf' }[doc.file_type as DocumentFileType]
  setResponseHeaders(event, {
    'Content-Type': doc.file_type,
    'Content-Disposition': `inline; filename="${doc.kind}-document.${extension}"`,
    'Content-Security-Policy': 'default-src \'none\'; img-src \'self\' data:; style-src \'unsafe-inline\'; sandbox',
    'X-Frame-Options': 'SAMEORIGIN',
  })
  return bytes
})

/*
 * Save a document (multipart form: the fields below plus an optional `file`).
 * The number and file are encrypted here, before they reach the database or
 * storage; see server/utils/documentVault.ts.
 */
import * as z from 'zod'

const fields = z.object({
  kind: z.enum(documentKindValues),
  docType: z.string().trim().min(1, 'Choose the document type').max(40),
  issuedBy: z.string().trim().max(80).default(''),
  expiresOn: z.union([z.literal(''), z.iso.date('Enter a valid expiration date')]).default(''),
  number: z.string().trim().max(40).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9 -]*$/, 'Letters, numbers, spaces and dashes only').default(''),
})

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { userId, admin } = await requireCustomer(event)
  privateResponse(event)

  const parts = await readMultipartFormData(event)
  const parsed = fields.safeParse(Object.fromEntries((parts ?? []).filter(p => !p.filename && p.name).map(p => [p.name!, p.data.toString('utf8')])))
  if (!parsed.success) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: z.prettifyError(parsed.error) })
  const input = parsed.data
  if (!(documentKinds[input.kind].types as readonly string[]).includes(input.docType)) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Choose a document type from the list' })
  }

  const upload = parts?.find(p => p.name === 'file' && p.filename && p.data.length)
  if (!upload && !input.number) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Add the document number, a file, or both.' })
  if (upload && upload.data.length > maxDocumentBytes) throw createError({ statusCode: 413, statusMessage: 'Files can be up to 10 MB.' })
  const fileType = upload ? sniffDocumentType(upload.data) : null
  if (upload && !fileType) throw createError({ statusCode: 415, statusMessage: 'Upload a JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC photo or a PDF.' })

  const { count, error: countError } = await admin.from('customer_documents').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).eq('user_id', userId)
  failOn(countError)
  if ((count ?? 0) >= maxDocumentsPerCustomer) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 409, statusMessage: `You can keep up to ${maxDocumentsPerCustomer} documents. Delete an old one first.` })
  }

  const id = crypto.randomUUID()
  const { key, wrapped, version } = await newDocumentKey(event, userId, id)
  const path = `${userId}/${id}`
  if (upload && fileType) {
    const sealed = await encryptFile(key, userId, id, fileType, new Uint8Array(upload.data))
    const { error } = await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).upload(path, sealed, { contentType: 'application/octet-stream', upsert: false })
    failOn(error)
  }

  const { error } = await admin.from('customer_documents').insert({
    id,
    user_id: userId,
    kind: input.kind,
    doc_type: input.docType,
    issued_by: input.issuedBy,
    expires_on: input.expiresOn || null,
    number_ciphertext: input.number ? await encryptNumber(key, userId, id, input.number) : null,
    number_last4: input.number.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '').slice(-4),
    wrapped_key: wrapped,
    key_version: version,
    file_path: upload ? path : null,
    file_type: fileType,
    file_size: upload ? upload.data.length : null,
  })
  if (error) {
    if (upload) await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).remove([path])
    failOn(error)
  }
  await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: id, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'upload' })
  return { id }
})

/**
 * Dashboard roles, lowest to highest. Each role can do everything the roles
 * below it can. Mirrors the `staff_role` enum in the database, where the same
 * order is enforced by row-level security.
 */
export const staffRoles = ['staff', 'manager', 'owner', 'admin'] as const
export type StaffRole = (typeof staffRoles)[number]

export const staffRoleLabels: Record<StaffRole, string> = {
  staff: 'Staff',
  manager: 'Manager',
  owner: 'Owner',
  admin: 'Admin',
}

export function isStaffRole(value: unknown): value is StaffRole {
  return staffRoles.includes(value as StaffRole)
}

/** True when `role` is `required` or higher. */
export function hasRole(role: StaffRole | null | undefined, required: StaffRole) {
  return !!role && staffRoles.indexOf(role) >= staffRoles.indexOf(required)
}

/**
 * Roles `actor` may grant, change or remove on other people: admins manage
 * everyone, owners everyone but admins, managers staff only, staff no one.
 */
export function manageableRoles(actor: StaffRole | null | undefined): StaffRole[] {
  if (actor === 'admin') return [...staffRoles]

 export const documentBucket = 'customer-documents'
 
+
+/**
+ * Erases encrypted files whose document rows are gone (queued by the
+ * customer_documents delete trigger, including whole-account deletions).
+ * Runs from the documents:purge task. Returns how many files were removed.
+ */
+export async function purgeDocumentFiles(admin: AdminClient, limit = 500) {
+  const { data, error } = await admin.from('customer_document_purge').select('file_path').order('queued_at').limit(limit)
+  failOn(error)
+  const paths = (data ?? []).map(row => row.file_path)
+  if (!paths.length) return 0
+  // Removing a file that's already gone isn't an error, so the queue always drains.
+  failOn((await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).remove(paths)).error)
+  failOn((await admin.from('customer_document_purge').delete().in('file_path', paths)).error)
+  return paths.length
+}

<script setup lang="ts">
/*
 * Account information: the signed-in customer's email, membership date and
 * dashboard role (staff only), optional contact details and notification
 * choices, saved documents (encrypted; see server/utils/documentVault.ts),
 * and changing their password. Signed-out visitors get a sign-in prompt.
 */
import * as z from 'zod'
import type { FormSubmitEvent } from '@nuxt/ui'

useSeoMeta({ title: 'Account', robots: 'noindex' })

const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
const user = useSupabaseUser()
const staff = useStaff()
const toast = useToast()
const signInOpen = ref(false)

// The session's JWT claims lack created_at; the full user record has it.
const { data: details } = await useAsyncData('account-details', async () => {
  if (!user.value) return null
  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
  return data.user ? { email: data.user.email ?? '', createdAt: data.user.created_at } : null
}, { watch: [() => user.value?.sub] })

const memberSince = computed(() => details.value?.createdAt
  ? new Date(details.value.createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'long', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' })
  : '')

const schema = z.object({
  password: z.string('Enter a new password').min(8, 'At least 8 characters'),
  confirm: z.string('Repeat the new password'),
}).refine(data => data.password === data.confirm, { message: 'Passwords don\'t match', path: ['confirm'] })
type Schema = z.output<typeof schema>

const state = reactive<Partial<Schema>>({ password: undefined, confirm: undefined })
const saving = ref(false)

async function onSubmit(event: FormSubmitEvent<Schema>) {
  saving.value = true
  const { error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({ password: event.data.password })
  saving.value = false
  if (error) {
    toast.add({ title: 'Couldn\'t update password', description: error.message, color: 'error' })
    return
  }
  state.password = undefined
  state.confirm = undefined
  toast.add({ title: 'Password updated', color: 'success', icon: 'i-lucide-circle-check' })
}
</script>

<template>

    title="Your account."

 }
 
+/* ---- Expiry reminders -----------------------------------------------------
+ * Shown in the site (account page and header) 30 and 7 days before a
+ * document expires and once it has expired. Proof of residency is left out:
+ * its date is the statement date, not an expiry.
+ */
+export const reminderKinds = ['id', 'ccw', 'fsc'] as const satisfies readonly DocumentKind[]
+export type ReminderStage = 30 | 7 | 0
+
+/** Today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) at the shop, in California. */
+export function shopToday(now = new Date()) {
+  return now.toLocaleDateString('en-CA', { timeZone: 'America/Los_Angeles' })
+}
+
+/** Whole days from `today` until `date` (both YYYY-MM-DD); negative once past. */
+export function daysUntil(date: string, today = shopToday()) {
+  return Math.round((Date.parse(`${date}T00:00Z`) - Date.parse(`${today}T00:00Z`)) / 86_400_000)
+}
+
+/** The reminder stage a document is in today, or null when none applies. */
+export function reminderStage(doc: { kind: string, expiresOn: string | null }, today = shopToday()): ReminderStage | null {
+  if (!doc.expiresOn || !(reminderKinds as readonly string[]).includes(doc.kind)) return null
+  const days = daysUntil(doc.expiresOn, today)
+  if (days < 0) return 0
+  if (days <= 7) return 7
+  if (days <= 30) return 30
+  return null
+}
+
+/** The stage to show, or null when there is none or the customer already dismissed it. */
+export function dueReminder(doc: { kind: string, expiresOn: string | null, reminderDismissed: number | null }, today = shopToday()) {
+  const stage = reminderStage(doc, today)
+  if (stage === null) return null
+  return doc.reminderDismissed === null || stage < doc.reminderDismissed ? stage : null
+}
+
+export interface DocumentReminder {
+  id: string
+  kind: DocumentKind
+  docType: string
+  expiresOn: string
+  stage: ReminderStage
+}
+
+/** "expires Mar 3, 2027 (in 24 days)" / "expired Mar 3, 2027". */
+export function reminderText(reminder: { expiresOn: string, stage: ReminderStage }, today = shopToday()) {
+  const date = new Date(`${reminder.expiresOn}T12:00`).toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' })
+  if (reminder.stage === 0) return `expired ${date}`
+  const days = daysUntil(reminder.expiresOn, today)
+  return `expires ${date} (${days === 0 ? 'today' : days === 1 ? 'tomorrow' : `in ${days} days`})`
+}
+

1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Account modal, opened from the header's account button.
4: * Email/password auth through Supabase (@nuxtjs/supabase):
5: * - signin / signup / forgot: the three forms, sharing one email field.
6: * - Signed in: shows the account email and a sign-out button.
7: * Password reset emails link to /account/reset-password, which sets the new one.
8: */
9:import * as z from 'zod'
10:import type { FormSubmitEvent } from '@nuxt/ui'
11:
12:type Mode = 'signin' | 'signup' | 'forgot'
13:
14:const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
15:const { site } = useAppConfig()
16:const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
17:const user = useSupabaseUser()
18:const staff = useStaff()
19:watch(user, () => staff.load(), { immediate: true })
20:
21:const mode = ref<Mode>('signin')
22:const loading = ref(false)
23:const error = ref('')
24:const message = ref('')
25:const showPassword = ref(false)
26:
27:const email = z.email('Enter a valid email address')
28:// Length rules apply when choosing a password, not when entering an existing one.
29:const password = z.string('Enter your password').min(1, 'Enter your password')
30:const newPassword = z.string('Choose a password').min(8, 'At least 8 characters')
31:const schemas = {
32:  signin: z.object({ email, password }),
33:  signup: z.object({ email, password: newPassword }),
34:  forgot: z.object({ email }),
35:}
36:type Schema = { email: string, password?: string }
37:
38:const state = reactive<Partial<Schema>>({ email: undefined, password: undefined })
39:
40:const copy = computed(() => ({
41:  signin: { title: 'Sign in', description: `Your ${site.name} account.`, submit: 'Sign in' },
42:  signup: { title: 'Create account', description: `Join ${site.name} online.`, submit: 'Create account' },
43:  forgot: { title: 'Reset password', description: 'We\'ll email you a link to set a new one.', submit: 'Send reset link' },
44:})[mode.value])
45:
46:const title = computed(() => user.value ? 'Your account' : copy.value.title)
47:const description = computed(() => user.value ? `Signed in to ${site.name}.` : copy.value.description)
48:
49:function switchMode(next: Mode) {
50:  mode.value = next
51:  error.value = ''
52:  message.value = ''
53:}
54:
55:async function onSubmit(event: FormSubmitEvent<Schema>) {
56:  loading.value = true
57:  error.value = ''
58:  message.value = ''
59:  const { email, password = '' } = event.data
60:  try {
61:    if (mode.value === 'signin') {
62:      const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })
63:      if (err) throw err
64:      open.value = false
65:    }
66:    else if (mode.value === 'signup') {
67:      const { data, error: err } = await supabase.auth.signUp({
68:        email,
69:        password,
70:        options: { emailRedirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/` },
71:      })
72:      if (err) throw err
73:      // With email confirmation on, there is no session until the link is clicked.
74:      if (data.session) open.value = false
75:      else message.value = 'Check your email to confirm your account, then sign in.'
76:    }
77:    else {
78:      const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email, {
79:        redirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/account/reset-password`,
80:      })
81:      if (err) throw err
82:      message.value = 'If that email has an account, a reset link is on its way.'
83:    }
84:  }
85:  catch (err) {
86:    error.value = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'
87:  }
88:  finally {
89:    loading.value = false
90:  }
91:}
92:
93:async function signOut() {
94:  loading.value = true
95:  error.value = ''
96:  const { error: err } = await supabase.auth.signOut()
97:  loading.value = false
98:  if (err) error.value = err.message
99:  else open.value = false
100:}
101:
102:// Start fresh each time the modal opens.
103:watch(open, (isOpen) => {
104:  if (!isOpen) return
105:  switchMode('signin')
106:  state.password = undefined
107:  showPassword.value = false
108:})
109:</script>

117:      content: 'max-w-md rounded-2xl',
118:      header: 'px-6 pt-6 pb-0 sm:px-8 sm:pt-8 border-none',
119:      title: 'font-display text-4xl font-normal leading-none tracking-tight',
120:      description: 'mt-2',

[app/composables/useAccountMenu.ts#5C22]
[Source raw SHA256:5c227ed3bee061310f1c1a4fb6fa359d1efcd26a8f6858263bfcdd88683fc67a]
1:/**
2: * The signed-in account menu, shared by the header's account dropdown and
3: * the mobile menu: account information, orders, the dashboard for staff
4: * (any dashboard role; row-level security still decides what they can do),
5: * then sign out.
6: */
7:import type { DropdownMenuItem } from '@nuxt/ui'
8:
9:export function useAccountMenu() {
10:  const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
11:  const user = useSupabaseUser()
12:  const staff = useStaff()
13:  const toast = useToast()
14:  const route = useRoute()
15:
16:  watch(() => user.value?.sub, () => staff.load(), { immediate: true })
17:
18:  async function signOut() {
19:    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut()
20:    if (error) {
21:      toast.add({ title: 'Couldn\'t sign out', description: error.message, color: 'error' })
22:      return
23:    }
24:    // Account and dashboard pages need a session: leave them.
25:    if (route.path.startsWith('/account') || route.path.startsWith('/admin')) await navigateTo('/')
26:  }
27:
28:  const items = computed<DropdownMenuItem[][]>(() => [
29:    [{ label: (user.value?.email as string | undefined) ?? 'Account', type: 'label' }],
30:    [
31:      { label: 'Account information', icon: 'i-lucide-user-round', to: '/account' },
32:      { label: 'Orders', icon: 'i-lucide-package', to: '/account/orders' },
33:      ...(staff.role.value ? [{ label: 'Dashboard', icon: 'i-lucide-layout-dashboard', to: '/admin' }] : []),
34:    ],
35:    [{ label: 'Log out', icon: 'i-lucide-log-out', color: 'error', onSelect: signOut }],
36:  ])
37:
38:  return { items, signOut, isStaff: computed(() => !!staff.role.value) }
39:}

[Source raw SHA256:52d2be35a5a276bf7b25ac12b2598b1dc543765bf3b4f2ad0f0faaa2a9cb844a]
1:/*
2: * Document master key status for the owner's Settings panel: which key
3: * version is current, which versions this server has, and how many
4: * documents are still wrapped by each version.
5: */
6:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
7:  const { admin } = await requireStaff(event, 'owner')
8:  const versions = documentKeyVersions(event)
9:  const { data, error } = await admin.from('customer_documents').select('key_version')
10:  failOn(error)
11:  const counts: Record<number, number> = {}
12:  for (const row of data ?? []) counts[row.key_version] = (counts[row.key_version] ?? 0) + 1
13:  const stale = Object.entries(counts).filter(([v]) => Number(v) !== versions.current).reduce((sum, [, n]) => sum + n, 0)
14:  return { ...versions, counts, stale }
15:})


[server/api/admin/documents/rewrap.post.ts#1ED4]
[Source raw SHA256:1ed444ef31935e3e4457a12409c0a80758ac8a10b18d3f7f7a370c14daee8bf8]
1:/*
2: * Key rotation: re-wrap documents still on an older master key with the
3: * current one (a batch per call; call again while `remaining` > 0). Owner only.
4: */
5:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
6:  const { userId, admin } = await requireStaff(event, 'owner')
7:  const rewrapped = await rewrapDocuments(event, admin, userId)
8:  const { current } = documentKeyVersions(event)
9:  const { count, error } = await admin.from('customer_documents').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).neq('key_version', current)
10:  failOn(error)
11:  return { rewrapped, remaining: count ?? 0 }
12:})

      "arguments": "{\"content\":\"<script setup lang=\\\"ts\\\">\\n/*\\n * Owner-only: customer document key rotation. Shows which master key version\\n * is current and how many documents are still wrapped by older ones, and\\n * re-wraps them in batches (server/api/admin/documents). The steps to add a\\n * new key are in .env.example (NUXT_DOCUMENTS_KEY_VERSION / RETIRED_KEYS).\\n */\\ninterface KeyStatus { current: number, ready: boolean, available: number[], counts: Record<string, number>, stale: number }\\n\\nconst toast = useToast()\\nconst { data, refresh, error } = await useFetch<KeyStatus>('/api/admin/documents/keys', { server: false })\\nconst running = ref(false)\\nconst missing = computed(() => Object.keys(data.value?.counts ?? {}).map(Number).filter(v => !data.value?.available.includes(v)))\\n\\nasync function rotate() {\\n  running.value = true\\n  let total = 0\\n  try {\\n    for (;;) {\\n      const { rewrapped, remaining } = await $fetch('/api/admin/documents/rewrap', { method: 'POST' })\\n      total += rewrapped\\n      if (!remaining || !rewrapped) break\\n    }\\n    toast.add({ title: 'Keys rotated', description: `${total.toLocaleString()} documents moved to key version ${data.value?.current}.`, color: 'success' })\\n  }\\n  catch (err) {\\n    const e = err as { data?: { statusMessage?: string } }\\n    toast.add({ title: 'Rotation stopped', description: e.data?.statusMessage ?? 'Please try again.', color: 'error' })\\n  }\\n  finally {\\n    running.value = false\\n    await refresh()\\n  }\\n}\\n</script>\\n\\n<template>\\n  <UCard>\\n    <template #header>\\n      <div class=\\\"flex items-start justify-between gap-3\\\">\\n        <div>\\n          <h2 class=\\\"font-sans text-lg font-medium\\\">\\n            Customer document encryption\\n          </h2>\\n          <p class=\\\"text-sm text-muted\\\">\\n            Only owners see this. Each document has its own key, locked with the server's master key. After adding a\\n            new master key on Railway (see .env.example), move every document onto it here, then remove the old one.\\n            Files themselves aren't re-encrypted, so this is quick.\\n          </p>\\n        </div>\\n        <UIcon\\n          name=\\\"i-lucide-key-round\\\"\\n          class=\\\"mt-1 size-4 shrink-0 text-muted\\\"\\n        />\\n      </div>\\n    </template>\\n    <p\\n      v-if=\\\"error\\\"\\n      class=\\\"text-sm text-error\\\"\\n    >\\n      Couldn't load key status.\\n    </p>\\n    <div\\n      v-else-if=\\\"data\\\"\\n      class=\\\"grid gap-3 text-sm\\\"\\n    >\\n      <UAlert\\n        v-if=\\\"!data.ready\\\"\\n        color=\\\"error\\\"\\n        variant=\\\"subtle\\\"\\n        icon=\\\"i-lucide-triangle-alert\\\"\\n        :description=\\\"`The current master key (version ${data.current}) isn't set on this server, so documents can't be saved or opened.`\\\"\\n      />\\n      <UAlert\\n        v-if=\\\"missing.length\\\"\\n        color=\\\"error\\\"\\n        variant=\\\"subtle\\\"\\n        icon=\\\"i-lucide-triangle-alert\\\"\\n        :description=\\\"`Some documents use key version ${missing.join(', ')}, which this server doesn't have. Add it back to NUXT_DOCUMENTS_RETIRED_KEYS or they can't be opened.`\\\"\\n      />\\n      <p>\\n        Current key version: <span class=\\\"font-medium text-highlighted tabular-nums\\\">{{ data.current }}</span>\\n      </p>\\n      <ul class=\\\"grid gap-1 text-muted\\\">\\n        <li\\n          v-for=\\\"(count, version) in data.counts\\\"\\n          :key=\\\"version\\\"\\n        >\\n          Version {{ version }}: <span class=\\\"font-medium text-highlighted tabular-nums\\\">{{ count.toLocaleString() }}</span> documents\\n        </li>\\n        <li v-if=\\\"!Object.keys(data.counts).length\\\">\\n          No documents saved yet.\\n        </li>\\n      </ul>\\n      <div class=\\\"flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3\\\">\\n        <UButton\\n          color=\\\"primary\\\"\\n          variant=\\\"outline\\\"\\n          icon=\\\"i-lucide-refresh-cw\\\"\\n          :label=\\\"data.stale ? `Move ${data.stale.toLocaleString()} to version ${data.current}` : 'All on the current key'\\\"\\n          :disabled=\\\"!data.stale || !data.ready || missing.length > 0\\\"\\n          :loading=\\\"running\\\"\\n          @click=\\\"rotate\\\"\\n        />\\n      </div>\\n    </div>\\n  </UCard>\\n</template>\\n\",\"path\":\"app/components/admin/DocumentKeys.vue\"}",

## user

is there a way to remove liability in the case of a breach so we arent at risk

## assistant

No. Nothing removes your liability completely. A waiver in your terms won't protect you if the shop didn't take reasonable care; California Civil Code §1668 voids contracts that excuse a business from its own violations of law. What you can do is make a breach much less likely, much less harmful, and much less expensive. This is general information, not legal advice; have a California attorney confirm it for your situation.

**The biggest lever: hold less data**

You can't leak what you don't keep. In order of how much risk each removes:

1. **Details only, no images.** Store document type, expiry date and last 4 digits. That keeps reminders and pre-checks working. A breach would expose almost nothing useful, and full driver license numbers are what trigger California's breach rules.
2. **Delete documents automatically after use.** For example, erase files 30 days after pickup or after expiry. You didn't pick this earlier, but it cuts exposure a lot.
3. **Keep uploads but make them optional**, with a clear statement that originals are still checked in person.

**Encryption helps legally, not just technically**

California's breach-notification law (Civil Code §1798.82) applies to unencrypted personal information. If encrypted data is stolen without the key, notification generally isn't required. That's why the design keeps the key (`NUXT_DOCUMENTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) in Railway, separate from the database and file storage. In practice:
- Never put the key in Supabase, in the code repository, or in shared documents.
- Limit who can see Railway's environment variables.
- Rotate the key if a staff member with access leaves. The new Settings card handles moving documents to the new key.

**"Reasonable security" is the standard you're judged against**

Civil Code §1798.81.5 requires reasonable security for California customers' personal information. What's already built is good evidence of that: encryption, a separate copy of the password needed to open files, two-factor sign-in, access logs, photo location data removed, and cleanup after account deletion. To strengthen it:
- Require two-factor for everyone with access to Supabase, Railway and the dashboard.
- Write a one-page incident response plan: who to call, how to rotate the key, how to notify customers.
- Set a written retention policy and follow it.

**Shift the cost if it happens**

- **Cyber liability insurance.** This is the real tool for transferring breach costs: notification, forensics, legal defense and claims. It's usually inexpensive for a small shop. Insurers will ask about encryption, two-factor and backups, which you can now answer well.
- **Business structure.** An LLC or corporation keeps a claim against the business away from your personal assets, provided it's kept properly separate.
- **Vendor terms.** Accept Supabase's and Railway's data processing agreements (DPAs) and keep copies.
- **Honest privacy policy and upload notice.** It won't waive liability. But clear consent ("optional, used only for pre-checks, deleted after X days") reduces disputes and claims of deceptive practices.

**What I'd recommend**

Switch to details-only (type, expiry, last 4), or keep uploads with automatic deletion after pickup or expiry. Add cyber insurance and an attorney review of the privacy policy either way. This keeps the reminder feature and most of the customer convenience, and drops the riskiest data you'd otherwise hold. It's a small change to what's already built.

Do you want details-only, or keep uploads with automatic deletion? If deletion, after how many days?

## user

so is it possible to use pictures but theyre only purpose is to parse details

## assistant

Yes. The safest version reads the photo **on the customer's phone or computer** and never uploads it. Only the details they confirm get sent to the server, and the photo is thrown away in the browser. You'd store no images at all, so a breach couldn't expose any.

**How it would work**
1. The customer taps "Scan" and takes or picks a photo.
2. The browser reads the details on the device.
3. A form appears, filled in with the type, expiry date and number. The customer fixes anything wrong and saves.
4. The server stores only what you choose, for example type, expiry and last 4 digits. The photo is never sent.

**How well it reads each document**
- **Driver license or state ID: very reliable.** The barcode on the back of US licenses (a standard called AAMVA PDF417) contains the license number, expiry date, name, birth date and address as structured text. Decoding the barcode is much more accurate than reading the printed front. Some phones' browsers, especially iPhone Safari, lack a built-in barcode reader, so we'd include a small open-source one (for example ZXing) so it works everywhere.
- **FSC, CCW and passports: less reliable.** These need text recognition (OCR) on the front of the card, for example with Tesseract.js running in the browser. It usually finds the dates and numbers, but the customer will need to check and correct them more often. It also adds a few MB that download only when someone scans.
- **Proof of residency:** OCR can find the statement date and address, but bills vary widely, so expect more manual correction.

Typing the details by hand always stays available as a fallback.

**Why do it on the device and not on the server or with a cloud OCR service**
Sending the photo to your server, or to a service like Google or AWS, means the full image passes through and is processed by systems you're responsible for. Even if you delete it right away, it's harder to prove it was never kept. If the photo never leaves the device, there's nothing to defend.

**Tradeoffs**
- Staff can't look at the actual document ahead of time. They'd only see the details the customer confirmed. Since originals are checked in person anyway, that's probably fine.
- Scanning doesn't prove the document is genuine. It just saves typing.
- You still decide how much of the parsed data to keep. I'd keep type, expiry and last 4, which is enough for reminders and pre-checks. If you need the full number, it stays encrypted as it is now.

**What changes in the code**
- Add a "Scan" button to the add-document window with on-device barcode and OCR reading.
- Remove file uploads, the encrypted file storage and the "Open file" button.
- Encrypted numbers, reminders, password unlock and two-factor stay as they are.
- Already-uploaded files can be deleted with the existing cleanup job. Locally these are only test data.

Should I build it this way? And for the stored details, do you want only the last 4 digits, or the full number kept encrypted?

1:/**
2: * Helpers for the customer routes in server/api/account. Like requireStaff,
3: * requireCustomer hands back a service-role client that bypasses row-level
4: * security, so every query must be scoped to the returned userId.
5: */
6:import type { H3Event } from 'h3'
7:import { serverSupabaseServiceRole, serverSupabaseUser } from '#supabase/server'
8:
9:export async function requireCustomer(event: H3Event) {
10:  const claims = await serverSupabaseUser(event).catch(() => null)
11:  const userId = claims?.sub
12:  if (!userId) throw createError({ statusCode: 401, statusMessage: 'Sign in required' })
13:  return {
14:    userId,
15:    sessionId: String(claims.session_id ?? ''),
16:    aal: String(claims.aal ?? 'aal1'),
17:    admin: serverSupabaseServiceRole(event),
18:  }
19:}
20:
21:/** True when the user has a verified two-factor (authenticator app) factor. */
22:export async function hasVerifiedFactor(admin: AdminClient, userId: string) {
23:  const { data, error } = await admin.auth.admin.mfa.listFactors({ userId })
24:  failOn(error)
25:  return (data?.factors ?? []).some(factor => factor.status === 'verified')
26:}
27:
28:/**
29: * requireCustomer for document routes: people who turned on two-factor
30: * sign-in must have entered their code in this session (aal2), so a stolen
31: * password alone never reaches their documents.
32: */
33:export async function requireDocumentSession(event: H3Event) {
34:  const session = await requireCustomer(event)
35:  if (session.aal !== 'aal2' && await hasVerifiedFactor(session.admin, session.userId)) {
36:    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Enter your two-factor code to continue.', data: { code: 'mfa_required' } })
37:  }
38:  return session
39:}
40:
41:/** Responses carrying document data: never cached, never sniffed, never framed elsewhere. */
42:export function privateResponse(event: H3Event) {
43:  setResponseHeaders(event, {
44:    'Cache-Control': 'no-store, private',
45:    'Pragma': 'no-cache',
46:    'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff',
47:    'Referrer-Policy': 'no-referrer',
48:  })
49:}
50:
51:export type DocumentAccessAction = 'view_number' | 'view_file' | 'upload' | 'delete' | 'unlock' | 'unlock_failed' | 'rewrap'
52:/** Log entries that aren't about one document (unlocking) use the nil uuid. */
53:export const noDocument = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'
54:
55:export async function logDocumentAccess(
56:  admin: AdminClient,
57:  entry: { documentId: string, ownerId: string, actorId: string, action: DocumentAccessAction },
58:) {
59:  const { error } = await admin.from('customer_document_access').insert({
60:    document_id: entry.documentId,
61:    owner_id: entry.ownerId,
62:    actor_id: entry.actorId,
63:    action: entry.action,
64:  })
65:  failOn(error)
66:}
67:
68:/** The caller's own document, or 404 (also for other people's ids, so ids can't be probed). */
69:export async function ownDocument(admin: AdminClient, userId: string, id: string) {
70:  if (!/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i.test(id)) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Document not found' })
71:  const { data, error } = await admin.from('customer_documents').select('*').eq('id', id).eq('user_id', userId).maybeSingle()
72:  failOn(error)
73:  if (!data) throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: 'Document not found' })
74:  return data
75:}
76:
77:export const documentBucket = 'customer-documents'
78:
79:/**
80: * Erases encrypted files whose document rows are gone (queued by the
81: * customer_documents delete trigger, including whole-account deletions).
82: * Runs from the documents:purge task. Returns how many files were removed.
83: */
84:export async function purgeDocumentFiles(admin: AdminClient, limit = 500) {
85:  const { data, error } = await admin.from('customer_document_purge').select('file_path').order('queued_at').limit(limit)
86:  failOn(error)
87:  const paths = (data ?? []).map(row => row.file_path)
88:  if (!paths.length) return 0
89:  // Removing a file that's already gone isn't an error, so the queue always drains.
90:  failOn((await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).remove(paths)).error)
91:  failOn((await admin.from('customer_document_purge').delete().in('file_path', paths)).error)
92:  return paths.length
93:}
94:
95:/* ---- Password unlock ------------------------------------------------------
96: * Viewing a document number or file needs the account password re-entered
97: * within the last UNLOCK_MINUTES, so an unattended signed-in browser or a
98: * stolen session cookie isn't enough. Unlocking sets an HttpOnly cookie
99: * signed with a key derived from the document master key, tied to the user
100: * and to this sign-in session, and sent only to the document routes.
101: */
102:export const UNLOCK_MINUTES = 10
103:export const UNLOCK_MAX_FAILURES = 5
104:const UNLOCK_COOKIE = 'aa-doc-unlock'
105:const UNLOCK_PATH = '/api/account/documents'
106:
107:const base64url = (bytes: ArrayBuffer) => toBase64(new Uint8Array(bytes)).replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '')
108:
109:export async function issueUnlock(event: H3Event, userId: string, sessionId: string) {
110:  const expires = Date.now() + UNLOCK_MINUTES * 60_000
111:  const payload = `${userId}.${sessionId}.${expires}`
112:  const signature = base64url(await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', await unlockSigningKey(event), new TextEncoder().encode(payload)))
113:  setCookie(event, UNLOCK_COOKIE, `${payload}.${signature}`, {
114:    httpOnly: true,
115:    secure: !import.meta.dev,
116:    sameSite: 'strict',
117:    path: UNLOCK_PATH,
118:    maxAge: UNLOCK_MINUTES * 60,
119:  })
120:  return new Date(expires).toISOString()
121:}
122:
123:export function clearUnlock(event: H3Event) {
124:  deleteCookie(event, UNLOCK_COOKIE, { path: UNLOCK_PATH })
125:}
126:
127:/** When this session's unlock expires, or null when it isn't unlocked. */
128:export async function unlockedUntil(event: H3Event, userId: string, sessionId: string) {
129:  const parts = (getCookie(event, UNLOCK_COOKIE) ?? '').split('.')
130:  if (parts.length !== 4) return null
131:  const [user, session, expires, signature] = parts as [string, string, string, string]
132:  if (user !== userId || session !== sessionId || !(Number(expires) > Date.now())) return null
133:  let given: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>
134:  try {
135:    given = fromBase64(signature.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/'))
136:  }
137:  catch {
138:    return null
139:  }
140:  const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', await unlockSigningKey(event), given, new TextEncoder().encode(`${user}.${session}.${expires}`))
141:  return valid ? new Date(Number(expires)).toISOString() : null
142:}
143:
144:export async function requireUnlocked(event: H3Event, userId: string, sessionId: string) {
145:  if (!await unlockedUntil(event, userId, sessionId)) {
146:    throw createError({ statusCode: 403, statusMessage: 'Confirm your password to view documents.', data: { code: 'unlock_required' } })
147:  }
148:}


[server/api/account/documents/index.post.ts#E1B4]
[Source raw SHA256:e1b455574ca5c7a37d3370c83ae26bc19e23bc949d30fddaf68a9e582c2438c2]
1:/*
2: * Save a document (multipart form: the fields below plus an optional `file`).
3: * The number and file are encrypted here, before they reach the database or
4: * storage; see server/utils/documentVault.ts.
5: */
6:import * as z from 'zod'
7:
8:const fields = z.object({
9:  kind: z.enum(documentKindValues),
10:  docType: z.string().trim().min(1, 'Choose the document type').max(40),
11:  issuedBy: z.string().trim().max(80).default(''),
12:  expiresOn: z.union([z.literal(''), z.iso.date('Enter a valid expiration date')]).default(''),
13:  number: z.string().trim().max(40).regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9 -]*$/, 'Letters, numbers, spaces and dashes only').default(''),
14:})
15:
16:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
17:  const { userId, admin } = await requireDocumentSession(event)
18:  privateResponse(event)
19:
20:  const parts = await readMultipartFormData(event)
21:  const parsed = fields.safeParse(Object.fromEntries((parts ?? []).filter(p => !p.filename && p.name).map(p => [p.name!, p.data.toString('utf8')])))
22:  if (!parsed.success) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: z.prettifyError(parsed.error) })
23:  const input = parsed.data
24:  if (!(documentKinds[input.kind].types as readonly string[]).includes(input.docType)) {
25:    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Choose a document type from the list' })
26:  }
27:
28:  const upload = parts?.find(p => p.name === 'file' && p.filename && p.data.length)
29:  if (!upload && !input.number) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Add the document number, a file, or both.' })
30:  if (upload && upload.data.length > maxDocumentBytes) throw createError({ statusCode: 413, statusMessage: 'Files can be up to 10 MB.' })
31:  const fileType = upload ? sniffDocumentType(upload.data) : null
32:  if (upload && !fileType) throw createError({ statusCode: 415, statusMessage: 'Upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo, or a PDF.' })
33:
34:  const { count, error: countError } = await admin.from('customer_documents').select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true }).eq('user_id', userId)
35:  failOn(countError)
36:  if ((count ?? 0) >= maxDocumentsPerCustomer) {
37:    throw createError({ statusCode: 409, statusMessage: `You can keep up to ${maxDocumentsPerCustomer} documents. Delete an old one first.` })
38:  }
39:
40:  // Photos lose their hidden metadata (GPS location, device, thumbnails) before encryption.
41:  let fileBytes: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> | null = null
42:  if (upload && fileType) {
43:    try {
44:      fileBytes = fileType === 'application/pdf' ? new Uint8Array(upload.data) : stripImageMetadata(upload.data, fileType)
45:    }
46:    catch (err) {
47:      if (err instanceof ImageMetadataError) throw createError({ statusCode: 415, statusMessage: err.message })
48:      throw err
49:    }
50:  }
51:
52:  const id = crypto.randomUUID()
53:  const { key, wrapped, version } = await newDocumentKey(event, userId, id)
54:  const path = `${userId}/${id}`
55:  if (fileBytes && fileType) {
56:    const sealed = await encryptFile(key, userId, id, fileType, fileBytes)
57:    const { error } = await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).upload(path, sealed, { contentType: 'application/octet-stream', upsert: false })
58:    failOn(error)
59:  }
60:
61:  const { error } = await admin.from('customer_documents').insert({
62:    id,
63:    user_id: userId,
64:    kind: input.kind,
65:    doc_type: input.docType,
66:    issued_by: input.issuedBy,
67:    expires_on: input.expiresOn || null,
68:    number_ciphertext: input.number ? await encryptNumber(key, userId, id, input.number) : null,
69:    number_last4: input.number.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '').slice(-4),
70:    wrapped_key: wrapped,
71:    key_version: version,
72:    file_path: fileBytes ? path : null,
73:    file_type: fileType,
74:    file_size: fileBytes ? fileBytes.length : null,
75:  })
76:  if (error) {
77:    if (upload) await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).remove([path])
78:    failOn(error)
79:  }
80:  await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: id, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'upload' })
81:  return { id }
82:})

1:/*
2: * Permanently delete one of the caller's documents (needs a recent password
3: * confirmation): the encrypted file first, then its row and key. Deleting the
4: * row queues the file for purging too; since it's already gone, that entry is
5: * cleared here.
6: */
7:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
8:  const { userId, sessionId, admin } = await requireDocumentSession(event)
9:  privateResponse(event)
10:  await requireUnlocked(event, userId, sessionId)
11:  const doc = await ownDocument(admin, userId, getRouterParam(event, 'id') ?? '')
12:  if (doc.file_path) failOn((await admin.storage.from(documentBucket).remove([doc.file_path])).error)
13:  failOn((await admin.from('customer_documents').delete().eq('id', doc.id).eq('user_id', userId)).error)
14:  if (doc.file_path) failOn((await admin.from('customer_document_purge').delete().eq('file_path', doc.file_path)).error)
15:  await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: doc.id, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'delete' })
16:  return { ok: true }
17:})


[server/api/account/index.delete.ts#F7B7]
[Source raw SHA256:f7b77537f15d3826d4be34c958514a4edeb63136f5a8e7028684ce49de0e65be]
1:/*
2: * Permanently delete the caller's account. Needs the account password (and
3: * the two-factor code this session, when two-factor is on), with the same
4: * wrong-password lockout as unlocking documents.
5: *
6: * Deleting the auth user cascades to the profile, saved documents (their
7: * encrypted files are queued and erased by the documents:purge task) and
8: * bookmarks. Orders stay as the shop's sales records, unlinked from the
9: * account (customer_id is set null). Staff must be removed from the team in
10: * the dashboard first, so a dashboard can't lose its last owner this way.
11: */
12:import * as z from 'zod'
13:
14:const body = z.object({ password: z.string().min(1).max(200) })
15:const WINDOW_MINUTES = 15
16:
17:export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
18:  const { userId, admin } = await requireDocumentSession(event)
19:  privateResponse(event)
20:  const parsed = body.safeParse(await readBody(event).catch(() => null))
21:  if (!parsed.success) throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: 'Enter your password' })
22:
23:  const { data: staff, error: staffError } = await admin.from('staff_members').select('user_id').eq('user_id', userId).maybeSingle()
24:  failOn(staffError)
25:  if (staff) throw createError({ statusCode: 409, statusMessage: 'Staff accounts are removed from the dashboard’s Management page. Ask an owner.' })
26:
27:  const since = new Date(Date.now() - WINDOW_MINUTES * 60_000).toISOString()
28:  const { count, error: countError } = await admin
29:    .from('customer_document_access')
30:    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
31:    .eq('owner_id', userId)
32:    .eq('action', 'unlock_failed')
33:    .gte('at', since)
34:  failOn(countError)
35:  if ((count ?? 0) >= UNLOCK_MAX_FAILURES) {
36:    throw createError({ statusCode: 429, statusMessage: `Too many wrong passwords. Try again in ${WINDOW_MINUTES} minutes.` })
37:  }
38:
39:  const { data: ok, error } = await admin.rpc('verify_user_password', { p_user: userId, p_password: parsed.data.password })
40:  failOn(error)
41:  if (!ok) {
42:    await logDocumentAccess(admin, { documentId: noDocument, ownerId: userId, actorId: userId, action: 'unlock_failed' })
43:    throw createError({ statusCode: 401, statusMessage: 'That password isn\'t right.' })
44:  }
45:
46:  failOn((await admin.auth.admin.deleteUser(userId)).error)
47:  clearUnlock(event)
48:  return { ok: true }
49:})


[supabase/migrations/20261102000000_document_security.sql#3FF0]
[Source raw SHA256:3ff0eb60fda19ddf25a3c877a7df2eca314d6a9a981904c0757d9e245e3fed63]
1:/* ---- Document security and reminders ------------------------------------- */
2:-- Follows 20261031000000_customer_profiles_documents.sql.
3:
4:-- Expiry reminders are shown in the site 30 and 7 days before a document
5:-- expires, and once it has expired. This holds the last reminder the customer
6:-- dismissed (30, 7, or 0 for "expired"), so each one is shown once until the
7:-- next stage arrives. Changing the expiry date resets it.
8:alter table public.customer_documents
9:  add column reminder_dismissed smallint check (reminder_dismissed in (30, 7, 0));
10:
11:-- HEIC can't have its location data removed without re-encoding, so uploads
12:-- are JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF (iPhones convert HEIC photos to JPEG for these).
13:alter table public.customer_documents drop constraint customer_documents_file_type_check;
14:alter table public.customer_documents
15:  add constraint customer_documents_file_type_check
16:  check (file_type in ('image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf'));
17:
18:-- New access-log entries: unlocking documents with a password (and failed
19:-- tries, which also drive the lockout), and re-wrapping a key after the
20:-- master key is rotated.
21:alter table public.customer_document_access drop constraint customer_document_access_action_check;
22:alter table public.customer_document_access
23:  add constraint customer_document_access_action_check
24:  check (action in ('view_number', 'view_file', 'upload', 'delete', 'unlock', 'unlock_failed', 'rewrap'));
25:-- Unlock entries aren't about one document; they use the nil uuid.
26:create index customer_document_access_failed_idx on public.customer_document_access (owner_id, at)
27:  where action = 'unlock_failed';
28:
29:-- Encrypted files whose rows are gone, waiting for the server to erase them
30:-- from storage (SQL can't remove a storage object's bytes). Rows disappear
31:-- when a customer deletes a document or when their whole account is deleted
32:-- (the cascade fires this trigger too). The row held the only copy of the
33:-- file's wrapped key, so a queued file is already unreadable; this removes
34:-- the ciphertext as well. Drained by the documents:purge server task.
35:create table public.customer_document_purge (
36:  file_path text primary key,
37:  queued_at timestamptz not null default now()
38:);
39:alter table public.customer_document_purge enable row level security;
40:revoke all on public.customer_document_purge from anon, authenticated;
41:
42:create function public.queue_document_purge()
43:returns trigger
44:language plpgsql
45:security definer
46:set search_path = ''
47:as $$
48:begin
49:  if old.file_path is not null then
50:    insert into public.customer_document_purge (file_path) values (old.file_path) on conflict do nothing;
51:  end if;
52:  return old;
53:end
54:$$;
55:revoke execute on function public.queue_document_purge() from public, anon, authenticated;
56:
57:create trigger customer_documents_queue_purge after delete on public.customer_documents
58:  for each row execute function public.queue_document_purge();
59:
60:-- A new expiry date starts the reminders over.
61:create function public.reset_document_reminder()
62:returns trigger
63:language plpgsql
64:set search_path = ''
65:as $$
66:begin
67:  if new.expires_on is distinct from old.expires_on then
68:    new.reminder_dismissed := null;
69:  end if;
70:  return new;
71:end
72:$$;
73:
74:create trigger customer_documents_reset_reminder before update on public.customer_documents
75:  for each row execute function public.reset_document_reminder();
76:
77:-- Confirms a customer's current password before their documents are shown
78:-- (server/api/account/documents/unlock.post.ts). Checks the stored bcrypt
79:-- hash directly, so it doesn't create a new sign-in session. Server only.
80:create function public.verify_user_password(p_user uuid, p_password text)
81:returns boolean
82:language sql
83:stable
84:security definer
85:set search_path = ''
86:as $$
87:  select exists (
88:    select 1 from auth.users
89:    where id = p_user
90:      and encrypted_password is not null and encrypted_password <> ''
91:      and encrypted_password = extensions.crypt(p_password, encrypted_password)
92:  )
93:$$;
94:revoke execute on function public.verify_user_password(uuid, text) from public, anon, authenticated;
95:grant execute on function public.verify_user_password(uuid, text) to service_role;

1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * The customer's saved ID, residency, CCW and FSC documents. Everything goes
4: * through server/api/account/documents, which encrypts numbers and files
5: * before storing them; this page only ever holds the last 4 digits until the
6: * customer asks to reveal a number. For pre-checking before pickup only.
7: *
8: * Security steps the server enforces, handled here:
9: * - mfa_required: two-factor is on but this sign-in hasn't entered a code.
10: * - unlock_required: numbers, files and deleting need the password again
11: *   (unlock lasts a few minutes, see UNLOCK_MINUTES on the server).
12: * Expiry reminders (30 and 7 days before, and once expired) show at the top.
13: */
14:import type { CustomerDocument, DocumentKind, DocumentsResponse } from '#shared/utils/customer'

16:const toast = useToast()

28:function errorCode(err: unknown) {

38:const today = shopToday()
39:function expiry(doc: CustomerDocument) {

42:  const days = daysUntil(doc.expiresOn, today)
43:  if (days < 0) return { label: `Expired ${label}`, color: 'error' as const }
44:  if (days <= 30) return { label: `Expires ${label}`, color: 'warning' as const }
45:  return { label: `Expires ${label}`, color: 'neutral' as const }
46:}

48:/* ---- Reminders ------------------------------------------------------------ */
49:const dismissing = ref<string | null>(null)

54:    await reminders.refresh()

64:/* ---- Unlocking (password again) ------------------------------------------- */
65:const unlockOpen = ref(false)

71:const isUnlocked = () => !!data.value.unlockedUntil && Date.parse(data.value.unlockedUntil) > Date.now()
72:
73:/** Runs `action` now when unlocked, otherwise after the password is confirmed. */
74:function whenUnlocked(action: () => unknown) {
75:  if (isUnlocked()) return action()
76:  afterUnlock = action
77:  password.value = ''
78:  unlockError.value = ''
79:  unlockOpen.value = true

81:
82:async function unlock() {

84:  unlockError.value = ''
85:  try {

87:    data.value = { ...data.value, unlockedUntil }
88:    password.value = ''
89:    unlockOpen.value = false
90:    const action = afterUnlock

94:  catch (err) {

97:  finally {

104:  revealed.clear()

108:/** Server says the unlock ran out: ask again and retry. */
109:function handleLocked(err: unknown, retry: () => unknown) {

111:  data.value = { ...data.value, unlockedUntil: null }
112:  whenUnlocked(retry)
113:  return true
114:}

120:/* ---- Revealing a number -------------------------------------------------- */
121:// Shown for 30 seconds, then hidden again.
122:const revealed = reactive(new Map<string, string>())
123:function reveal(doc: CustomerDocument) {

125:    revealed.delete(doc.id)
126:    return
127:  }
128:  whenUnlocked(async () => {

131:      revealed.set(doc.id, number)
132:      setTimeout(() => revealed.delete(doc.id), 30_000)
133:    }
134:    catch (err) {
135:      if (!handleLocked(err, () => reveal(doc))) toast.add({ title: 'Couldn\'t show the number', description: errorMessage(err), color: 'error' })
136:    }
137:  })
138:}

140:function openFile(doc: CustomerDocument) {

142:}

150:

158:const addOpen = computed({

165:async function save() {
166:  const kind = adding.value
167:  if (!kind) return
168:  if (!form.docType) return toast.add({ title: 'Choose the document type', color: 'warning' })
169:  if (!form.number.trim() && !file.value) return toast.add({ title: 'Add the document number, a photo, or both', color: 'warning' })
170:  if (file.value && file.value.size > maxDocumentBytes) return toast.add({ title: 'Files can be up to 10 MB', color: 'warning' })
171:
172:  const body = new FormData()
173:  body.set('kind', kind)
174:  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(form)) body.set(k, v)
175:  if (file.value) body.set('file', file.value)
176:  saving.value = true
177:  try {
178:    await $fetch('/api/account/documents', { method: 'POST', body })
179:    adding.value = null
180:    toast.add({ title: `${documentKinds[kind].label} saved`, description: 'Stored encrypted.', color: 'success', icon: 'i-lucide-lock' })
181:    await reloadAll()
182:  }
183:  catch (err) {
184:    toast.add({ title: 'Couldn\'t save the document', description: errorMessage(err), color: 'error' })
185:  }
186:  finally {
187:    saving.value = false
188:  }
189:}
190:

192:const deleting = ref<CustomerDocument | null>(null)
193:const deleteOpen = computed({

198:})
199:const removing = ref(false)

213:    }

216:    }

218:}

138:  if (!doc) return
139:  removing.value = true

142:    deleting.value = null

144:    await reloadAll()

146:  catch (err) {

150:    removing.value = false
151:  }
152:}

157:}

## assistant

The site no longer stores document photos or full numbers. It keeps only what reminders and paperwork prep need. Customers can still use a photo to fill in the form: the barcode on the back of a license or state ID is read in their own browser, and the photo is never sent to your server. I tested this in a real browser against your port 3000 dev server, and all checks passed.

**Kept (useful, low risk)**
- Expiry reminders at 30 days, 7 days and once expired, with the header dot and menu count.
- For each document: type, issuer, expiration date and the **last 4 characters** of the number. That's enough to tell documents apart and to check paperwork before pickup.
- **Scan:** the customer photographs the barcode on the back of a driver license or state ID. The form fills itself with type, state, expiry and last 4. Name, birth date and address are thrown away on the device. The barcode reader is served from your own site, not a third-party service.
- Optional two-factor sign-in, and the password check with lockout when deleting an account.

**Dropped (liability with no real benefit now)**
- Document photos and PDFs. Their storage bucket is deleted locally, along with the hourly cleanup job that erased deleted accounts' files.
- Full document numbers, encrypted or not.
- The document master key, key rotation and the owner's key card in Settings. With nothing sensitive stored, there's no key to lose or leak.
- The password unlock before viewing documents, since there's nothing sensitive left to reveal.

If the database leaked, it would expose the document type, expiry date and last 4 characters, but no photo or full number. The full ID number is what California's breach-notification law focuses on. Keep cyber insurance and have an attorney review the policy anyway.

**Test results**
- **Scanning:** a real license barcode image filled in "Driver license · CA", the correct expiry and last 4 "4321". Nothing was uploaded while scanning; the browser only downloaded the barcode reader. The saved request held just the details, about 100 bytes.
- **Database:** the table now holds only type, issuer, expiry, last 4 and reminder state. Files and full numbers sent by the old upload style are refused.
- **Reminders:** they appeared correctly (20 days and 5 days). Deleting a document worked, and deleting the account was refused with a wrong password and worked with the right one.
- **Other checks:** an unreadable photo shows a friendly message. The old file, number and unlock addresses are gone, and nothing overflows on a phone-width screen. There were no console errors.
- **Code checks:** 12 checks on reading the barcode pass, including decoding real barcode images. Lint passes, and the type check shows only the existing errors in `marketing.ts`.
- The run caught one real bug, a missing `}` in my styles, which I fixed. Test accounts are cleaned up.

**What you need to do**
- **Live site:** run the new migration `supabase/migrations/20261106000000_documents_details_only.sql`, and delete the empty `customer-documents` bucket in Supabase Storage (SQL isn't allowed to remove it).
- **Leftover key:** you can remove `NUXT_DOCUMENTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from `.env`, and don't add it to Railway.
- **Privacy policy:** updated to match. It now says the site saves no photos or full numbers and that scanning happens on the customer's device.

**Limits**
- Scanning only works for driver licenses and state IDs, which have the barcode. FSC, CCW and residency details are typed by hand. Reading the printed card front was unreliable and would have added a large download, so I left it out.
- I haven't tested scanning with a real phone camera on an actual card; the tests used generated barcode images.
- Two-factor sign-in is still untested, because your local Supabase needs a restart before setup works.
- Two-factor is still optional for staff. Since the site holds no document images or numbers for staff to look at anymore, requiring it matters less.

1:<script setup lang="ts">
2:/*
3: * Asks for the 6-digit code from the customer's authenticator app and raises
4: * this sign-in session to two-factor level (aal2). Used after signing in and
5: * when the documents section needs it.
6: */
7:const emit = defineEmits<{ verified: [] }>()
8:const supabase = useSupabaseClient()
9:const code = ref('')
10:const loading = ref(false)
11:const error = ref('')
12:
13:async function verify() {
14:  loading.value = true
15:  error.value = ''
16:  try {
17:    const { data, error: listError } = await supabase.auth.mfa.listFactors()
18:    if (listError) throw listError
19:    const factor = data.totp[0]
20:    if (!factor) throw new Error('No authenticator app is set up on this account.')
21:    const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challengeAndVerify({ factorId: factor.id, code: code.value.trim() })
22:    if (verifyError) throw verifyError
23:    code.value = ''
24:    emit('verified')
25:  }
26:  catch (err) {
27:    error.value = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'That code didn\'t work. Try the newest one.'
28:  }
29:  finally {
30:    loading.value = false
31:  }
32:}
33:</script>
34:
35:<template>
36:  <form
37:    class="grid gap-4"
38:    @submit.prevent="verify"
39:  >
40:    <UFormField
41:      label="Code from your authenticator app"
42:      :error="error || undefined"
43:    >
44:      <UInput
45:        v-model="code"
46:        inputmode="numeric"
47:        autocomplete="one-time-code"
48:        maxlength="6"
49:        size="xl"
50:        class="w-full font-mono tracking-widest"
51:        autofocus
52:      />
53:    </UFormField>
54:    <UButton
55:      type="submit"
56:      size="xl"
57:      block
58:      label="Verify"
59:      :loading="loading"
60:      :disabled="!/^\d{6}$/.test(code.trim())"
61:    />
62:  </form>
63:</template>
